phrases.he: הָיוּ בוֹ חָפִין וּנְקָבִין, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If it retained the teeth and the gaps it remains unclean.

phrases.he: נִטְּלוּ חָפִין, טָמֵא מִפְּנֵי נְקָבִין.
phrases.en: If the teeth were missing it is still unclean on account of the gaps; if the gaps were blocked up it is unclean on account of the teeth.

phrases.he: נִסְתַּתְּמוּ נְקָבִין, טָמֵא מִפְּנֵי חָפִין.
phrases.en: If the teeth were missing and the gaps were blocked up, or if they were merged into one another, it is clean.

phrases.he: נִטְּלוּ חָפִין וְנִסְתַּתְּמוּ נְקָבִין, אוֹ שֶׁפָּרְצוּ זֶה לְתוֹךְ זֶה, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If in a mustard-strainer three holes in its bottom were merged into one another the strainer is clean.

phrases.he: מְסַנֶּנֶת שֶׁל חַרְדָּל שֶׁנִּפְרְצוּ בָהּ שְׁלֹשָׁה נְקָבִים מִלְּמַטָּן זֶה לְתוֹךְ זֶה, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: A metal mill-funnel is unclean.

phrases.he: וְהָאֲפַרְכֵּס שֶׁל מַתָּכוֹת, טְמֵאָה
כְּלֵי עֵץ, כְּלֵי עוֹר, כְּלֵי עֶצֶם, כְּלֵי זְכוּכִית, פְּשׁוּטֵיהֶן טְהוֹרִין, וּמְקַבְּלֵיהֶן טְמֵאִים. נִשְׁבְּרוּ, טָהָרוּ.
phrases.en: Vessels of wood, leather, bone or glass: those that are flat are clean and those that form a receptacle are susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: חָזַר וְעָשָׂה מֵהֶן כֵּלִים, מְקַבְּלִין טֻמְאָה מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא.
phrases.en: If they are broken they become clean again. If one remade them into vessels they are susceptible to impurity henceforth.

phrases.he: הַשִּׁדָּה, וְהַתֵּבָה, וְהַמִּגְדָּל, כַּוֶּרֶת הַקַּשׁ, וְכַוֶּרֶת הַקָּנִים, וּבוֹר סְפִינָה אֲלֶכְּסַנְדְּרִית, שֶׁיֶּשׁ לָהֶם שׁוּלַיִם, וְהֵן מַחֲזִיקִין אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה בְלַח, שֶׁהֵם כּוֹרַיִם בְּיָבֵשׁ, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: A chest, a box, a cupboard, a straw basket, a reed basket, or the tank of an Alexandrian ship, that have flat bottoms and can hold a minimum of forty se'ah in liquid measure which represent two kor in dry measure, are clean.

phrases.he: וּשְׁאָר כָּל הַכֵּלִים, בֵּין מְקַבְּלִין, בֵּין אֵינָם מְקַבְּלִין, טְמֵאִין, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: All other vessels whether they can contain the minimum or cannot contain it, are susceptible to impurity, the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, דַּרְדּוּר עֲגָלָה, וְקֻסְטוֹת הַמְּלָכִים, וַעֲרֵבַת הָעַבְּדָנִין, וּבוֹר סְפִינָה קְטַנָּה, וְהָאָרוֹן, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמְּקַבְּלִין, טְמֵאִין, שֶׁאֵינָן עֲשׂוּיִן לִטַּלְטֵל אֶלָּא בְמַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכָן.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: the tub of a wagon, the food chests of kings, the tanners trough, the tank of a small ship, and an ark, even though they are able to contain the minimum, are susceptible to impurity, since they are intended to be moved about with their contents.

phrases.he: וּשְׁאָר כָּל הַכֵּלִים, הַמְּקַבְּלִים, טְהוֹרִין, וְשֶׁאֵינָן מְקַבְּלִין, טְמֵאִין.
phrases.en: As to all other vessels, those that can contain the minimum are clean and those that cannot contain it are susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: אֵין בֵּין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אֶלָּא עֲרֵבַת בַּעַל הַבָּיִת
phrases.en: There is no difference between Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Judah except a baking trough which belongs to a householder.

phrases.he: אֲרוּבוֹת שֶׁל נַחְתּוֹמִים, טְמֵאוֹת.
phrases.en: Bakers’ baking-boards are susceptible to impurity, but those used by householders are clean.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל בַּעֲלֵי בָתִּים, טְהוֹרוֹת.
phrases.en: But if he dyed them red or saffron they are susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: סֵרְקָן אוֹ כִרְכְּמָן, טְמֵאוֹת.
phrases.en: If a bakers’ shelf was fixed to a wall: Rabbi Eliezer rules that it is clean And the sages rule that it is susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: דַּף שֶׁל נַחְתּוֹמִין שֶׁקְּבָעוֹ בַכֹּתֶל, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מְטַהֵר, וַחֲכָמִים מְטַמְּאִים.
phrases.en: The bakers' frame is susceptible to impurity but one used by householders is clean.

phrases.he: סְרוֹד שֶׁל נַחְתּוֹמִין, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If he made a rim on its four sides it is susceptible to impurity, but if one side was open it is clean.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל בַּעֲלֵי בָתִּים, טָהוֹר.
גִּפְּפוֹ מֵאַרְבַּע רוּחוֹתָיו, טָמֵא.
נִפְרַץ מֵרוּחַ אַחַת, טָהוֹר.
רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, אִם הִתְקִינוֹ לִהְיוֹת קוֹרֵץ עָלָיו, טָמֵא. וְכֵן הַמַּעֲרוֹךְ, טָמֵא:
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: if he fixed it so that one can cut the dough upon it, it is susceptible to impurity. Similarly, a rolling-pin is susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: יַם נָפָה שֶׁל סִלָּתִין, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: The container of the flour-dealers’ sifter is susceptible to impurity, but the one of a householder is clean.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל בַּעֲלֵי בָתִּים, טָהוֹר.
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף שֶׁל גּוֹדֶלֶת טָמֵא מוֹשָׁב, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַבָּנוֹת יוֹשְׁבוֹת בְּתוֹכוֹ וְגוֹדְלוֹת:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: also one that is used by a hairdresser is susceptible to impurity as a seat, since girls sit in it when their hair is dressed.

phrases.he: כָּל הַתְּלוֹיִים, טְמֵאִין, חוּץ מִתְּלוֹי נָפָה וּכְבָרָה שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: All hangers are susceptible to impurity, except for those of a sifter and a sieve that are used by householders, the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, כֻּלָּן טְהוֹרִין, חוּץ מִתְּלוֹי נָפָה שֶׁל סִלָּתִין, וּתְלוֹי כִּבְרַת גְּרָנוֹת, וּתְלוֹי מַגַּל יָד, וּתְלוֹי מַקֵּל הַבַּלָּשִׁין, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן מְסַיְּעִין בִּשְׁעַת הַמְּלָאכָה.
phrases.en: But the sages say: all hangers are clean, excepting those of a sifter of flour-dealers, of a sieve used in threshing-floors, of a hand-sickle and of a detective's staff, since they aid when the instrument is in use.

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, הֶעָשׂוּי לְסַיֵּעַ בִּשְׁעַת מְלָאכָה, טָמֵא. הֶעָשׂוּי לִתְלוֹי, טָהוֹר
phrases.en: This is the general rule: [a hanger] that is intended to aid when the instrument is in use is susceptible to impurity and one intended to serve only as a hanger is clean.

phrases.he: רַחַת שֶׁל גָּרוֹסוֹת, טְמֵאָה. שֶׁל אוֹצָרוֹת, טְהוֹרָה. שֶׁל גִּתּוֹת, טְמֵאָה. שֶׁל גְּרָנוֹת, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: The grist-dealers’ shovel is susceptible to impurity but the one used in grain stores is clean. The one used in wine- presses is susceptible to impurity but that used in threshing- floors is clean.

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, הֶעָשׂוּי לְקַבָּלָה, טָמֵא. לְכִנּוּס, טָהוֹר
phrases.en: This is the general rule: [a shovel] that is intended to hold anything is susceptible to impurity but one intended only to heap stuff together is clean.

phrases.he: נִבְלֵי הַשָּׁרָה, טְמֵאִין. וְנִבְלֵי בְנֵי לֵוִי, טְהוֹרִין. כָּל הַמַּשְׁקִין, טְמֵאִין.
phrases.en: Ordinary harps are susceptible to impurity, but the harps of Levites are clean.

phrases.he: וּמַשְׁקֵה בֵית מַטְבְּחַיָּא, טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: All liquids are susceptible to impurity, but the liquids in the Temple slaughtering house are clean.

phrases.he: כָּל הַסְּפָרִים מְטַמְּאִין אֶת הַיָּדַיִם, חוּץ מִסֵּפֶר הָעֲזָרָה. הַמַּרְכּוֹף, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: All scrolls convey impurity to the hands, excepting the scroll of the Temple courtyard. A wooden toy horse is clean.

phrases.he: הַבַּטְנוֹן, וְהַנִּקְטְמוֹן, וְהָאֵרוּס, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ טְמֵאִים.
phrases.en: The belly-lute, the donkey-shaped musical instrument and the erus are susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, הָאֵרוּס טָמֵא מוֹשָׁב, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָאַלָּיִת יוֹשֶׁבֶת עָלָיו. מְצֻדַּת הַחֻלְדָּה, טְמֵאָה. וְשֶׁל הָעַכְבָּרִין, טְהוֹרָה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: the erus is susceptible to sitting impurity since the wailing woman sits on it. A weasel-trap is susceptible to impurity, but a mouse- trap is clean.

phrases.he: כָּל כְּלִי עֵץ שֶׁנֶּחֱלַק לִשְׁנַיִם, טָהוֹר, חוּץ מִשֻּׁלְחָן הַכָּפוּל, וְתַמְחוּי הַמִּזְנוֹן, וְהָאֱפִיפוֹרִין שֶׁל בַּעֲלֵי הַבָּיִת.
phrases.en: A wooden vessel that was broken into two parts becomes clean, except for a folding table, a dish with compartments for [different kinds of] food, and a householder's footstool.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף הַמָּגֵס, וְקוֹד הַבַּבְלִי כַּיּוֹצֵא בָהֶן.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: a double dish and a Babylonian drinking vessel are subject to the same law.

phrases.he: כְּלֵי עֵץ, מֵאֵימָתַי מְקַבְּלִין טֻמְאָה.
phrases.en: When do wooden vessels begin to be susceptible to impurity? A bed and a cot, after they are sanded with fishskin.

phrases.he: הַמִּטָּה וְהָעֲרִיסָה, מִשֶּׁיְּשׁוּפֵם בְּעוֹר הַדָּג.
phrases.en: If the owner determined not to sand them over they are susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: גָּמַר שֶׁלֹּא לָשׁוּף, טְמֵאָה.
רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, הַמִּטָּה, מִשֶּׁיְּסָרֵג בָּהּ שְׁלֹשָׁה בָתִּים:
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir says: a bed becomes susceptible to impurity as soon as three rows of meshes have been knitted in it.

phrases.he: הַסַּלִּים שֶׁל עֵץ, מִשֶּׁיַּחְסֹם וִיקַנֵּב.
phrases.en: Wooden baskets [become susceptible to impurity] as soon as their rims are rounded off and their rough ends are smoothed off.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל תְּמָרָה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא קִנֵּב מִבִּפְנִים, טָמֵא, שֶׁכֵּן מְקַיְּמִין.
phrases.en: But those that are made of palm-branches [become susceptible to impurity] even though their ends were not smoothed off on the inside, since they are allowed to remain in this condition.

phrases.he: כַּלְכָּלָה, מִשֶּׁיַּחְסֹם וִיקַנֵּב וְיִגְמֹר אֶת הַתְּלוֹיָה.
phrases.en: A basket [of reed-grass becomes susceptible to impurity] as soon as its rim is rounded off, its rough ends are smoothed off, and its hanger is finished.

phrases.he: בֵּית הַלְּגִינִין, וּבֵית הַכּוֹסוֹת, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא קִנֵּב מִבִּפְנִים, טָמֵא, שֶׁכֵּן מְקַיְּמִין
phrases.en: A wicker basket flasks or for cups [is susceptible to impurity] even if the rough ends were not smoothed off on the inside, since these are allowed to remain in this condition.

phrases.he: הַקְּנוֹנִין הַקְּטַנִּים, וְהַקְּלָתוֹת, מִשֶּׁיַּחְסֹם וִיקַנֵּב.
phrases.en: Small reed baskets and baskets [become susceptible to impurity] as soon as their rims are rounded off and their rough ends are smoothed off.

phrases.he: הַקְּנוֹנִים הַגְּדוֹלִים, וְהַסּוּגִין הַגְּדוֹלִים, מִשֶּׁיַּעֲשֶׂה שְׁנֵי דוּרִים לָרֹחַב שֶׁלָּהֶם.
phrases.en: Large reed baskets and large hampers, as soon as two rows have been made round their sides.

phrases.he: יָם נָפָה, וּכְבָרָה, וְכַף שֶׁל מֹאזְנַיִם, מִשֶּׁיַּעֲשֶׂה דוּר אֶחָד לָרֹחַב שֶׁלָּהֶן.
phrases.en: The container of a sifter or a sieve and a cup of the balances, as soon as one circling band has been made round their sides.

phrases.he: הַקֻּפָּה, מִשֶּׁיַּעֲשֶׂה שְׁתֵּי צְפִירוֹת לָרֹחַב שֶׁלָּהּ.
phrases.en: A willow basket, as soon as two twists have been made around its wide sides.

phrases.he: וְהֶעָרָק, מִשֶּׁיַּעֲשֶׂה בוֹ צְפִירָה אֶחָת
phrases.en: And a rush basket, as soon as one twist has been made round it.

phrases.he: כְּלֵי עוֹר, מֵאֵימָתַי מְקַבְּלִין טֻמְאָה.
phrases.en: When do leather vessels become susceptible to impurity?A leather pouch, as soon as its hem has been stitched, its rough ends trimmed and its straps sewn on.

phrases.he: הַתּוּרְמֵל, מִשֶּׁיַּחְסֹם וִיקַנֵּב וְיַעֲשֶׂה קִיחוֹתָיו.
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, מִשֶּׁיַּעֲשֶׂה אֶת אָזְנָיו.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: so soon as its ears have been sewn on.

phrases.he: סְקֹרְטְיָא, מִשֶּׁיַּחְסֹם וִיקַנֵּב וְיַעֲשֶׂה אֶת צִיצָתָהּ.
phrases.en: A leather apron [becomes susceptible to impurity] as soon as its hem has been stitched, its rough end trimmed and its strings sewn on.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, מִשֶּׁיַּעֲשֶׂה אֶת טַבְּעוֹתֶיהָ. קָטָבוֹלְיָא, מִשֶּׁיַּחְסֹם וִיקַנֵּב.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: as soon as its loops have been sewn on. A leather bed cover [becomes susceptible] as soon as its hem has been stitched and its rough ends trimmed.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, מִשֶּׁיַּעֲשֶׂה אֶת קִיחוֹתֶיהָ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: as soon as its straps have been sewn on.

phrases.he: הַכַּר וְהַכֶּסֶת שֶׁל עוֹר, מִשֶּׁיַּחְסֹם וִיקַנֵּב.
phrases.en: A leather cushion or mattress [becomes susceptible] as soon as its hem has been stitched and its rough ends trimmed.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, מִשֶּׁיִּתְפְּרֵם וִישַׁיֵּר בָּהֶם פָּחוֹת מֵחֲמִשָּׁה טְפָחִים:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: as it has been sew up and less than five handbreadths remained open.

phrases.he: פָּטִילְיָה, טְמֵאָה. וַחֲסִינָה, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: A basket [for figs] is susceptible to uncleanness but a basket for wheat is clean.

phrases.he: סִגְנִיּוֹת שֶׁל עָלִין, טְהוֹרוֹת. שֶׁל נְצָרִין, טְמֵאוֹת.
phrases.en: Small baskets made of leaves are clean, but those made of branches are susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: חוֹתָל שֶׁהוּא נוֹתֵן לְתוֹכוֹ וְנוֹטֵל מִתּוֹכוֹ, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: The palm wrapping [in which dates are left] and into which they can be easily put and from which they can easily be taken out is susceptible to uncleanness, but if this cannot be done without tearing it or undoing it, it is clean.

phrases.he: וְאִם אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל עַד שֶׁיִּקְרָעֶנּוּ אוֹ עַד שֶׁיַּתִּירֶנּוּ, טָהוֹר
קְסָיָה שֶׁל זוֹרֵי גְרָנוֹת, שֶׁל הוֹלְכֵי דְרָכִים, שֶׁל עוֹשֵׂי פִשְׁתָּן, טְמֵאָה.
phrases.en: The leather glove of winnowers, travelers, or flax workers is susceptible to uncleanness. But the one for dyers or blacksmiths is clean.

phrases.he: אֲבָל שֶׁל צַבָּעִין וְשֶׁל נַפָּחִין, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: the same law applies to the glove of grist dealers.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אַף שֶׁל גָּרוֹסוֹת כַּיּוֹצֵא בָהֶן.
phrases.en: This is the general rule: that which is made for holding anything is susceptible to uncleanness, but that which only affords protection against perspiration is clean.

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, הֶעָשׂוּי לְקַבָּלָה, טָמֵא. מִפְּנֵי הַזֵּעָה, טָהוֹר
הַמַּלְקוֹט שֶׁל בָּקָר, וְהֶחָסִים שֶׁלּוֹ, וְהַמַּדָּף שֶׁל דְּבוֹרִים, וְהַמְּנָפָה, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: The dung bag of a bull and its muzzle, a bee shelf, and a fan are clean.

phrases.he: כְּסוּי שֶׁל קֻפְסָא, טָמֵא. כְּסוּי קַמְטְרָא, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: The cover of a small box is susceptible to uncleanness; The cover of a clothes chest is clean.

phrases.he: כְּסוּי תֵּבָה, כְּסוּי טֶנִי, וְהַמַּכְבֵּשׁ שֶׁל חָרָשׁ, וְהַכֶּסֶת שֶׁתַּחַת הַתֵּבָה, וְהַקִּמְרוֹן שֶׁלָּהּ, וְאַנְגְּלִין שֶׁל סֵפֶר, בֵּית הַנֶּגֶר, בֵּית הַמַּנְעוּל, וּבֵית הַמְּזוּזָה, וְתִיק נְבָלִין, וְתִיק כִּנּוֹרֶת, וְהָאֵמוּם שֶׁל גּוֹדְלֵי מִצְנָפוֹת, וְהַמַּרְכּוֹף שֶׁל זַמָּר, וּרְבִיעִית שֶׁל אַלָּיִת, וּגְנוֹגְנִית הֶעָנִי, וְסָמוֹכוֹת הַמִּטָּה, וּטְפוּס שֶׁל תְּפִלָּה, וְאֵמוּם שֶׁל עוֹשֵׂה סוּתוֹת, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ טְהוֹרִים. זֶה הַכְּלָל,
phrases.en: The cover of a box, the cover of a basket, a carpenter's vice, a cushion under a box or its arched cover, a reading-desk for a book, a bolt-socket, a lock-socket, a mezuzah case, a lyre case, a violin case, the block of the turban-makers, a wooden musical toy horse, the clappers of a wailing woman, a poor man's parasol, bed posts, a tefillin mould, and the mould of string makers all these are clean.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, כָּל מְשַׁמְּשֵׁי מְשַׁמְּשָׁיו שֶׁל אָדָם בִּשְׁעַת מְלָאכָה וְשֶׁלֹּא בִשְׁעַת מְלָאכָה, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: This is the general rule which Rabbi Yose stated: all objects that serve as a protection to objects that a man uses, both when the latter are in use and when they are not in use, are susceptible to uncleanness; but those that serve them as a protection only when the latter are in use are clean.

phrases.he: וְכֹל שֶׁאֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בִשְׁעַת מְלָאכָה, טָהוֹר

תִּיק הַסַּיִף וְהַסַּכִּין וְהַפִּגְיוֹן, תִּיק מִסְפֶּרֶת וּמִסְפָּרַיִם וְהַתַּעַר, תִּיק מִכְחוֹל, וּבֵית הַכּוֹחַל, תִּיק מַכְתֵּב, וּתְרוּנְתֵּק, תִּיק טַבְלָא וּסְקֹרְטְיָא, בֵּית הַחִצִּים, בֵּית הַפָּגוֹשׁוֹת, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ טְמֵאִים.
phrases.en: The sheath of a sword, a knife or a dagger, the case for scissors, or shears or a razor, the case of make-up and the make-up box, the stylus case, the compass case, the tablet case, the case for a board, a quiver and a javelin case all these are susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: תִּיק סִמְפּוֹנְיָא, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהוּא נוֹתֵן מִלְמַעְלָה, טָמֵא. מִצִּדּוֹ, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: The case for a double flute is susceptible to uncleanness if the instrument is put in from above, but if it is put in from the side it is clean.

phrases.he: תִּיק חֲלִילִין, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מְטַהֵר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא נוֹתְנוֹ מִצִּדּוֹ.
phrases.en: A case for flutes Rabbi Judah says it is clean because these are put in from the side. The covering of a club, a bow or a spear is clean.

phrases.he: חִפּוּי הָאַלָּה, הַקֶּשֶׁת, וְהָרֹמַח, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: This is the general rule: that which serves as a case is susceptible to uncleanness, but that which is merely a covering is clean.

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, הֶעָשׂוּי לְתִיק, טָמֵא. לְחִפּוּי, טָהוֹר
כָּל כְּלֵי בַעֲלֵי בָתִּים, שִׁעוּרָן בְּרִמּוֹנִים.
phrases.en: All [wooden] vessels that belong to householder [become clean if the holes in them are] the size of pomegranates.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, בְּמַה שֶּׁהֵן.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: [the size of the hole depends] on what it is used for.

phrases.he: קֻפּוֹת הַגַּנָּנִים, שִׁעוּרָן בַּאֲגֻדּוֹת שֶׁל יָרָק.
phrases.en: Gardeners’ vegetable baskets [become clean if the holes in them are] the size of bundles of vegetables.

phrases.he: שֶׁל בַּעֲלֵי בָתִּים, בְּתֶבֶן. שֶׁל בַּלָּנִין, בִּגְבָבָה.
phrases.en: Baskets of householders [become clean if the holes in them are] the size of [bundles] of straws. Those of bath-keepers, if bundles of chaff [will drop through].

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, כֻּלָּן בְּרִמּוֹנִים:
phrases.en: Rabbi Joshua says: in all these the size is that of pomegranates.

phrases.he: הַחֵמֶת, שִׁעוּרָהּ בִּפְקָעִיּוֹת שֶׁל שֶׁתִי.
phrases.en: A skin bottle [becomes clean if the holes in it are of] a size through which warp-stoppers [can fall out].

phrases.he: אִם אֵינָהּ מְקַבֶּלֶת שֶׁל שְׁתִי, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמְּקַבֶּלֶת שֶׁל עֵרֶב, טְמֵאָה.
phrases.en: If a warp-stopper cannot be held in, but it can still hold a woof-stopper it remains unclean.

phrases.he: בֵּית קְעָרוֹת שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְקַבֵּל קְעָרוֹת, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמְּקַבֵּל אֶת הַתַּמְחוּיִין, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: A dish holder that cannot hold dishes but can still hold trays remains unclean.

phrases.he: בֵּית הָרְעִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְקַבֵּל מַשְׁקִין, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמְּקַבֵּל אֶת הָרְעִי, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: A chamber- pot that cannot hold liquids but can still hold excrements remains unclean.

phrases.he: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מְטַהֵר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵין מְקַיְּמִין אוֹתוֹ
phrases.en: Rabban Gamaliel rules that it is clean since people do not usually keep one that is in such a condition.

phrases.he: הַסַּלִּין שֶׁל פַּת, שִׁעוּרָן בְּכִכָּרוֹת שֶׁל פָּת.
phrases.en: Bread-baskets [become clean if] the size [of their hole is such] that loaves of bread [would fall through].

phrases.he: אֱפִיפְיָרוֹת שֶׁעָשָׂה לָהֶן קָנִים מִלְּמַטָּן לְמַעְלָה לְחִזּוּק, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: Papyrus frames through into which reeds were inserted from the bottom upwards to strengthen them, are clean.

phrases.he: עָשָׂה לָהּ גַּפַּיִם כָּל שֶׁהֵן, טְמֵאָה.
רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, אִם אֵינָהּ יְכוֹלָה לְהִנָּטֵל בַּגַּפַּיִם, טְהוֹרָה:
phrases.en: If he fixed walls to it, they are susceptible to impurity. Rabbi Shimon says: if it cannot be lifted up by these walls it is clean.

phrases.he: הָרִמּוֹנִים שֶׁאָמְרוּ, שְׁלֹשָׁה, אֲחוּזִין זֶה בָזֶה.
phrases.en: The pomegranates of which they have spoken--three attached to one another.

phrases.he: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, בְּנָפָה וּבִכְבָרָה, כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּטֹּל וִיהַלֵּךְ, וּבְקֻפָּה, כְּדֵי שֶׁיַּפְשִׁיל לַאֲחוֹרָיו.
phrases.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamaliel says: in a sifter or a sieve [the size of the hole must be such that a pomegranate will drop out] when one picks it up and walks about with it. In a basket it must be such [as would allow a pomegranate] to fall through while one hangs it behind him.

phrases.he: וּשְׁאָר כָּל הַכֵּלִים שֶׁאֵינָן יְכוֹלִין לְקַבֵּל רִמּוֹנִים, כְּגוֹן הָרֹבַע, וַחֲצִי הָרֹבַע, הַקְּנוֹנִים הַקְּטַנִּים, שִׁעוּרָן בְּרֻבָּן, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: And all other vessels which cannot hold pomegranates as, for instance, the quarter kav measure and the half quarter kav measure, and small baskets, the size [of their holes must be] such as would extend over the greater part of them, the words of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Shimon says: [the size of their hole must be such that] olives [could fall through].

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, בְּזֵיתִים. נִפְרְצוּ, שִׁעוּרָן בְּזֵיתִים.
phrases.en: If their sides were broken [the size of their hole must be] such as olives would drop through.

phrases.he: נִגְמְמוּ, שִׁעוּרָן בְּמַה שֶּׁהֵן
phrases.en: If they are worn away the size must be such as would allow the objects which are usually kept in them [to drop through].

phrases.he: הָרִמּוֹן שֶׁאָמְרוּ, לֹא קָטָן וְלֹא גָדוֹל אֶלָּא בֵינוֹנִי.
phrases.en: The pomegranate of which they spoke refers to one that is neither small nor big but of moderate size.

phrases.he: וּלְמָה הֻזְכְּרוּ רִמּוֹנֵי בָדָאן, שֶׁיְּהוּ מְקַדְּשִׁין כָּל שֶׁהֵן, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: And why did they mention the pomegranates of Baddan? That whatever their quantity they cause [other pomegranates] to be forbidden, the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אוֹמֵר, לְשַׁעֵר בָּהֶן אֶת הַכֵּלִים.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yohanan ben Nuri said: to use them as a measure for holes in vessels.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, לְכָךְ וּלְכָךְ הֻזְכְּרוּ, לְשַׁעֵר בָּהֶן אֶת הַכֵּלִים, וְיִהְיוּ מְקַדְּשִׁין כָּל שֶׁהֵן.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva said: they were mentioned for both reasons: that they are to be used as a measure for holes in vessels and that whatever their quantity they cause [other pomegranates] to be forbidden.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, לֹא הֻזְכְּרוּ רִמּוֹנֵי בָדָאן וַחֲצִירֵי גֶבַע, אֶלָּא שֶׁיִּהְיוּ מִתְעַשְּׂרִין וַדַּאי בְּכָל מָקוֹם:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose said: the pomegranates of Baddan and the leeks of Geba were mentioned only to indicate that they must be tithed everywhere with certain tithe.

phrases.he: כַּבֵּיצָה שֶׁאָמְרוּ, לֹא גְדוֹלָה וְלֹא קְטַנָּה אֶלָּא בֵינוֹנִית.
phrases.en: The egg of which they spoke it is one that is neither big nor small but of moderate size.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, מֵבִיא גְדוֹלָה שֶׁבַּגְּדוֹלוֹת וּקְטַנָּה שֶׁבַּקְּטַנּוֹת, וְנוֹתֵן לְתוֹךְ הַמַּיִם, וְחוֹלֵק אֶת הַמָּיִם.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: the largest and the smallest must be brought and put in water and the displaced water is then divided.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, וְכִי מִי מוֹדִיעֵנִי אֵיזוֹהִי גְדוֹלָה וְאֵיזוֹהִי קְטַנָּה, אֶלָּא הַכֹּל לְפִי דַעְתּוֹ שֶׁל רוֹאֶה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: but who can tell me which is the largest and which is the smallest? Rather, it all depends on the observer's estimate.

phrases.he: כַּגְּרוֹגֶרֶת שֶׁאָמְרוּ, לֹא גְדוֹלָה וְלֹא קְטַנָּה אֶלָּא בֵינוֹנִית.
phrases.en: The dried fig of which they spoke--- it is one that is neither big nor small but of moderate size.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, הַגְּדוֹלָה שֶׁבְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל הִיא הַבֵּינוֹנִית שֶׁבַּמְּדִינוֹת:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: the biggest in the land of Israel is like one of medium size in other lands.

phrases.he: כַּזַּיִת שֶׁאָמְרוּ, לֹא גָדוֹל וְלֹא קָטָן אֶלָּא בֵינוֹנִי, זֶה אֵגוֹרִי.
phrases.en: The olive of which they spoke it is one that is neither big nor small but of moderate size the egori.

phrases.he: כַּשְּׂעֹרָה שֶׁאָמְרוּ, לֹא גְדוֹלָה וְלֹא קְטַנָּה אֶלָּא בֵינוֹנִית, זוֹ מִדְבָּרִית.
phrases.en: The barleycorn of which they spoke it is one that is neither big nor small but of moderate size the midbarit The lentil of which they spoke it is one that is neither big nor small but of moderate size--the egyptian kind.

phrases.he: כָּעֲדָשָׁה שֶׁאָמְרוּ, לֹא גְדוֹלָה וְלֹא קְטַנָּה אֶלָּא בֵינוֹנִית, זוֹ מִצְרִית.
phrases.en: "Any movable object conveys uncleanness if it is of the thickness of an ox goad" it is one that is neither big nor small but of moderate size.

phrases.he: כָּל הַמִּטַּלְטְלִין מְבִיאִין אֶת הַטֻּמְאָה בָּעֳבִי הַמַּרְדֵּעַ, לֹא גָדוֹל וְלֹא קָטָן אֶלָּא בֵינוֹנִי.
phrases.en: What is meant by "one of moderate size?" One whose circumference is just a handbreadth.

phrases.he: אֵיזֶה הוּא בֵינוֹנִי, כֹּל שֶׁהֶקֵּפוֹ טֶפַח
הָאַמָּה שֶׁאָמְרוּ, בָּאַמָּה הַבֵּינוֹנִית.
phrases.en: The cubit of which they spoke is one of medium size.

phrases.he: וּשְׁתֵּי אַמּוֹת הָיָה בְשׁוּשַׁן הַבִּירָה, אַחַת עַל קֶרֶן מִזְרָחִית צְפוֹנִית וְאַחַת עַל קֶרֶן מִזְרָחִית דְּרוֹמִית.
phrases.en: There were two standard cubits in Shushan Habirah, one in the north-eastern corner and the other in the south-eastern corner.

phrases.he: שֶׁעַל קֶרֶן מִזְרָחִית צְפוֹנִית הָיְתָה יְתֵרָה עַל שֶׁל משֶׁה חֲצִי אֶצְבַּע.
phrases.en: The one in the north-eastern corner exceeded that of Moses by half a fingerbreadth, while the one in the south-eastern corner exceeded the other by half a fingerbreadth, so that the latter exceeded that of Moses by a fingerbreadth.

phrases.he: שֶׁעַל קֶרֶן מִזְרָחִית דְּרוֹמִית הָיְתָה יְתֵרָה עָלֶיהָ חֲצִי אֶצְבַּע, נִמְצֵאת יְתֵרָה עַל שֶׁל משֶׁה אֶצְבָּע.
phrases.en: But why were there a larger and a smaller cubit? Only for this reason: so that craftsmen might take their orders according to the smaller cubit and return their finished work according to the larger cubit, so that they might not be guilty of any possible trespassing of Temple property.

phrases.he: וְלָמָּה אָמְרוּ אַחַת גְּדוֹלָה וְאַחַת קְטַנָּה, אֶלָּא שֶׁהָאֻמָּנִין נוֹטְלִין בַּקְּטַנָּה וּמַחֲזִירִין בַּגְּדוֹלָה, כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יָבֹאוּ לִידֵי מְעִילָה
רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, כָּל הָאַמּוֹת הָיוּ בֵינוֹנִיּוֹת, חוּץ מִמִּזְבַּח הַזָּהָב וְהַקֶּרֶן וְהַסּוֹבֵב וְהַיְסוֹד.
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir says: all cubits were of the moderate length except that for the golden altar, the horns, the surround and the base.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַמַּת הַבִּנְיָן שִׁשָּׁה טְפָחִים, וְשֶׁל כֵּלִים חֲמִשָּׁה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: the cubit used for the building was one of six handbreadths and that for the vessels one of five handbreadths.

phrases.he: וְיֵשׁ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּמִדָּה דַקָּה, מִדּוֹת הַלַּח וְהַיָּבֵשׁ שִׁעוּרָן בָּאִיטַלְקִי, זוֹ מִדְבָּרִית.
phrases.en: Sometimes they stated a smaller measure: Liquid and dry measures were measured with the Italian standard which was the one that was used in the wilderness.

phrases.he: וְיֵשׁ שֶׁאָמְרוּ, הַכֹּל לְפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא אָדָם, הַקּוֹמֵץ אֶת הַמִּנְחָה, וְהַחוֹפֵן אֶת הַקְּטֹרֶת, וְהַשּׁוֹתֶה כִמְלֹא לֻגְמָיו בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, וְכִמְזוֹן שְׁתֵּי סְעֻדּוֹת לָעֵרוּב, מְזוֹנוֹ לְחֹל אֲבָל לֹא לְשַׁבָּת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: Sometimes they stated a measure that varied according to the individual concerned: One who takes the handful of a minhah, One who takes both hands full of incense, One who drinks a cheek full on Yom Kippur, And the two meals for an eruv, The quantity being the food one eats on weekdays and not on Shabbat, the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, לְשַׁבָּת אֲבָל לֹא לְחֹל.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: as on Shabbat and not as on weekdays.

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ מִתְכַּוְּנִין לְהָקֵל.
phrases.en: And both intended to give the more lenient ruling.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, מִשְּׁתֵּי יָדוֹת לְכִכָּר, מִשָּׁלֹשׁ לְקָב.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: two thirds of a loaf, when three [loaves] are made of a kav.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא אוֹמֵר, מִכִּכָּר בְּפֻנְדְּיוֹן, מֵאַרְבַּע סְאִין בְּסָלַע
phrases.en: Rabbi Yohanan ben Beroka says: not less than a loaf that is purchased for a pundium when the price of wheat is four se'ah for a sela’.

phrases.he: וְיֵשׁ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְמִדָּה גַסָּה, מְלֹא תַרְוָד רָקָב, כִּמְלֹא תַרְוָד גָּדוֹל שֶׁל רוֹפְאִים.
phrases.en: And sometimes they stated a large measure:A ladleful of corpse mould refers to the big ladle of physicians; The split bean in the case of skin disease refers to the Cilician kind; One who eats on Yom Kippur a quantity of the bulk of a large date, refers to the size of the date and its pit; In the case of skins of wine and oil [the holes] must be as big as their large stopper; In the case of a light hole that was not made by man's hands the prescribed size of which is that of a large fist, the reference is to the fist of Ben Batiah Rabbi Yose said: and it is as big as a large human head.

phrases.he: וּגְרִיס נְגָעִים, כַּגְּרִיס הַקִּלְקִי.
הָאוֹכֵל בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים כַּכּוֹתֶבֶת הַגַּסָּה, כָּמוֹהָ וּכְגַּרְעִינָתָהּ.
וְנוֹדוֹת יַיִן וָשֶׁמֶן, שִׁעוּרָן כְּפִיקָה גְדוֹלָה שֶׁלָּהֶן.
וּמָאוֹר שֶׁלֹּא נַעֲשָׂה בִידֵי אָדָם, שִׁעוּרוֹ כִמְלֹא אֶגְרוֹף גָּדוֹל, זֶה הוּא אֶגְרוֹפוֹ שֶׁל בֶּן בָּטִיחַ.
אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, יֶשְׁנוֹ כְרֹאשׁ גָּדוֹל שֶׁל אָדָם.
phrases.en: And in the case of one made by human hands the prescribed size is that of the large drill in the Temple chamber which is the size of the Italian pondium or the Neronian sela or like the hole in a yoke.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה בִידֵי אָדָם, שִׁעוּרוֹ כִמְלֹא מַקְדֵּחַ גָּדוֹל שֶׁל לִשְׁכָּה, שֶׁהוּא כְפֻנְדְּיוֹן הָאִיטַלְקִי, וּכְסֶלַע הַנֵּירוֹנִית, וְכִמְלֹא נֶקֶב שֶׁבָּעֹל
כֹּל שֶׁבַּיָּם טָהוֹר, חוּץ מִכֶּלֶב הַמַּיִם, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא בוֹרֵחַ לַיַּבָּשָׁה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
phrases.en: All that live in the sea are clean, except the sea-dog because it seeks refuge on dry land, the words of Rabbi Akiba.

phrases.he: הָעוֹשֶׂה כֵלִים מִן הַגָּדֵל בַּיָּם וְחִבֵּר לָהֶם מִן הַגָּדֵל בָּאָרֶץ, אֲפִלּוּ חוּט, אֲפִלּוּ מְשִׁיחָה, דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא מְקַבֵּל טֻמְאָה, טָמֵא
phrases.en: If one made vessels from what grows in the sea and joined to them anything that grows on land, even if only a thread or a cord, if it is susceptible to uncleanness, they are unclean.

phrases.he: וְיֵשׁ בְּמֶה שֶּׁנִּבְרָא בַיּוֹם הָרִאשׁוֹן טֻמְאָה, בַּשֵּׁנִי אֵין בּוֹ טֻמְאָה, בַּשְּׁלִישִׁי יֶשׁ בּוֹ טֻמְאָה, בָּרְבִיעִי וּבַחֲמִישִׁי אֵין בָּהֶם טֻמְאָה, חוּץ מִכְּנַף הָעוֹז וּבֵיצַת נַעֲמִית הַמְצֻפָּה.
phrases.en: The laws of uncleanness can apply to what was created on the first day. There can be no uncleanness in what was created on the second day. The laws of uncleanness can apply to what was created on the third day. No there can be no uncleanness in what was created on the fourth day and on the fifth day, except for the wing of the vulture or an ostrich-egg that is plated.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי, מַה נִּשְׁתַּנָּה כְנַף הָעוֹז מִכָּל הַכְּנָפָיִם.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yohanan ben Nuri said: why should the wing of a vulture be different from all other wings? The laws of uncleanness can apply to all that was created on the sixth day.

phrases.he: וְכֹל שֶׁנִּבְרָא בַיּוֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁי, טָמֵא
הָעוֹשֶׂה כְלִי קִבּוּל, מִכָּל מָקוֹם, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If one made a receptacle whatever its size it is susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: הָעוֹשֶׂה מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב, מִכָּל מָקוֹם, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If one made a couch or a bed whatever its purpose it is susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: הָעוֹשֶׂה כִיס מֵעוֹר הַמַּצָּה, מִן הַנְּיָר, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If one made a wallet from untanned hide or from papyrus it is susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: הָרִמּוֹן, הָאַלּוֹן, וְהָאֱגוֹז, שֶׁחֲקָקוּם הַתִּינוֹקוֹת לָמֹד בָּהֶם אֶת הֶעָפָר אוֹ שֶׁהִתְקִינוּם לְכַף מֹאזְנַיִם, טָמֵא, שֶׁיֶּשׁ לָהֶם
phrases.en: A pomegranate, an acorn and a nut which children hollowed out to measure dust or fashioned them into a pair of scales, are susceptible to uncleanness, since in the case of children an act is valid though an intention is not.

phrases.he: מַעֲשֶׂה וְאֵין לָהֶם מַחֲשָׁבָה:

קְנֵה מֹאזְנַיִם וְהַמָּחוֹק שֶׁיֶּשׁ בָּהֶן בֵּית קִבּוּל מַתָּכוֹת, וְהָאֵסֶל שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ בֵית קִבּוּל מָעוֹת, וְקָנֶה שֶׁל עָנִי שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ בֵית קִבּוּל מַיִם, וּמַקֵּל שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ בֵית קִבּוּל מְזוּזָה וּמַרְגָּלִיּוֹת, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ טְמֵאִין. וְעַל כֻּלָּן
phrases.en: The beam of a balance and a leveler that contain a receptacle for metal, carrying-stick that has a receptacle for money, a beggar's cane that has a receptacle for water, and a stick that has a receptacle for a mezuzah and for pearls are susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי, אוֹי לִי אִם אֹמַר, אוֹי לִי אִם לֹא אֹמַר:
phrases.en: About all these Rabbi Yohanan ben Zakkai said: Oy to me if I should mention them, Oy to me if I don't mention them.

phrases.he: תַּחְתִּית הַצּוֹרְפִים, טְמֵאָה. וְשֶׁל נַפָּחִין, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: The base of the goldsmiths’ anvil is susceptible to uncleanness, but that of the blacksmiths is clean.

phrases.he: מַשְׁחֶזֶת שֶׁיֶּשׁ בָּהּ בֵּית קִבּוּל שֶׁמֶן, טְמֵאָה. וְשֶׁאֵין בָּהּ, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: A whetting-board which has a receptacle for oil is susceptible to uncleanness, but one that has none is clean.

phrases.he: פִּנְקָס שֶׁיֶּשׁ בָּהּ בֵּית קִבּוּל שַׁעֲוָה, טְמֵאָה. וְשֶׁאֵין בָּהּ, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: A writing-tablet that has a receptacle for wax is susceptible to uncleanness, but one that has none is clean.

phrases.he: מַחֲצֶלֶת הַקַּשׁ וּשְׁפוֹפֶרֶת הַקַּשׁ, רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מְטַמֵּא, וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי מְטַהֵר.
phrases.en: A straw mat or a tube of straw: Rabbi Akiva rules it is susceptible to uncleanness; But Rabbi Yohanan ben Nuri rules that is it clean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, אַף שֶׁל פַּקּוּעוֹת כַּיּוֹצֵא בָהֶן.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: the hollow stalk of colocynth is subject to the same law.

phrases.he: מַחֲצֶלֶת קָנִים וְשֶׁל חֵלֶף, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: A mat of reeds or rushes is clean.

phrases.he: שְׁפוֹפֶרֶת הַקָּנֶה שֶׁחֲתָכָהּ לְקַבָּלָה, טְהוֹרָה, עַד שֶׁיּוֹצִיא אֶת כָּל הַכָּכָי
phrases.en: A reed-tube that was cut for holding anything remains clean until all the pith has been removed.
A wooden chest: Beth Shammai says: it is measured on the inside; And Bet Hillel says: on the outside.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, נִמְדֶּדֶת מִבִּפְנִים.
phrases.en: Both agree that the thickness of the legs and the thickness of the rim are not included in the measurement.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, נִמְדֶּדֶת מִבַּחוּץ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: both agree that the thickness of the legs and the thickness of the rim are included in the measurement, but the space between them is not included.

phrases.he: מוֹדִים אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ שֶׁאֵין עֳבִי הָרַגְלַיִם וָעֳבִי לִזְבְּזִין נִמְדָּד.
רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, מוֹדִים שֶׁעֳבִי הָרַגְלַיִם וָעֳבִי לִזְבְּזִין נִמְדָּד, וּבֵינֵיהֶם אֵינוֹ נִמְדָּד.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon Shezuri ruled: if the legs are one handbreadth high the space between them is not included in the measurement, otherwise it is included.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שְׁזוּרִי אוֹמֵר, אִם הָיוּ הָרַגְלַיִם גְּבוֹהוֹת טֶפַח, אֵין בֵּינֵיהֶם נִמְדָּד.
וְאִם לָאו, בֵּינֵיהֶן נִמְדָּד

מוּכְנִי שֶׁלָּהּ, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהִיא נִשְׁמֶטֶת, אֵינָהּ חִבּוּר לָהּ, וְאֵינָהּ נִמְדֶּדֶת עִמָּהּ, וְאֵינָהּ מַצֶּלֶת עִמָּהּ בְּאֹהֶל הַמֵּת, וְאֵין גּוֹרְרִין אוֹתָהּ בְּשַׁבָּת בִּזְמַן שֶׁיֶּשׁ בְּתוֹכָהּ מָעוֹת.
phrases.en: Its carriage: if it can be slipped off, is not regarded as connected, nor is it included in its measurement, nor does it afford protection together with it in the tent of a corpse, nor may it be drawn along on Shabbat if it contains money.

phrases.he: וְאִם אֵינָהּ נִשְׁמֶטֶת, חִבּוּר לָהּ, וְנִמְדֶּדֶת עִמָּהּ, וּמַצֶּלֶת עִמָּהּ בְּאֹהֶל הַמֵּת, וְגוֹרְרִין אוֹתָהּ בְּשַׁבָּת אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֶּשׁ בְּתוֹכָהּ מָעוֹת.
phrases.en: If it cannot be slipped off, it is regarded as connected, it is included in its measurement, it affords protection together with it in the tent of a corpse, it may be drawn along on Shabbat even if it contains money.

phrases.he: הַקִּמְרוֹן שֶׁלָּהּ, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהוּא קָבוּעַ, חִבּוּר לָהּ וְנִמְדָּד עִמָּהּ.
phrases.en: Its arched top, if it is fixed [to the box], is considered connected and is measured with it, but if it is not fixed it is not connected and is not measured with it.

phrases.he: וְאִם אֵינוֹ קָבוּעַ, אֵינוֹ חִבּוּר לָהּ וְאֵינוֹ נִמְדָּד עִמָּהּ.
כֵּיצַד מוֹדְדִין אוֹתוֹ, רֹאשׁ תּוֹר.
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אִם אֵינָהּ יְכוֹלָה לַעֲמֹד בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ, טְהוֹרָה:
phrases.en: How is it measured? As an ox-head. Rabbi Judah says: if it cannot stand by itself it is clean.

phrases.he: הַשִּׁדָּה וְהַתֵּבָה וְהַמִּגְדָּל שֶׁנִּטְּלָה אַחַת מֵרַגְלֵיהֶן, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמְּקַבְּלִין, טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: If one of the legs was missing from a chest, a box or a cupboard, even though it is still capable of holding [things], it is clean, since it cannot hold [things] in the usual manner.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁאֵינָן מְקַבְּלִין כְּדַרְכָּן, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מְטַמֵּא.
phrases.en: But Rabbi Yose says: it is susceptible to impurity.

phrases.he: וְנַקְלִיטֵי הַמִּטָּה וַחֲמוֹר וְחִפּוּי, טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: The poles of a bed, its base, and [its] covering are clean.

phrases.he: אֵין טָמֵא אֶלָּא מִטָּה וּמַלְבֵּן.
phrases.en: Only the bed itself and its rectangle [frame] are susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: וּמַלְבְּנֵי בְנֵי לֵוִי, טְהוֹרִין
phrases.en: The rectangle frames of the Levites are clean.

phrases.he: מַלְבֵּן שֶׁנְּתָנוֹ עַל לְשׁוֹנוֹת, רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מְטַמְּאִין, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מְטַהֲרִין.
phrases.en: A bed frame that was put on props: Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Judah say it is susceptible to uncleanness. But Rabbi Yose and Rabbi Shimon say that it is clean.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, מַה שָּׁנָה זֶה מִמַּלְבְּנֵי בְנֵי לֵוִי, שֶׁמַּלְבְּנֵי בְנֵי לֵוִי טְהוֹרִין:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose said: Why is this different from the rectangle frames of the Levites which are clean?

phrases.he: מִטָּה שֶׁהָיְתָה טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס, נִטְּלָה קְצָרָה וּשְׁתֵּי כְרָעַיִם, טְמֵאָה.
phrases.en: A bed that had contracted midras uncleanness: If a short side was removed and its two legs still remains it is unclean.

phrases.he: אֲרֻכָּה וּשְׁתֵּי כְרָעַיִם, טְהוֹרָה. רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה מְטַמֵּא.
phrases.en: But if a long side and two legs were removed it becomes clean. Rabbi Nehemiah says: it is unclean.

phrases.he: גָּדַד שְׁתֵּי לְשׁוֹנוֹת לוֹכְסָן, גָּדַד שְׁתֵּי כְרָעַיִם (טֶפַח עַל טֶפַח) לוֹכְסָן, אוֹ שֶׁמִּעֲטָהּ פָּחוֹת מִטֶּפַח, טְהוֹרָה
phrases.en: If two props at opposite corners were cut off, or if two legs at opposite corners were cut off, or if the bed was reduced to a level of less than a handbreadth, it becomes clean.

phrases.he: מִטָּה שֶׁהָיְתָה טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס, נִשְׁבְּרָה אֲרֻכָּה וְתִקְּנָהּ, טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס.
phrases.en: A bed that had contracted midras impurity:If a long side of it was broken and then he repaired it, it still retains its midras impurity.

phrases.he: נִשְׁבְּרָה שְׁנִיָּה וְתִקְּנָהּ, טְהוֹרָה מִן הַמִּדְרָס, אֲבָל טְמֵאָה מַגַּע מִדְרָס.
phrases.en: If the second side was also broke and then he repaired it, it becomes pure from midras impurity but is unclean by virtue of contact with midras.

phrases.he: לֹא הִסְפִּיק לְתַקֵּן אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה עַד שֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרָה שְׁנִיָּה, טְהוֹרָה
phrases.en: If before one could manage to repair the first side the second one broke, the bed becomes clean.

phrases.he: כֶּרַע שֶׁהָיְתָה טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס, וְחִבְּרָהּ לַמִּטָּה, כֻּלָּהּ טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס.
phrases.en: If a [bed] leg that had contracted midras uncleanness was joined to a bed, all the bed contracts midras uncleanness.

phrases.he: פֵּרְשָׁה, הִיא טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס, וְהַמִּטָּה מַגַּע מִדְרָס.
phrases.en: If it was subsequently taken off, it retains its midras uncleanness while the bed is unclean from contact with midras.

phrases.he: הָיְתָה טְמֵאָה טֻמְאַת שִׁבְעָה וְחִבְּרָהּ לַמִּטָּה, כֻּלָּהּ טְמֵאָה טֻמְאַת שִׁבְעָה.
phrases.en: If a bed leg that was subject to a seven-day uncleanness was joined to a bed, all the bed contracts seven-day uncleanness.

phrases.he: פֵּרְשָׁה, הִיא טְמֵאָה טֻמְאַת שִׁבְעָה, וְהַמִּטָּה טְמֵאָה טֻמְאַת עָרֶב.
phrases.en: If it was subsequently taken off it remains subject to seven-day uncleanness while the bed is only subject to evening-uncleanness.

phrases.he: הָיְתָה טְמֵאָה טֻמְאַת עֶרֶב וְחִבְּרָהּ לַמִּטָּה, כֻּלָּהּ טְמֵאָה טֻמְאַת עָרֶב.
phrases.en: If a leg that was subject to evening uncleanness was joined to a bed, all the bed contracts evening uncleanness.

phrases.he: פֵּרְשָׁה, הִיא טְמֵאָה טֻמְאַת עֶרֶב, וְהַמִּטָּה טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: If it was subsequently taken off it is still subject to evening uncleanness while the bed becomes clean.

phrases.he: וְכֵן הַשֵּׁן שֶׁל מַעְדֵּר
phrases.en: The same law applies also to the prong of a mattock.

phrases.he: תְּפִלָּה, אַרְבָּעָה כֵלִים. הִתִּיר קְצִיצָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה וְתִקְּנָהּ, טְמֵאָה טְמֵא מֵת, וְכֵן שְׁנִיָּה, וְכֵן שְׁלִישִׁית.
phrases.en: A tefillin box consisting of four vessels: if the first compartment was unloosed, and then he mended it, it retains its corpse uncleanness. So is it also the case with the second and the third.

phrases.he: הִתִּיר אֶת הָרְבִיעִית, טְהוֹרָה מִטְּמֵא מֵת, אֲבָל טְמֵאָה מַגַּע טְמֵא מֵת.
phrases.en: If he unloosed the fourth it becomes free from corpse uncleanness but it is still unclean from contact with corpse uncleanness.

phrases.he: חָזַר לָרִאשׁוֹנָה וְהִתִּירָהּ וְתִקְּנָהּ, טְמֵאָה בְמַגָּע, וְכֵן שְׁנִיָּה.
phrases.en: If he went back to the first compartment and unloosed and mended it, it remains unclean from contact. So also in the case of the second compartment.

phrases.he: הִתִּיר אֶת הַשְּׁלִישִׁית, טְהוֹרָה, שֶׁהָרְבִיעִית בְּמַגָּע, וְאֵין מַגָּע עוֹשֶׂה מַגָּע
phrases.en: If he then unloosed the third compartment and mended it becomes clean, since the fourth is unclean from contact, and what is unclean from contact cannot convey uncleanness by contact.

phrases.he: מִטָּה שֶׁנִּגְנַב חֶצְיָהּ, אוֹ אָבַד חֶצְיָהּ, אוֹ חֲלָקוּהָ אַחִין, אוֹ שֻׁתָּפִין, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: A bed half of which was stolen or lost, or one which brothers or joint owners divided between themselves, becomes clean.

phrases.he: הֶחֱזִירוּהָ, מְקַבֶּלֶת טֻמְאָה מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא.
phrases.en: If it was restored it is susceptible to uncleanness henceforth.

phrases.he: מִטָּה מִטַּמְּאָה חֲבִילָה, וּמִטַּהֶרֶת חֲבִילָה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר.
phrases.en: A bed may contract uncleanness and be rendered clean when all its parts are bound together, the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, מִטַּמְּאָה אֵבָרִים, וּמִטַּהֶרֶת אֵבָרִים:
phrases.en: But the sages say: it can contract uncleanness and is rendered clean in single parts.

phrases.he: הַמְפָרֵק אֶת הַמִּטָּה לְהַטְבִּילָהּ, וְהַנּוֹגֵעַ בַּחֲבָלִין, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: One who dismantles a bed in order that he might immerse it and [while doing so] touches the ropes remains clean.

phrases.he: הַחֶבֶל מֵאֵימָתַי הוּא חִבּוּר לַמִּטָּה, מִשֶּׁיְּסָרֵג בָּהּ שְׁלֹשָׁה בָתִּים.
phrases.en: When does the rope begin to constitute a connective with the bed? As soon as three rows of meshes of it have been knotted.

phrases.he: וְהַנּוֹגֵעַ מִן הַקֶּשֶׁר וְלִפְנִים, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: And [if another rope was tied to this one] and a person touches it: If from the knot inwards he becomes unclean; But if from the knot outwards he remains clean.

phrases.he: מִן הַקֶּשֶׁר וְלַחוּץ, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: As to the loose ends of the knot, any one that touches that part which is needed for it becomes unclean.

phrases.he: נִימֵי הַקֶּשֶׁר, הַנּוֹגֵעַ בְּצָרְכּוֹ, טָמֵא. וְכַמָּה הוּא צָרְכּוֹ,
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, שָׁלֹשׁ אֶצְבָּעוֹת:
phrases.en: And how much is needed for it? Rabbi Judah says: three fingerbreadths.

phrases.he: הַחֶבֶל הַיּוֹצֵא מִן הַמִּטָּה, עַד חֲמִשָּׁה טְפָחִים, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: A rope that hangs out from a bed:If it is shorter than five handbreadths, it is clean, If it is from five to ten handbreadths long, it is unclean.

phrases.he: מֵחֲמִשָּׁה וְעַד עֲשָׂרָה, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: From ten handbreadths and longer is clean; For it is with [this rope] that paschal lambs were tied and beds were lowered down.

phrases.he: מֵעֲשָׂרָה וְלַחוּץ, טָהוֹר, שֶׁבּוֹ קוֹשְׁרִין אֶת הַפְּסָחִים, וּמְשַׁלְשְׁלִין אֶת הַמִּטּוֹת
מִזְרָן הַיּוֹצֵא מִן הַמִּטָּה, כָּל שֶׁהוּא, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: If a part of a mattress hangs over, it is unclean whatever its length, the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, עַד עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: only that which is shorter than ten handbreadths.

phrases.he: שְׁיָרֵי מִזְרָן, שִׁבְעָה טְפָחִים, כְּדֵי לַעֲשׂוֹתוֹ חֶבֶק לַחֲמוֹר
phrases.en: The remnant of a mattress remains unclean if the length is at least seven handbreadths from which a donkey's covering can be made.

phrases.he: נִשָּׂא הַזָּב עַל הַמִּטָּה וְעַל הַמִּזְרָן, מְטַמֵּא שְׁנַיִם וּפוֹסֵל אֶחָד, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: If a zav was carried on a bed and on its mattress, the latter causes an uncleanness of two grades and an unfitness of one grade, the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, נִשָּׂא הַזָּב עַל הַמִּטָּה וְעַל הַמִּזְרָן, עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים, מְטַמֵּא שְׁנַיִם וּפוֹסֵל אֶחָד.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: if a zav was carried on a bed and on its mattress the part that is shorter than ten handbreadths causes an uncleanness of two grades and an unfitness of one grade, but that which is over the ten handbreadths causes only an uncleanness of one grade and an unfitness of one grade.

phrases.he: מֵעֲשָׂרָה וְלַחוּץ, מְטַמֵּא אֶחָד וּפוֹסֵל אֶחָד.
phrases.en: If he was carried on the mattress, [on the overhanging part] that was shorter than ten handbreadths, it becomes unclean, but if on the part that was longer than ten handbreadths it remains clean.

phrases.he: נִשָּׂא עַל הַמִּזְרָן, מֵעֲשָׂרָה וְלִפְנִים, טָמֵא. מֵעֲשָׂרָה וְלַחוּץ, טָהוֹר
מִטָּה שֶׁהָיְתָה טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס, וְכָרַךְ לָהּ מִזְרָן, כֻּלָּהּ טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס.
phrases.en: If around a bed that had contracted midras uncleanness one wrapped a mattress, the whole becomes subject to midras uncleanness.

phrases.he: פֵּרְשָׁה, הִיא טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס, וְהַמִּזְרָן מַגַּע מִדְרָס.
phrases.en: If it was removed, the bed remains subject to midras uncleanness but the mattress is unclean only from contact with midras.

phrases.he: הָיְתָה טְמֵאָה טֻמְאַת שִׁבְעָה, וְכָרַךְ לָהּ מִזְרָן, כֻּלָּהּ טְמֵאָה טֻמְאַת שִׁבְעָה.
phrases.en: If around a bed that had contracted seven-day uncleanness one wrapped a mattress, the whole becomes subject to seven-day uncleanness.

phrases.he: פֵּרְשָׁה, הִיא טְמֵאָה טֻמְאַת שִׁבְעָה, וְהַמִּזְרָן טָמֵא טֻמְאַת עָרֶב.
phrases.en: If it was removed, the bed remains subject to seven-day uncleanness but the mattress is unclean until the evening.

phrases.he: הָיְתָה טְמֵאָה טֻמְאַת עֶרֶב, וְכָרַךְ לָהּ מִזְרָן, כֻּלָּהּ טְמֵאָה טֻמְאַת עָרֶב.
phrases.en: If the bed was subject to evening uncleanness and around it he wrapped a mattress, the whole becomes subject to evening uncleanness; If it was removed, the bed remains subject to evening uncleanness but the mattress becomes clean.

phrases.he: פֵּרְשָׁה, הִיא טְמֵאָה טֻמְאַת עֶרֶב, וְהַמִּזְרָן טָהוֹר
מִטָּה שֶׁכָּרַךְ לָהּ מִזְרָן, וְנָגַע בָּהֶן הַמֵּת, טְמֵאִין טֻמְאַת שִׁבְעָה.
phrases.en: If a mattress was wrapped around a bed and a corpse touched them, they are subject to a seven-day uncleanness; If they are taken apart they are still subject to a seven-day uncleanness.

phrases.he: פֵּרְשׁוּ, טְמֵאִין טֻמְאַת שִׁבְעָה.
phrases.en: If a sheretz touched them they are subject to an evening uncleanness; If they are taken apart they are still subject to evening uncleanness.

phrases.he: נָגַע בָּהֶן הַשֶּׁרֶץ, טְמֵאִין טֻמְאַת עָרֶב.
phrases.en: A bed from which the two longer sides were removed and two new ones were prepared for it but the original sockets were not changed: If the new sides were broken the bed retains its uncleanness, But if the old ones were broken it becomes clean, since all depends on the old ones.

phrases.he: פֵּרְשׁוּ, טְמֵאִין טֻמְאַת עָרֶב.
מִטָּה שֶׁנִּטְּלוּ שְׁתֵּי אֲרֻכּוֹת שֶׁלָּהּ וְעָשָׂה לָהּ חֲדָשׁוֹת, וְלֹא שִׁנָּה אֶת הַנְּקָבִים, נִשְׁתַּבְּרוּ חֲדָשׁוֹת, טְמֵאָה.
וִישָׁנוֹת, טְהוֹרָה, שֶׁהַכֹּל הוֹלֵךְ אַחַר הַיְשָׁנוֹת
תֵּבָה שֶׁפִּתְחָהּ מִלְמַעְלָה, טְמֵאָה טְמֵא מֵת.
phrases.en: A box whose opening is at the top is susceptible to corpse uncleanness.

phrases.he: נִפְחֲתָה מִלְמַעְלָה, טְמֵאָה טְמֵא מֵת. נִפְחֲתָה מִלְּמַטָּה, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: If a piece fell out above it is still susceptible to corpse uncleanness. If it was damaged below, it becomes clean.

phrases.he: מְגוּרוֹת שֶׁבָּהּ, טְמֵאוֹת, וְאֵינָם חִבּוּר לָהּ
phrases.en: The compartments within it remain unclean and are not regarded as a connected to it.

phrases.he: הַתּוּרְמֵל שֶׁנִּפְחֲתָה כִּיס שֶׁבְּתוֹכוֹ, טָמֵא, וְאֵינוֹ חִבּוּר לוֹ.
phrases.en: A shepherd's bag which the pocket within it was damaged retains its uncleanness and is not regarded as a connected to it.

phrases.he: הַחֵמֶת שֶׁבֵּיצִים שֶׁלָּהּ מְקַבְּלוֹת עִמָּהּ, וְנִפְחֲתוּ, טְהוֹרוֹת, שֶׁאֵינָם מְקַבְּלוֹת כְּדַרְכָּן
phrases.en: A skin whose testicle bags serve also as receptacles and they were damaged, they become clean, since they will no longer serve their original purpose.

phrases.he: תֵּבָה שֶׁפִּתְחָהּ מִצִּדָּהּ, טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס וּטְמֵא מֵת.
phrases.en: A box whose opening is at the side is susceptible to both midras uncleanness and corpse uncleanness.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, אֵימָתַי, בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵינָהּ גְּבוֹהָה עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים, אוֹ שֶׁאֵין לָהּ לִזְבֵּז טֶפַח.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose said: When does this apply? When it is less than ten handbreadths in height or when it does not have a rim one handbreadth deep.

phrases.he: נִפְחֲתָה מִלְמַעְלָן, טְמֵאָה טְמֵא מֵת.
phrases.en: If it was damaged above it is still susceptible to corpse uncleanness.

phrases.he: נִפְחֲתָה מִלְּמַטָּן, רַבִּי מֵאִיר מְטַמֵּא.
phrases.en: If it was damaged below: Rabbi Meir rules that it is susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים מְטַהֲרִין, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁבָּטַל הָעִקָּר, בָּטְלָה הַטְּפֵלָה
phrases.en: But the sages rule that it is clean because if the primary function ceases the secondary one also ceases.

phrases.he: מִשְׁפֶּלֶת שֶׁנִּפְחֲתָה מִלְּקַבֵּל רִמּוֹנִים, רַבִּי מֵאִיר מְטַמֵּא.
phrases.en: A dung-basket that was so damaged that it will not hold pomegranates: Rabbi Meir says is still susceptible to uncleanness, But the sages say that it is clean because if the primary function ceases the secondary one also ceases.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים מְטַהֲרִים, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁבָּטַל הָעִקָּר, בָּטְלָה הַטְּפֵלָה
הַכָּרִים וְהַכְּסָתוֹת וְהַשַּׂקִּין וְהַמַּרְצוּפִין שֶׁנִּפְחֲתוּ, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ טְמֵאִים מִדְרָס.
phrases.en: Pillows, bed coverings, sacks and packing cases that were damaged are still susceptible to midras uncleanness.

phrases.he: הַקְּלוּסְטָר, אַרְבָּעָה קַבִּין, הַתּוּרְמֵל חֲמֵשֶׁת קַבִּין, הַכְּרֵיתִית סְאָה.
phrases.en: A fodder-bag that can hold four kav, a shepherd's bag that can hold five kav, a traveling bag that can hold a se'ah, a skin that can hold seven kav, Rabbi Judah adds: also a spice-bag, and a food wallet that can hold the smallest quantity are susceptible to midras uncleanness.

phrases.he: הַחֵמֶת שֶׁל שִׁבְעַת קַבִּין,
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף הָרִבְצָל וְהַמִּזְוָדָה כָּל שֶׁהֵן, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ טְמֵאִין מִדְרָס.
phrases.en: If any of them was damaged it becomes clean, since if the primary function ceases the secondary function also ceases.

phrases.he: וְכֻלָּם שֶׁנִּפְחֲתוּ, טְהוֹרִים, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁבָּטַל הָעִקָּר, וּבָטְלָה הַטְּפֵלָה
חֵמֶת חֲלִילִין, טְהוֹרָה מִן הַמִּדְרָס. עֲרֵבַת פִּיסוֹנוֹת,
phrases.en: A bagpipe is not susceptible to midras uncleanness.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, מִדְרָס.
phrases.en: A trough for mixing mortar: Bet Shammai says: it is susceptible to midras uncleanness , And Bet Hillel says it is susceptible to corpse uncleanness only.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, טְמֵא מֵת.
phrases.en: If a trough of a capacity from two log to nine kav is split, it becomes susceptible to midras uncleanness.

phrases.he: עֲרֵבָה מִשְּׁנֵי לֹג וְעַד תִּשְׁעָה קַבִּין שֶׁנִּסְדְּקָה, טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס.
phrases.en: If he left it out in the rain and it swelled it is susceptible to corpse uncleanness alone.

phrases.he: הִנִּיחָהּ בַּגְּשָׁמִים וְנִתְפְּחָה, טְמֵאָה טְמֵא מֵת.
phrases.en: [If he left it out] during the east wind and it split, it is susceptible to midras uncleanness.

phrases.he: בַּקָּדִים וְנִסְדְּקָה, מְקַבֶּלֶת מִדְרָס.
phrases.en: In this respect the law is stricter in the case of remnants of wooden vessels than in [that of such vessels] in their original condition.

phrases.he: זֶה חֹמֶר בִּשְׁיָרֵי כְלֵי עֵץ מִבִּתְחִלָּתָן.
phrases.en: It is also stricter in regard to the remnants of wicker vessels than [to such vessels] as are in their original condition, for when they are in their original condition they are insusceptible to uncleanness until their rim is finished, but after their rim has been finished, even though their edges fell away leaving only the slightest trace of them, they are unclean.

phrases.he: וְחֹמֶר בִּשְׁיָרֵי כְלֵי נְצָרִים מִבִּתְחִלָּתָן, שֶׁמִּתְּחִלָּתָן אֵינָם מְקַבְּלִים טֻמְאָה עַד שֶׁיִּתְחַסֵּמוּ.
נִתְחַסְּמוּ, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנָּשְׁרוּ שִׂפְתוֹתֵיהֶן כָּל שֶׁהֵן, טְמֵאִין
מַקֵּל שֶׁעֲשָׂאוֹ בֵּית יָד לְקֻרְדֹּם, חִבּוּר לַטֻּמְאָה בִּשְׁעַת מְלָאכָה.
phrases.en: If a stick was used as a handle for a hatchet, it is regarded as connected for uncleanness at the time of use.

phrases.he: הַדְּיוּסְטָר, חִבּוּר לַטֻּמְאָה בִּשְׁעַת מְלָאכָה.
phrases.en: A yarn winder is regarded as connected for uncleanness at the time of its use.

phrases.he: קְבָעוֹ בִכְלוֹנָס, טָמֵא, וְאֵינוֹ חִבּוּר לָהּ.
phrases.en: If it was fixed to a pole it is susceptible to uncleanness, but it is not considered connected to it.

phrases.he: עָשָׂה לוֹ דְיוּסְטָר, אֵין טָמֵא אֶלָּא צָרְכּוֹ.
phrases.en: If the pole itself was converted into a yarn winder, only that part which is needed for use is susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: כִּסֵּא שֶׁקְּבָעוֹ בִכְלוֹנָס, טָמֵא, וְאֵינוֹ חִבּוּר לוֹ.
phrases.en: A seat that was fixed to the pole is susceptible to uncleanness, but the latter is not regarded as connected to it.

phrases.he: עָשָׂה בוֹ כִסֵּא, אֵין טָמֵא אֶלָּא מְקוֹמוֹ.
phrases.en: If the pole itself was turned into a seat, only the place of the seat is susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: קְבָעוֹ בְקוֹרַת בֵּית הַבַּד, טָמֵא, וְאֵינוֹ חִבּוּר לָהּ.
phrases.en: A seat that was fixed to the beam of an olive-press is susceptible to uncleanness, but it is not connected to it.

phrases.he: עָשָׂה בְרֹאשָׁהּ כִּסֵּא, טָהוֹר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאוֹמְרִין לוֹ, עֲמֹד וְנַעֲשֶׂה אֶת מְלַאכְתֵּנוּ
phrases.en: If the end of a beam was turned into a seat it remains clean, because people would tell him, "Get up and let us do our work."

phrases.he: עֲרֵבָה גְדוֹלָה שֶׁנִּפְחֲתָה מִלְּקַבֵּל רִמּוֹנִים, וְהִתְקִינָהּ לִישִׁיבָה, רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מְטַמֵּא.
phrases.en: If a large trough was so damaged that it could no longer hold pomegranates and he fixed it to be used as a seat: Rabbi Akiva says that it is susceptible to uncleanness, But the sages say that it remains clean unless its rough parts have been smoothed.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים מְטַהֲרִין, עַד שֶׁיְּקַצֵּעַ.
phrases.en: If it was turned into a feeding bowl for cattle, even if it was fixed to a wall, it is susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: עֲשָׂאָהּ אֵבוּס לַבְּהֵמָה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁקְּבָעָהּ בַּכֹּתֶל, טְמֵאָה
כֹּפֶת שֶׁקְּבָעוֹ בְנִדְבָּךְ, קְבָעוֹ וְלֹא בָנָה עָלָיו, בָּנָה עָלָיו וְלֹא קְבָעוֹ, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: A wood block that was fixed to a row on a wall, whether he fixed it and did not built upon it or built upon it but did not fix it, it is susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: קְבָעוֹ וּבָנָה עָלָיו, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If he fixed it and also built upon, it is clean.

phrases.he: מַפָּץ שֶׁנְּתָנוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי הַקּוֹרוֹת, קְבָעוֹ וְלֹא נָתַן עָלָיו אֶת הַמַּעֲזִיבָה, נָתַן עָלָיו אֶת הַמַּעֲזִיבָה וְלֹא קְבָעוֹ, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: Matting that was spread over the roof-beams, whether he fixed it but did not put on the plasterwork or whether he put on the plasterwork but did not fix it, it is susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: קְבָעוֹ וְנָתַן עָלָיו אֶת הַמַּעֲזִיבָה, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If it was fixed and he laid plasterwork over it, it is clean.

phrases.he: קְעָרָה שֶׁקְּבָעָהּ בְּשִׁדָּה תֵּבָה וּמִגְדָּל, כְּדֶרֶךְ קַבָּלָתָהּ, טְמֵאָה.
phrases.en: A dish that was fixed to a chest, box or cupboard: If in such a manner as to hold its contents in the usual way, it is susceptible to uncleanness, But if it was in a manner that it cannot hold its contents in the usual way it is clean.

phrases.he: שֶׁלֹּא כְדֶרֶךְ קַבָּלָתָהּ, טְהוֹרָה
סָדִין שֶׁהוּא טְמֵא מִדְרָס וַעֲשָׂאוֹ וִילוֹן, טָהוֹר מִן הַמִּדְרָס, אֲבָל טָמֵא טְמֵא מֵת. מֵאֵימָתַי הִיא טָהֳרָתוֹ.
phrases.en: If a sheet that was susceptible to midras uncleanness made into a curtain, it becomes clean from midras uncleanness but it is still susceptible to corpse uncleanness.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, מִשֶּׁיִּתָּבֵר.
phrases.en: When does it become insusceptible to [midras] uncleanness? Bet Shammai says: when the loops have been tied to it.

phrases.he: בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, מִשֶּׁיִּקָּשֵׁר.
phrases.en: . Bet Hillel says: when it has been attached.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, מִשֶּׁיִּקָּבֵעַ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says: when it has been fixed.

phrases.he: מַחֲצֶלֶת שֶׁעָשָׂה לָהּ קָנִים לְאָרְכָּהּ, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: A mat whose reeds stretched lengthwise is insusceptible to uncleanness; But the sages rule: only if they lay in the shape of [the Greek letter] chi.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, עַד שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה כְמִין כִי.
phrases.en: If they were laid along its width and there was a distance of less than four handbreadths between the two reeds, it is insusceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: עֲשָׂאָם לְרָחְבָּהּ וְאֵין בֵּין קָנֶה לַחֲבֵרוֹ אַרְבָּעָה טְפָחִים, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If it was divided along its width, Rabbi Judah rules that is clean.

phrases.he: נֶחְלְקָה לְרָחְבָּהּ, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מְטַהֵר.
phrases.en: So also, where the end-knots are untied, it is clean.

phrases.he: וְכֵן הַמַּתִּיר רָאשֵׁי הַמַּעֲדַנִּין, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: If it was divided along its length but three end-knots remained intact across a stretch of six handbreadths, it is susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: נֶחְלְקָה לְאָרְכָּהּ וְנִשְׁתַּיְּרוּ בָהּ שְׁלֹשָׁה מַעֲדַנִּים שֶׁל שִׁשָּׁה טְפָחִים, טְמֵאָה.
phrases.en: When does a mat become susceptible to uncleanness? When its rough ends are trimmed, this being the completion of its manufacture.

phrases.he: מַחֲצֶלֶת, מֵאֵימָתַי מְקַבֶּלֶת טֻמְאָה.
מִשֶּׁתִּקָּנֵב, וְהִיא גְמַר מְלַאכְתָּהּ
הַנּוֹגֵעַ בַּכֹּבֶד הָעֶלְיוֹן, בַּכֹּבֶד הַתַּחְתּוֹן, בַּנִּירִים, וּבַקֵּירוֹס, וּבְחוּט שֶׁהֶעֱבִירוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי אַרְגָּמָן, וּבְעִירָה שֶׁאֵינוֹ עָתִיד לְהַחֲזִירָהּ, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: One who touches the upper beam, the lower beam, the harnesses, the sley, the thread that is drawn over purple material, or a spool which is not to be shot back, remains clean.

phrases.he: בְּנֶפֶשׁ הַמַּסֶּכֶת, וּבַשְּׁתִי הָעוֹמֵד, וּבְכָפוּל שֶׁהֶעֱבִירוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי הָאַרְגָּמָן, וּבְעִירָה שֶׁהִיא עֲתִידָה לְהַחֲזִירָהּ, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If he touches the woof, the standing warp, the double thread that is drawn over purple material or a spool which is to be shot back, he becomes unclean.

phrases.he: הַנּוֹגֵעַ בַּצֶּמֶר שֶׁעַל הָאִימָּה, בָּאַשְׁוָיָה, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If one touches the wool that is on the distaff, or on the spool, he remains clean.

phrases.he: הַנּוֹגֵעַ בַּפִּיקָה, עַד שֶׁלֹּא פֵרְעָהּ, טָמֵא. מִשֶּׁפֵּרְעָהּ, טָהוֹר
phrases.en: If he touches the spinner: Before it was uncovered he is unclean, After it was uncovered he remains clean.

phrases.he: הַנּוֹגֵעַ בָּעֹל, וּבַקַּטְרָב, בָּעַיִן, וּבָעֲבוֹת, אֲפִלּוּ בִשְׁעַת מְלָאכָה, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: One who touches the yoke, the crossbar, the collar-piece, or the thick ropes, even when they are being used, he remains clean.

phrases.he: בַּחֶרֶב, וּבַבֹּרֶךְ, וּבַיָּצוּל, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If he touched the tail piece, knee or handle, he becomes unclean.

phrases.he: בָּעַיִן שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת, בַּלְּחָיַיִן, וּבָעֲרָיִין, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If he touched the metal rings, the guides, or the flanks, he becomes unclean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מְטַהֵר בַּלְּחָיַיִם, שֶׁאֵינָם עֲשׂוּיִן אֶלָּא לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הֶעָפָר
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says that he remains clean if he touched the guides since they only serve to increase the soil.

phrases.he: הַנּוֹגֵעַ בְּיַד מְגֵרָה, מִכָּאן וּמִכָּאן, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: One who touches the handle of a saw at either end becomes unclean; [If he touched] its string, cord, cross-piece or side-pieces, a carpenter's vice, or the bow-handle of a bow-drill, he remains clean.

phrases.he: בַּחוּט, וּבַמְּשִׁיחָה, בָּאַמָּה, וּבַסְּנִיפִין, בַּמַּכְבֵּשׁ שֶׁל חָרָשׁ, וּבַקַּשְׁטָנִית, טָהוֹר.
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף הַנּוֹגֵעַ בַּמַּלְבֵּן שֶׁל מַסָּר הַגָּדוֹל, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: so too he who touches the frame of a large saw remains clean.

phrases.he: הַנּוֹגֵעַ בַּיֶּתֶר וּבַקֶּשֶׁת, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהִיא מְתוּחָה, טָהוֹר. מְצֻדַּת הָאֵישׁוּת, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: One who touches the bow-string or the bow, even though it was stretched, he remains clean. A mole-trap is clean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, כָּל זְמַן שֶׁהִיא מְתוּחָה, חִבּוּר:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: when it is stretched, the separate parts are [regarded as] connected.

phrases.he: הַשֻּׁלְחָן וְהַדְּלֻפְקִי שֶׁנִּפְחֲתוּ, אוֹ שֶׁחִפָּן בְּשַׁיִשׁ וְשִׁיֵּר בָּהֶם מְקוֹם הַנָּחַת הַכּוֹסוֹת, טְמֵאִים.
phrases.en: If a table or a side-board was damaged or he covered them with marble but room was left for cups to be set, it is unclean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, מְקוֹם הַנָּחַת חֲתִיכוֹת:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah ruled: there must be room enough for pieces of food.

phrases.he: הַשֻּׁלְחָן שֶׁנִּטְּלָה אַחַת מֵרַגְלָיו, טָהוֹר. נִטְּלָה שְׁנִיָּה, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: A table one of whose legs was removed is clean. If a second leg was removed it is still clean.

phrases.he: נִטְּלָה הַשְּׁלִישִׁית, טָמֵא כְּשֶׁיַּחְשֹׁב עָלָיו.
phrases.en: But if a third was removed it becomes unclean where the owner has the intention of using it.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אֵין צָרִיךְ מַחֲשָׁבָה. וְכֵן הַדְּלֻפְקִי:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: no intention is necessary. The same law applies also to the side-board.

phrases.he: סַפְסָל שֶׁנִּטַּל אַחַד מֵרָאשָׁיו, טָהוֹר. נִטַּל הַשֵּׁנִי, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: A bench, one of whose legs was removed, is clean. If its second leg also was removed it is still clean.

phrases.he: אִם יֶשׁ בּוֹ גֹבַהּ טֶפַח, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If it was one handbreadth high it is unclean.

phrases.he: שְׁרַפְרַף שֶׁנִּטַּל אַחַד מֵרָאשָׁיו, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: A footstool one of whose legs was removed is unclean.

phrases.he: וְכֵן הַכִּסֵּא שֶׁלִּפְנֵי קַתֶּדְרָא
phrases.en: The same applies to the stool in front of a cathedra.

phrases.he: כִּסֵּא שֶׁל כַּלָּה שֶׁנִּטְּלוּ חִפּוּיָו, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי מְטַמְּאִין, וּבֵית הִלֵּל מְטַהֲרִין.
phrases.en: A bride's stool which lost the coverings for the seatboards: Bet Shammai rules that it still susceptible to uncleanness, And Bet Hillel rules that it is clean.

phrases.he: שַׁמַּאי אוֹמֵר, אַף מַלְבֵּן שֶׁל כִּסֵּא, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: Shammai rules: even the frame of the stool is susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: כִּסֵּא שֶׁקְּבָעוֹ בַעֲרֵבָה, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי מְטַמְּאִין, וּבֵית הִלֵּל מְטַהֲרִין.
phrases.en: A stool which was fixed to a kneading-trough, Bet Shammai rules that it susceptible to uncleanness, And Bet Hillel rules that it is clean.

phrases.he: שַׁמַּאי אוֹמֵר, אַף הֶעָשׂוּי בָּהּ
phrases.en: Shammai rules: even one made out of it is susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: כִּסֵּא שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ חִפּוּיָו יוֹצְאִין, וְנִטְּלוּ, טָמֵא, שֶׁכֵּן דַּרְכּוֹ לִהְיוֹת מַטֵּהוּ עַל צִדּוֹ וְיוֹשֵׁב עָלָיו:
phrases.en: A chair whose seat boards did not project and then they were removed, it is still susceptible to uncleanness, for it is usual to turn it on its side and to sit on it.

phrases.he: כִּסֵּא שֶׁנִּטַּל חִפּוּיוֹ הָאֶמְצָעִי וְהַחִיצוֹנִים קַיָּמִים, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: A chair whose middle seat board was removed but the outer ones remained, it is still susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: נִטְּלוּ הַחִיצוֹנִים וְהָאֶמְצָעִי קַיָּם, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If the outer ones were removed and the middle seat board remained it is also susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, אִם הָיָה רָחָב טָפַח:
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: only if it was a handbreadth wide.

phrases.he: כִּסֵּא שֶׁנִּטְּלוּ שְׁנַיִם מֵחִפּוּיָו זֶה בְצַד זֶה, רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מְטַמֵּא, וַחֲכָמִים מְטַהֲרִין.
phrases.en: A chair, of which two seat boards were removed, this one next to this one: Rabbi Akiva says: it is susceptible to impurity; And the sages say that it is clean.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, אַף כִּסֵּא שֶׁל כַּלָּה שֶׁנִּטְּלוּ חִפּוּיָו וְנִשְׁתַּיֵּר בּוֹ בֵית קַבָּלָה, טָהוֹר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁבָּטַל הָעִקָּר וּבָטְלָה הַטְּפֵלָה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah said: so too if the seat boards of a bride's chair were lost, though the receptacle under remained, it is clean, since where the primary function has ceased, the secondary one also ceases.

phrases.he: שִׁדָּה שֶׁנִּטַּל הָעֶלְיוֹן, טְמֵאָה מִפְּנֵי הַתַּחְתּוֹן.
phrases.en: A chest whose top part was removed is still susceptible to uncleanness on account of its bottom; If its bottom was removed it is still susceptible to uncleanness on account of its top part.

phrases.he: נִטַּל הַתַּחְתּוֹן, טְמֵאָה מִפְּנֵי הָעֶלְיוֹן.
phrases.en: If both the top part and the bottom part were removed: Rabbi Judah says that it is susceptible to uncleanness on account of its sides, But the sages rule that it is clean.

phrases.he: נִטַּל הָעֶלְיוֹן וְהַתַּחְתּוֹן, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מְטַמֵּא מִפְּנֵי הַדַּפִּין, וַחֲכָמִים מְטַהֲרִין.
phrases.en: A stonecutter's seat is subject to midras uncleanness.

phrases.he: יְשִׁיבַת הַסַּתָּת, טָמֵא מִדְרָס
כֹּפֶת שֶׁסֵּרְקוֹ, וְכִרְכְּמוֹ, וַעֲשָׂאוֹ פָנִים, רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מְטַמֵּא.
phrases.en: A [wooden] block which was painted red or saffron, or was polished: Rabbi Akiva says that it is susceptible to uncleanness, But the sages say that it remains clean unless [a seat] was carved out.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים מְטַהֲרִין, עַד שֶׁיָּחֹק בּוֹ.
phrases.en: A small basket or a big one that was filled with straw or other soft material remains clean [even] if it was prepared as a seat.

phrases.he: הַסַּל וְהַכַּלְכָּלָה שֶׁמִּלְאָן תֶּבֶן אוֹ מוֹכִין, הִתְקִינָן לִישִׁיבָה, טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: But if it was plaited over with reed-grass or with a cord it becomes susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: סֵרְגָן בְּגֶמִי אוֹ בִמְשִׁיחָה, טְמֵאִין
הָאַסְלָה, טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס וּטְמֵא מֵת.
phrases.en: A toilet is subject to both midras and corpse uncleanness.

phrases.he: פֵּרְשָׁה, הָעוֹר טָמֵא מִדְרָס, וְהַבַּרְזֶל טָמֵא טְמֵא מֵת.
phrases.en: If the leather seat was separated, the leather is subject to midras uncleanness and the iron is subject only to corpse uncleanness.

phrases.he: הַטְּרַסְקָל שֶׁחִפּוּיוֹ שֶׁל עוֹר, טָמֵא מִדְרָס וּטְמֵא מֵת.
phrases.en: A folding stool whose cover is of leather is subject to both midras and corpse uncleanness.

phrases.he: פֵּרְשָׁה, הָעוֹר טָמֵא מִדְרָס, וְהַטְּרַסְקָל טָהוֹר מִכְּלוּם.
phrases.en: If it was taken apart, the leather is subject to midras uncleanness while the stool is altogether clean.

phrases.he: סַפְסָלִין שֶׁבַּמֶּרְחָץ וּשְׁתֵּי רַגְלָיו שֶׁל עֵץ, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: A bath-house bench that has two wooden legs is susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: אַחַת שֶׁל עֵץ וְאַחַת שֶׁל אֶבֶן, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If one leg was of wood and the other of stone it is clean.

phrases.he: הַנְּסָרִין שֶׁבַּמֶּרְחָץ שֶׁשִּׁגְּמָן, רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מְטַמֵּא וַחֲכָמִים מְטַהֲרִין, שֶׁאֵינָם עֲשׂוּיִן אֶלָּא שֶׁיִּהְיוּ הַמַּיִם מְהַלְּכִין תַּחְתֵּיהֶן.
phrases.en: Boards in a bath-house which were joined together: Rabbi Akiva says that they are susceptible to [midras] uncleanness; But the sages say that they are clean, since they are made only for the water to flow under them.

phrases.he: קַנְקֵילִין שֶׁיֶּשׁ בָּהּ בֵּית קַבָּלַת כְּסוּת, טְמֵאָה. וְהָעֲשׂוּיָה כְּכַוֶּרֶת, טְהוֹרָה
phrases.en: A fumigation-cage that contains a receptacle for garments is susceptible to uncleanness, But one that is made like a bee-hive is clean.

phrases.he: הַכַּדּוּר וְהָאִמּוּם וְהַקָּמֵעַ וְהַתְּפִלִּין שֶׁנִּקְרְעוּ, הַנּוֹגֵעַ בָּהֶן, טָמֵא. וּבְמַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכָן, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If a ball, a mould, an amulet or tefillin were torn, one that touches them becomes unclean, But one that touches what is inside them remains clean.

phrases.he: הָאֻכָּף שֶׁנִּקְרַע, הַנּוֹגֵעַ בְּמַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכוֹ, טָמֵא, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַתֶּפֶר מְחַבְּרוֹ
phrases.en: If a saddle was torn, one that touches its contents unclean, because the stitching joins them.

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ טְמֵאִין מִשּׁוּם מֶרְכָּב, זָרֵיז הָאַשְׁקְלוֹנִי, וּמְדוֹכָה הַמָּדִית, וְעָבִיט שֶׁל גָּמָל, וְטַפֵּיטָן שֶׁל סוּס.
phrases.en: The following are susceptible to uncleanness as objects that are fit for riding upon (merkav): an Ashkelon donkey belt, a Medean saddle, a camel's pillow, and a horse-cloth.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אַף טַפֵּיטָן שֶׁל סוּס טָמֵא מִשּׁוּם מוֹשָׁב, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁעוֹמְדִין עָלָיו בַּקֻּמְפּוֹן.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: a horse-cloth is susceptible to uncleanness as a seat, since people stand on it in the arena.

phrases.he: אֲבָל אֻכָּף שֶׁל נָאקָה, טָמֵא
phrases.en: But a saddle of a female camel is susceptible to [sitting] uncleanness.

phrases.he: מַה בֵּין מֶרְכָּב לְמוֹשָׁב.
phrases.en: What is the practical difference between [the uncleanness of an object used for] riding upon and [one used for] sitting upon? In the case of the former the effect of contact with it is different from the effect of carrying it, but in the case of the latter there is no difference between the effect of coming in contact with it or carrying it.

phrases.he: מֶרְכָּב חָלַק מַגָּעוֹ מִמַּשָּׂאוֹ, וּמוֹשָׁב לֹא חָלַק מַגָּעוֹ מִמַּשָּׂאוֹ.
phrases.en: The pack-frame of a donkey on which a zav sat is clean; But if the size of the spaces has been changed or if they have been broken one into another it is susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: תָּפִית שֶׁל חֲמוֹר שֶׁהוּא יוֹשֵׁב עָלֶיהָ, טָהוֹר.
שִׁנָּה בָהּ אֶת הַנְּקָבִין, אוֹ שֶׁפֵּרְצָן זֶה לְתוֹךְ זֶה, טְמֵאָה
הַמִּטָּה וְהַכַּר וְהַכֶּסֶת שֶׁל מֵת, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ טְמֵאִין מִדְרָס.
phrases.en: A bier, the mattress and the pillow of a corpse are susceptible to the uncleanness of midras.

phrases.he: כִּסֵּא שֶׁל כַּלָּה, וּמַשְׁבֵּר שֶׁל חַיָּה, וְכִסֵּא שֶׁל כּוֹבֵס שֶׁהוּא כוֹרֵם עָלָיו אֶת הַכֵּלִים,
phrases.en: A bride's stool, a midwife's stool, and a launderer's stool on which he piles the clothes: Rabbi Yose says: it is not regarded as a seat.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, אֵין בָּהֶם מִשּׁוּם מוֹשָׁב:
הַחֵרֶם, טָמֵא מִפְּנֵי הַזּוּטוֹ.
phrases.en: A fishing net is susceptible to uncleanness on account of its bag.

phrases.he: הָרְשָׁתוֹת, וְהַמִּכְמָרוֹת, וְהַמַּדָּף, וְהַפְּלָצוּר, וּמְצֻדּוֹת הַסְּכָרִין, טְמֵאִין.
phrases.en: Nets, snares, bird-traps, slings and fishermen's skeins are susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: וְהַאָקוֹן, וְהָרְטוֹב, וְהַכְּלוּב, טְהוֹרִין
phrases.en: A fish-trap, a bird-basket and a bird-cage are not susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: שְׁלֹשָׁה תְרִיסִין הֵם. תְּרִיס הַכָּפוּף, טָמֵא מִדְרָס.
phrases.en: There are three different types of shields:A bent shield is susceptible to midras uncleanness; A shield used in the arena is susceptible to corpse uncleanness; And the Arabian toy shield is pure from all uncleanness.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁמְּשַׂחֲקִין בּוֹ בַּקֻּנְפּוֹן, טָמֵא טְמֵא מֵת.
וְדִיצַת הָעַרְבִיִּין, טְהוֹרָה מִכְּלוּם
שָׁלֹשׁ עֲגָלוֹת הֵן. הָעֲשׂוּיָה כְקַתֶּדְרָא, טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס.
phrases.en: There are three different types of wagons:The one made like a cathedra is susceptible to midras uncleanness; The one made like a bed is susceptible to corpse uncleanness, And the one for [the transport of] stones is free from all uncleanness.

phrases.he: כְּמִטָּה, טְמֵאָה טְמֵא מֵת.
וְשֶׁל אֲבָנִים, טְהוֹרָה מִכְּלוּם
שָׁלֹשׁ עֲרֵבוֹת הֵן. עֲרֵבָה מִשְּׁנֵי לֹג וְעַד תִּשְׁעָה קַבִּין שֶׁנִּסְדְּקָה, טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס.
phrases.en: There are three different types of baking-troughs:If a baking-trough of a capacity from two log to nine kav was split it is susceptible to midras uncleanness; If it was whole it is susceptible to corpse uncleanness; And if it holds the prescribed measure it is free from all uncleanness.

phrases.he: שְׁלֵמָה, טְמֵאָה טְמֵא מֵת.
וְהַבָּאָה בַמִּדָּה, טְהוֹרָה מִכְּלוּם
שָׁלֹשׁ תֵּבוֹת הֵן. תֵּבָה שֶׁפִּתְחָהּ מִצִּדָּהּ, טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס.
phrases.en: There are three different types of boxes:A box whose opening is at the sides is susceptible to midras uncleanness; If it is on the top it is susceptible to corpse uncleanness; And if it holds the prescribed measure it is free from all uncleanness.

phrases.he: מִלְמַעְלָן, טְמֵאָה טְמֵא מֵת.
וְהַבָּאָה בַמִּדָּה, טְהוֹרָה מִכְּלוּם
שְׁלֹשָׁה תַרְבּוּסִין הֵן. שֶׁל סַפָּרִין, טָמֵא מִדְרָס.
phrases.en: There are three different types of leather covers:That of barbers is susceptible to midras uncleanness; That on which people eat is susceptible to corpse uncleanness.

phrases.he: שֶׁאוֹכְלִין עָלָיו, טָמֵא טְמֵא מֵת.
phrases.en: And that for [spreading out] olives is free from all uncleanness.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל זֵיתִים, טָהוֹר מִכְּלוּם
שָׁלֹשׁ בְּסָסִיּוֹת הֵן. שֶׁלִּפְנֵי הַמִּטָּה וְשֶׁלִּפְנֵי סוֹפְרִים, טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס.
phrases.en: There are three different types of bases:One which lies before a bed or before a scribe is susceptible to midras uncleanness; One for a side-table is susceptible to corpse uncleanness; And one for a cupboard is free from all uncleanness.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל דְּלֻפְקִי, טְמֵאָה טְמֵא מֵת.
וְשֶׁל מִגְדָּל, טְהוֹרָה מִכְּלוּם
שָׁלֹשׁ פִּנְקָסִיּוֹת הֵן. הָאֱפִיפוֹרִין, טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס.
phrases.en: There are three different types of writing tablets:That of papyrus is susceptible to midras uncleanness; That which had a receptacle for wax is susceptible to corpse uncleanness; And that which is smooth is free from all uncleanness.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁיֶּשׁ בָּהּ בֵּית קִבּוּל שַׁעֲוָה, טְמֵאָה טְמֵא מֵת. וַחֲלָקָה, טְהוֹרָה מִכְּלוּם
שָׁלֹשׁ מִטּוֹת הֵן. הָעֲשׂוּיָה לִשְׁכִיבָה, טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס.
phrases.en: There are three different types of beds:One that is used for lying upon is susceptible to midras uncleanness; One used by glass makers is susceptible to corpse uncleanness; And one used by weavers is free from all uncleanness.

phrases.he: שֶׁל זַגָּגִין, טְמֵאָה טְמֵא מֵת.
וְשֶׁל סָרָגִין, טְהוֹרָה מִכְּלוּם
שָׁלֹשׁ מַשְׁפֵּלוֹת הֵן. שֶׁל זֶבֶל, טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס.
phrases.en: There are three different types of baskets:The one for dung is susceptible to midras uncleanness; The one for straw is susceptible to corpse uncleanness; And a camel's rope bag is free from all uncleanness.

phrases.he: שֶׁל תֶּבֶן, טְמֵאָה טְמֵא מֵת.
וְהַפֻּחְלָץ שֶׁל גְּמַלִּים, טָהוֹר מִכְּלוּם
שְׁלֹשָׁה מַפָּצִים הֵן. הָעֲשׂוּיָה לִישִׁיבָה, טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס.
phrases.en: There are three different types of mats:One used for sitting upon is susceptible to midras uncleanness; One used by dyers is susceptible to corpse uncleanness.

phrases.he: שֶׁל צַבָּעִין, טָמֵא טְמֵא מֵת.
phrases.en: And one used in wine-presses is free from all uncleanness.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל גִּתּוֹת, טָהוֹר מִכְּלוּם
שָׁלֹשׁ חֲמָתוֹת וְשָׁלֹשׁ תּוּרְמְלִין הֵן.
phrases.en: There are three different types of water skins and three different types of shepherds' wallets:Those that can hold the prescribed quantity are susceptible to midras uncleanness; Those that cannot hold the prescribed quantity are susceptible to corpse uncleanness; And those made of fish skin are free from all uncleanness.

phrases.he: הַמְקַבְּלִים כַּשִּׁעוּר, טְמֵאִין מִדְרָס.
וְשֶׁאֵינָן מְקַבְּלִין כַּשִּׁעוּר, טְמֵאִים טְמֵא מֵת.
וְשֶׁל עוֹר הַדָּג, טָהוֹר מִכְּלוּם
שְׁלֹשָׁה עוֹרוֹת הֵן. הֶעָשׂוּי לְשָׁטִיחַ, טָמֵא מִדְרָס.
phrases.en: There are three different types of hides:That which is used as a rug is susceptible to midras uncleanness; That which is used as a wrapper for vessels is susceptible to corpse uncleanness; And that which is intended for straps and sandals is free from all uncleanness.

phrases.he: לְתַכְרִיךְ הַכֵּלִים, טָמֵא טְמֵא מֵת.
וְשֶׁל רְצוּעוֹת וְשֶׁל סַנְדָּלִים, טְהוֹרָה מִכְּלוּם
שְׁלֹשָׁה סְדִינִין הֵן. הֶעָשׂוּי לִשְׁכִיבָה, טָמֵא מִדְרָס.
phrases.en: There are three different types of sheets:One used for lying upon is susceptible to midras uncleanness; One used as a curtain is susceptible to corpse uncleanness; And one used as a mural decoration is free from all uncleanness.

phrases.he: לְוִילוֹן, טָמֵא טְמֵא מֵת.
וְשֶׁל צוּרוֹת, טָהוֹר מִכְּלוּם
שָׁלֹשׁ מִטְפָּחוֹת הֵן. שֶׁל יָדַיִם, טָמֵא מִדְרָס.
phrases.en: There are three different types of napkins:One used for hands is susceptible to midras uncleanness; One used for books is susceptible to corpse uncleanness; And the one used as a shroud or a covering for the harps of the Levites is free from all uncleanness.

phrases.he: שֶׁל סְפָרִין, טְמֵאָה טְמֵא מֵת, וְשֶׁל תַּכְרִיךְ וְשֶׁל נִבְלֵי בְנֵי לֵוִי, טְהוֹרָה מִכְּלוּם
שְׁלֹשָׁה פְרָקִילִינִין הֵן. שֶׁל צָדֵי חַיָּה וָעוֹף, טָמֵא מִדְרָס.
phrases.en: There are three different types of hip-boots:Those used by the hunters of animals and birds are susceptible to midras uncleanness; Those used by locust gatherers are susceptible to corpse uncleanness.

phrases.he: שֶׁל חֲגָבִין, טָמֵא טְמֵא מֵת.
phrases.en: And those used by fig-pickers are free from all uncleanness.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל קַיָּצִין, טָהוֹר מִכְּלוּם
שָׁלֹשׁ סְבָכוֹת הֵן. שֶׁל יַלְדָּה, טְמֵאָה טֻמְאַת מִדְרָס.
phrases.en: There are three different types of hair nets:A girl's is susceptible to midras uncleanness; An old woman's is susceptible to corpse uncleanness; And [the hair net] of a woman who "goes out" is free from all uncleanness.

phrases.he: שֶׁל זְקֵנָה, טְמֵאָה טְמֵא מֵת.
וְשֶׁל יוֹצֵאת לַחוּץ, טְהוֹרָה מִכְּלוּם
שָׁלֹשׁ קֻפּוֹת הֵן. מְהוּהָה שֶׁטְּלָיָהּ עַל הַבְּרִיָּה, הוֹלְכִין אַחַר הַבְּרִיָּה.
phrases.en: There are three different types of baskets: If a worn-out basket is patched on to a sound one, all is determined by the sound one; If a small basket is patched on to a large one all is determined by the large one; If they are equal all is determined by the inner one.

phrases.he: קְטַנָּה עַל הַגְּדוֹלָה, הוֹלְכִין אַחַר הַגְּדוֹלָה.
הָיוּ שָׁווֹת, הוֹלְכִין אַחַר הַפְּנִימִית.
רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, כַּף מֹאזְנַיִם שֶׁטְּלָיָהּ עַל שׁוּלֵי הַמֵּחַם, מִבִּפְנִים, טָמֵא. מִבַּחוּץ, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: if the cup of a balance was patched on to the bottom of a boiler on the inside, the latter becomes unclean; but if on the outside it remains clean.

phrases.he: טְלָיָהּ עַל צִדָּהּ, בֵּין מִבִּפְנִים בֵּין מִבַּחוּץ, טָהוֹר
phrases.en: If it was patched on to the side, whether on the inside or the outside, it remains clean.

phrases.he: כָּל הַכֵּלִים יֵשׁ לָהֶם אֲחוֹרַיִם וָתוֹךְ, כְּגוֹן הַכָּרִים וְהַכְּסָתוֹת וְהַשַּׂקִּין וְהַמַּרְצוּפִין, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.en: All vessels have [different laws] for outer and inner sides, as for instance, cushions, coverings, sacks and packing-bags, the words of Rabbi Judah.

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, כֹּל שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ תוֹבְרוֹת, יֶשׁ לוֹ אֲחוֹרַיִם וָתוֹךְ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir says: any vessel that has loops has [different laws] for inner and outer sides but one that has no loops does not have different laws for outer and inner sides.

phrases.he: וְכֹל שֶׁאֵין לוֹ תוֹבְרוֹת, אֵין לוֹ אֲחוֹרַיִם וָתוֹךְ.
