phrases.en: Bet Hillel say: when their contents have been increased [by more than their original quantity] even if they do not overflow.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, רַבּוּ אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא שָׁטְפוּ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: when they overflow although their contents have not been so increased.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, שָׁטְפוּ אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא רַבּוּ.
phrases.en: [These] are valid [for preparing dough] for hallah and for the washing of the hands.

phrases.he: כְּשֵׁרִין לַחַלָּה וְלִטֹּל מֵהֶן לַיָּדָיִם
לְמַעְלָה מֵהֶן, מֵי תַמְצִיּוֹת שֶׁלֹּא פָסְקוּ.
phrases.en: Superior to such [water] is the water of rain flows which have not stopped.

phrases.he: שָׁתָה טָמֵא וְשָׁתָה טָהוֹר, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If an unclean person drank of it and then a clean person drank of it, he is clean.

phrases.he: שָׁתָה טָמֵא וּמִלֵּא בִכְלִי טָהוֹר, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If an unclean person drank of it and water was then drawn from it in a clean vessel, it is clean.

phrases.he: שָׁתָה טָמֵא וְנָפַל כִּכָּר שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֵדִיחַ, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If an unclean person drank of it and a loaf of terumah fell in, even if he washed his hand in it, it is clean.

phrases.he: מִלֵּא בִכְלִי טָמֵא וְשָׁתָה טָהוֹר, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If one drew water from it in an unclean vessel and then a clean person drank [out of the pool], he is clean.

phrases.he: מִלֵּא בִכְלִי טָמֵא וּמִלֵּא בִכְלִי טָהוֹר, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If one drew water from it in an unclean vessel and a loaf of terumah fell [into the pool], even if he washed his hands in it, it is clean.

phrases.he: מִלֵּא בִכְלִי טָמֵא וְנָפַל כִּכָּר שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֵדִיחַ, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If unclean water fell into it and a clean person drank of it, he is clean.

phrases.he: נָפְלוּ מַיִם טְמֵאִים וְשָׁתָה טָהוֹר, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If unclean water fell into it and one drew water from it in a clean vessel, it is clean.

phrases.he: נָפְלוּ מַיִם טְמֵאִים וּמִלֵּא בִכְלִי טָהוֹר, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If unclean water fell into it and a loaf of terumah fell in, even if he washed his hands in it, it is clean.

phrases.he: נָפְלוּ מַיִם טְמֵאִים וְנָפַל כִּכָּר שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֵדִיחַ, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: [All such water] is valid for terumah and for the washing of the hands.

phrases.he: כְּשֵׁרִים לַתְּרוּמָה וְלִטֹּל מֵהֶם לַיָּדָיִם
לְמַעְלָה מֵהֶן, מִקְוֶה שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה, שֶׁבּוֹ טוֹבְלִין וּמַטְבִּילִין.
phrases.en: Superior to such [water] is [the water of] the mikveh containing forty seahs, for in it people may immerse themselves and immerse other [things].

phrases.he: לְמַעְלָה מֵהֶן, מַעְיָן שֶׁמֵּימָיו מֻעָטִין וְרַבּוּ עָלָיו מַיִם שְׁאוּבִין, שָׁוֶה לַמִּקְוֶה לְטַהֵר בְּאַשְׁבֹּרֶן, וְלַמַּעְיָן לְהַטְבִּיל בּוֹ בְּכָל שֶׁהוּא
phrases.en: Superior to such [water] is [the water of] a spring whose own water is little but has been increased by a greater quantity of drawn water. It is equivalent to the mikveh in as much as it may render clean by standing water, and to an [ordinary] spring in as much as one may immerse in it whatever the quantity of its contents.

phrases.he: לְמַעְלָה מֵהֶן, מַיִם מֻכִּין, שֶׁהֵן מְטַהֲרִין בְּזוֹחֲלִין.
phrases.en: Superior to them are "smitten waters" which can purify even when flowing [on the ground].

phrases.he: לְמַעְלָה מֵהֶן, מַיִם חַיִּים, שֶׁבָּהֶן טְבִילָה לַזָּבִים, וְהַזָּיָה לַמְצֹרָעִים, וּכְשֵׁרִים לְקַדֵּשׁ מֵהֶן מֵי חַטָּאת
phrases.en: Superior to them are "living waters" for in them there is immersion for zavim and sprinkling for metzoraim, and they are valid for the preparation of the hatat waters.

phrases.he: הַטָּמֵא שֶׁיָּרַד לִטְבֹּל, סָפֵק טָבַל סָפֵק לֹא טָבַל, אֲפִלּוּ טָבַל, סָפֵק יֶשׁ בּוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה סָפֵק אֵין בּוֹ.
phrases.en: An unclean man who went down to immerse himself: If it is doubtful whether he did immerse himself or not; And even if he did immerse himself, it is doubtful whether the mikveh contained forty seahs or not; And if there were two mikvehs, one containing forty seahs but the other not containing forty seahs, and he immersed himself in one of them but he does not know in which of them he immersed himself, In such a doubt he is unclean.

phrases.he: שְׁנֵי מִקְוָאוֹת, אֶחָד יֶשׁ בּוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה וְאֶחָד שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ, טָבַל בְּאַחַד מֵהֶם וְאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ בְּאֵיזֶה מֵהֶן טָבַל, סְפֵקוֹ טָמֵא
מִקְוֶה שֶׁנִּמְדַּד וְנִמְצָא חָסֵר, כָּל טָהֳרוֹת שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ עַל גַּבָּיו לְמַפְרֵעַ, בֵּין בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד בֵּין בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים, טְמֵאוֹת.
phrases.en: If a mikveh was measured and was found lacking [in its prescribed quantity], all things which had been purified in it, whether in private domain or in a public domain, are accounted unclean retroactively.

phrases.he: בַּמֶּה דְבָרִים אֲמוּרִים, בְּטֻמְאָה חֲמוּרָה.
phrases.en: To what does this rule apply? To a serious uncleanness.

phrases.he: אֲבָל בְּטֻמְאָה קַלָּה, כְּגוֹן אָכַל אֳכָלִים טְמֵאִים, וְשָׁתָה מַשְׁקִין טְמֵאִים, בָּא רֹאשׁוֹ וְרֻבּוֹ בְּמַיִם שְׁאוּבִים, אוֹ שֶׁנָּפְלוּ עַל רֹאשׁוֹ וְעַל רֻבּוֹ שְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין מַיִם שְׁאוּבִין, וְיָרַד לִטְבֹּל, סָפֵק טָבַל סָפֵק לֹא טָבַל, אֲפִלּוּ טָבַל, סָפֵק יֶשׁ בּוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה סָפֵק אֵין בּוֹ.
phrases.en: But in the case of a lesser uncleanness, for instance if he ate unclean foods or drank unclean liquids, or if his head and the greater part of his body entered into drawn water, or if three logs of drawn water fell on his head and the greater part of his body, and he then went down to immerse himself and he is in doubt whether he immersed himself or not, or even if he did immerse himself there is [still] a doubt whether the mikveh contained forty seahs or not, or if there were two mikvehs, one containing forty seahs and not the other, and he immersed himself in one of them but does not know in which of them he immersed himself, in such a doubt he is accounted clean.

phrases.he: שְׁנֵי מִקְוָאוֹת, אֶחָד יֶשׁ בּוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה, וְאֶחָד שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ, טָבַל בְּאַחַד מֵהֶן וְאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ בְּאֵיזֶה מֵהֶן טָבַל, סְפֵקוֹ טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose considers him unclean, for Rabbi Yose says: anything which is presumed to be unclean always remains in a condition of unfitness until it is known that it has become clean; but if there is a doubt whether a person became unclean or caused uncleanness, it is to be accounted clean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מְטַמֵּא, שֶׁרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, כָּל דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא בְחֶזְקַת טֻמְאָה, לְעוֹלָם הוּא בִפְסוּלוֹ, עַד שֶׁיִּוָּדַע שֶׁטָּהַר.
אֲבָל סְפֵקוֹ לִטָּמֵא וּלְטַמֵּא, טָהוֹר

סְפֵק מַיִם שְׁאוּבִין שֶׁטִּהֲרוּ חֲכָמִים, סָפֵק נָפְלוּ, סָפֵק לֹא נָפְלוּ, אֲפִלּוּ נָפְלוּ, סָפֵק יֶשׁ בָּהֶם אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה סָפֵק אֵין בָּהֶם, שְׁנֵי מִקְוָאוֹת, אֶחָד יֶשׁ בּוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה וְאֶחָד אֵין בּוֹ, נָפַל לְאַחַד מֵהֶן וְאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ לְאֵיזֶה מֵהֶן נָפַל, סְפֵקוֹ טָהוֹר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ בַמֶּה יִתְלֶה.
phrases.en: The case of a doubt about drawn water which the sages have declared clean;If there is a doubt whether [three logs of drawn water] fell into the mikveh or not, Or even if they did fall in, there is a doubt whether [the mikveh] contained forty seahs or not, Or if there were two mikvehs one of which contained forty seahs and the other did not, and drawn water fell into one of them and it is not known into which of them it fell, In such a doubt it is accounted clean, because there exists [a possibility] on which we may depend [in declaring it clean].

phrases.he: הָיוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם פְּחוּתִים מֵאַרְבָּעִים סְאָה, וְנָפַל לְאַחַד מֵהֶם וְאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ לְאֵיזֶה מֵהֶן נָפַל, סְפֵקוֹ טָמֵא, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ בַמֶּה יִתְלֶה
phrases.en: If they both contained less than forty seahs, and [drawn water] fell into one of them and it is not known into which of them it fell, in such a doubt it is accounted unclean, because there exists no [possibility] on which we may depend [in declaring it clean].

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, רְבִיעִית מַיִם שְׁאוּבִין בַּתְּחִלָּה, פּוֹסְלִין אֶת הַמִּקְוֶה, וּשְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין עַל פְּנֵי הַמַּיִם.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: a quarter-log of drawn water in the beginning makes the mikveh invalid, and three logs on the surface of the water.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, בֵּין בַּתְּחִלָּה בֵּין בַּסּוֹף, שִׁעוּרוֹ שְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין:
phrases.en: But the sages say: both in the beginning and at the end, the measure [which makes the mikveh invalid] is three logs.

phrases.he: מִקְוֶה שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ שָׁלשׁ גֻּמּוֹת שֶׁל מַיִם שְׁאוּבִין שֶׁל לֹג לֹג, אִם יָדוּעַ שֶׁנָּפַל לְתוֹכוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאִין מַיִם כְּשֵׁרִין עַד שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעוּ לַגֻּמָּא הַשְּׁלִישִׁית, כָּשֵׁר. וְאִם לָאו, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: If there were three cavities in a mikveh each holding a log of drawn water, if it is known that forty seahs of valid water fell in before reaching the third cavity, [such a mikveh is] valid; otherwise it is invalid.

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַכְשִׁיר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא כְמִקְוֶה סָמוּךְ לְמִקְוֶה
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon declares it valid, since it resembles a mikveh adjoining another mikveh.

phrases.he: הַמְסַנֵּק אֶת הַטִּיט לַצְּדָדִין וּמָשְׁכוּ מִמֶּנּוּ שְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין, כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.en: If one scraped mud to the sides and then three logs [of water] were drawn out from it [from the mud], [the mikveh is still] valid.

phrases.he: הָיָה תוֹלֵשׁ וּמָשְׁכוּ מִמֶּנּוּ שְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: But if removed the mud away and three logs were drawn from it [into the mikveh] it becomes invalid.

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַכְשִׁיר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא נִתְכַּוֵּן לִשְׁאֹב
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon pronounces it valid, since there was no intention to draw [the water].

phrases.he: הַמַּנִּיחַ קַנְקַנִּים בְּרֹאשׁ הַגַּג לְנַגְּבָן וְנִתְמַלְּאוּ מַיִם,
phrases.en: If one had left wine-jars on the roof to dry and they became filled with water: Rabbi Eliezer says: if it was the season of rain and there was [in the cistern] a little water, one may break the jars; otherwise one may not break them.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אִם עוֹנַת גְּשָׁמִים הִיא, אִם יֶשׁ בּוֹ כִמְעַט מַיִם בַּבּוֹר, יְשַׁבֵּר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Joshua says: in either case one may break them or tilt them over, but one may not empty [them into the cistern].

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו, לֹא יְשַׁבֵּר.
רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ יְשַׁבֵּר, אוֹ יִכְפֶּה, אֲבָל לֹא יְעָרֶה:
הַסַּיָּד שֶׁשָּׁכַח עָצִיץ בַּבּוֹר וְנִתְמַלֵּא מַיִם, אִם הָיוּ הַמַּיִם צָפִים עַל גַּבָּיו כָּל שֶׁהוּא, יְשַׁבֵּר.
phrases.en: A plasterer forgot his lime-tub in a cistern and it became filled with water: if water flowed above it a little, it may be broken; and if not, it may not be broken, the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו, לֹא יְשַׁבֵּר, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר.
וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ יְשַׁבֵּר:
phrases.en: But Rabbi Joshua says: in either case it may be broken.

phrases.he: הַמְסַדֵּר קַנְקַנִּים בְּתוֹךְ הַבּוֹר וְנִתְמַלְּאוּ מַיִם, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁבָּלַע הַבּוֹר אֶת מֵימָיו, הֲרֵי זֶה יְשַׁבֵּר:
phrases.en: If one had arranged wine-jars in a cistern and they became filled with water, even though the water of the cistern was all soaked up, they may be broken.

phrases.he: מִקְוֶה שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה מַיִם וָטִיט,
phrases.en: A mikveh which contains forty seahs of water and mud [combined]: Rabbi Eliezer says: one may immerse objects in the water but one may not immerse them in the mud.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, מַטְבִּילִין בַּמַּיִם וְאֵין מַטְבִּילִין בַּטִּיט.
phrases.en: But Rabbi Joshua says: in the water and also in the mud.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, בַּמַּיִם וּבַטִּיט. בְּאֵיזֶה טִיט מַטְבִּילִין.
phrases.en: In what kind of mud may objects be immersed? Mud over which water floats.

phrases.he: בְּטִיט שֶׁהַמַּיִם צָפִים עַל גַּבָּיו.
phrases.en: If the water was on one side only, Rabbi Joshua agrees that objects may be immersed in the water but may not be immersed in the mud.

phrases.he: הָיוּ הַמַּיִם מִצַּד אֶחָד, מוֹדֶה רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ שֶׁמַּטְבִּילִין בַּמַּיִם וְאֵין מַטְבִּילִין בַּטִּיט. בְּאֵיזֶה טִיט אָמְרוּ.
phrases.en: Of what kind of mud have they spoken? Mud into which a reed will sink of itself, the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: בְּטִיט שֶׁהַקָּנֶה יוֹרֵד מֵאֵלָיו, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, מְקוֹם שֶׁאֵין קְנֵה הַמִּדָּה עוֹמֵד.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: [mud] in which a measuring-rod will not stand upright.

phrases.he: אַבָּא אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן דּוֹלְעַאי אוֹמֵר, מְקוֹם שֶׁהַמִּשְׁקֹלֶת יוֹרֶדֶת.
phrases.en: Abba Elazar ben Dulai says: [mud] into which a plummet will sink.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, הַיּוֹרֵד בְּפִי חָבִית.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: such as will go down into the mouth of a jar.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, הַנִּכְנָס בִּשְׁפוֹפֶרֶת הַנּוֹד.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: such as will enter into the tube of a water- skin.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר, הַנִּמְדָּד בַּלֹּג
phrases.en: Rabbi Elazar bar Zadok says: such as can be measured in a log measure.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, שְׁנֵי מִקְוָאוֹת שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה, וְנָפְלוּ לָזֶה לֹג וּמֶחֱצָה וְלָזֶה לֹג וּמֶחֱצָה וְנִתְעָרְבוּ, כְּשֵׁרִים, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא נִקְרָא עֲלֵיהֶן שֵׁם פְּסוּל.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: two mikvehs neither of which contains forty seahs and a log and a half [of drawn water] fell into this one and a log and a half into this one, and then they are mixed together, they remain valid, since they had never been called as invalid.

phrases.he: אֲבָל מִקְוֶה שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה וְנָפְלוּ בוֹ שְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין וְנֶחֱלַק לִשְׁנַיִם, פָּסוּל, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנִּקְרָא עָלָיו שֵׁם פְּסוּל.
phrases.en: But if there is a mikveh holding less than forty seahs, and three logs [of drawn water] fell into it, and it was then divided into two, it is invalid, since it had already been called invalid.

phrases.he: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ מַכְשִׁיר, שֶׁהָיָה
רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, כָּל מִקְוֶה שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה וְנָפְלוּ לוֹ שְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין וְחָסַר אֲפִלּוּ קֹרְטוֹב, כָּשֵׁר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁחָסְרוּ לוֹ שְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין.
phrases.en: Rabbi Joshua declares it valid, for Rabbi Joshua used to say: any mikveh containing less than forty seahs into which three logs [of drawn water] fell and from which a kortov was withdrawn becomes valid, since the three logs have also been diminished.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, לְעוֹלָם הוּא בִפְסוּלוֹ, עַד שֶׁיֵּצֵא מִמֶּנּוּ מְלוֹאוֹ וָעוֹד:
phrases.en: But the sages say: it always remains invalid until the amount of its former contents and a little more are removed.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד. הַבּוֹר שֶׁבְּחָצֵר וְנָפְלוּ לוֹ שְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין, לְעוֹלָם הוּא בִפְסוּלוֹ, עַד שֶׁיֵּצֵא מִמֶּנּוּ מְלוֹאוֹ וָעוֹד, אוֹ עַד שֶׁיַּעֲמִיד בֶּחָצֵר אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה וְיִטְהֲרוּ הָעֶלְיוֹנִים מִן הַתַּחְתּוֹנִים.
phrases.en: How so? If there was a cistern in a courtyard and three logs [of drawn water] fell into it, it will always remain invalid until the whole of it is removed and a little more, or until [another mikveh containing] forty se'ahs is placed in the courtyard, so that the higher mikveh is rendered valid by the lower.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה פּוֹסֵל, אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן פָּקָק
phrases.en: Rabbi Elazer ben Azariah declares it invalid unless the [new mikveh] is stopped up.

phrases.he: בּוֹר שֶׁהוּא מָלֵא מַיִם שְׁאוּבִין וְהָאַמָּה נִכְנֶסֶת לוֹ וְיוֹצְאָה מִמֶּנּוּ, לְעוֹלָם הוּא בִפְסוּלוֹ, עַד שֶׁיִּתְחַשֵּׁב שֶׁלֹּא נִשְׁתַּיֵּר מִן הָרִאשׁוֹנִים שְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין.
phrases.en: If a cistern is full of drawn water and a channel leads into it and out of it, it continues to be invalid until it can be reckoned that there does not remain in it three logs of the former [water].

phrases.he: שְׁנַיִם שֶׁהָיוּ מַטִּילִין לַמִּקְוֶה, זֶה לֹג וּמֶחֱצָה וָזֶה לֹג וּמֶחֱצָה, הַסּוֹחֵט אֶת כְּסוּתוֹ וּמַטִּיל מִמְּקוֹמוֹת הַרְבֵּה, וְהַמְּעָרֶה מִן הַצַּרְצוּר וּמַטִּיל מִמְּקוֹמוֹת הַרְבֵּה, רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מַכְשִׁיר, וַחֲכָמִים פּוֹסְלִין.
phrases.en: If two men each poured a log and a half [of drawn water] into a mikveh, or if one wrung out his clothes and so poured in [water] from several places, or if one emptied out a water-jug and so poured in [water]from several places, Rabbi Akiva declares it valid, But the sages declare it invalid.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, לֹא אָמְרוּ מַטִּילִין, אֶלָּא מַטִּיל.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva said: they did not say "if they poured in," rather "if one poured in.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ, לֹא כָךְ וְלֹא כָךְ אָמְרוּ, אֶלָּא שֶׁנָּפְלוּ לוֹ שְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין:
phrases.en: But they said: they said neither thus nor thus, but rather "if there fell in three logs [of drawn water]."

phrases.he: מִכְּלִי אֶחָד, מִשְּׁנַיִם וּמִשְּׁלשָׁה, מִצְטָרְפִין. וּמֵאַרְבָּעָה, אֵין מִצְטָרְפִין.
phrases.en: [If the three logs of drawn water fell in] from one vessel or from two or from three, they combine together; but if from four, they do not combine together.

phrases.he: בַּעַל קֶרִי הַחוֹלֶה שֶׁנָּפְלוּ עָלָיו תִּשְׁעָה קַבִּין מַיִם, וְטָהוֹר שֶׁנָּפְלוּ עַל רֹאשׁוֹ וְעַל רֻבּוֹ שְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין מַיִם שְׁאוּבִין, מִכְּלִי אֶחָד, מִשְּׁנַיִם וּמִשְּׁלשָׁה, מִצְטָרְפִין. מֵאַרְבָּעָה, אֵין מִצְטָרְפִין. בַּמֶּה דְבָרִים אֲמוּרִים.
phrases.en: If a man who had a seminal issue was sick and nine kavs of water fell on him, or if there fell on the head and the greater part of the body of a clean person three logs of drawn water from one vessel or from two or from three, they combine together; but if from four, they do not combine together.

phrases.he: בִּזְמַן שֶׁהִתְחִיל הַשֵּׁנִי עַד שֶׁלֹּא פָסַק הָרִאשׁוֹן. וּבַמֶּה דְבָרִים אֲמוּרִים.
phrases.en: In what case does this apply? When the second began before the first finished. And in what case does [the other statement] apply? When there was no intention to increase it.

phrases.he: בִּזְמַן שֶׁלֹּא נִתְכַּוֵּן לְרַבּוֹת.
phrases.en: But if there was an intention to increase it, if only a kortov in a whole year, they combine together to add up to the three logs.

phrases.he: אֲבָל נִתְכַּוֵּן לְרַבּוֹת, אֲפִלּוּ קֹרְטוֹב בְּכָל הַשָּׁנָה, מִצְטָרְפִין לִשְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין
הַמַּנִּיחַ כֵּלִים תַּחַת הַצִּנּוֹר, אֶחָד כֵּלִים גְּדוֹלִים וְאֶחָד כֵּלִים קְטַנִּים, אֲפִלּוּ כְלֵי גְלָלִים, כְּלֵי אֲבָנִים, כְּלֵי אֲדָמָה, פּוֹסְלִין אֶת הַמִּקְוֶה.
phrases.en: If one put vessels under a water-spout, whether they be large vessels or small vessels or even vessels of dung, vessels of stone or earthen vessels, they make the mikveh invalid.

phrases.he: אֶחָד הַמַּנִּיחַ וְאֶחָד הַשּׁוֹכֵחַ, כְּדִבְרֵי בֵית שַׁמַּאי.
phrases.en: It is all alike whether they were put there [purposely] or were [merely] forgotten, the words of Bet Shammai.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל מְטַהֲרִין בְּשׁוֹכֵחַ.
phrases.en: But Bet Hillel declare it clean in the case of one who forgets.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר, נִמְנוּ וְרַבּוּ בֵית שַׁמַּאי עַל בֵּית הִלֵּל.
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir said: they voted and Bet Shammai had a majority over Bet Hillel.

phrases.he: וּמוֹדִים בְּשׁוֹכֵחַ בֶּחָצֵר שֶׁהוּא טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: Yet they agree in the case of one who forgets [and leaves vessels] in a courtyard that the mikveh remains clean.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, עֲדַיִין מַחֲלֹקֶת בִּמְקוֹמָהּ עוֹמָדֶת:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose said: the controversy still remains as it was.

phrases.he: הַמַּנִּיחַ טַבְלָא תַּחַת הַצִּנּוֹר, אִם יֶשׁ לָהּ לְבִזְבֵּז, פּוֹסֶלֶת אֶת הַמִּקְוֶה.
phrases.en: One who put a board under a water-spout: if it had a rim to it, it disqualifies the mikveh; otherwise it does not disqualify the mikveh.

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו, אֵינָהּ פּוֹסֶלֶת אֶת הַמִּקְוֶה.
phrases.en: If he made it stand upright to be rinsed, in neither case does it disqualify the mikveh.

phrases.he: זְקָפָהּ לִדּוֹחַ, בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ אֵינָהּ פּוֹסֶלֶת אֶת הַמִּקְוֶה
הַחוֹטֵט בְּצִנּוֹר לְקַבֵּל צְרוֹרוֹת, בְּשֶׁל עֵץ, כָּל שֶׁהוּא. וּבְשֶׁל חֶרֶס, רְבִיעִית.
phrases.en: If one makes a hollow in a water-spout to collect pebbles, its water disqualifies the mikveh; In the case of a wooden [spout] if it holds even a little, But in the case of an earthenware [spout] if it will hold a quarter-log.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אַף בְּשֶׁל חֶרֶס, כָּל שֶׁהוּא.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: also in the case of an earthenware [spout] if it holds even a little: they have spoken of "a quarter-log" only in the case of broken sherds of an earthenware utensil.

phrases.he: לֹא אָמְרוּ רְבִיעִית אֶלָּא בְשִׁבְרֵי כְלֵי חֶרֶס.
phrases.en: If the pieces of gravel moved about inside [the hollow], it disqualifies the mikveh.

phrases.he: הָיוּ צְרוֹרוֹת מִתְחַלְחֲלִים בְּתוֹכוֹ, פּוֹסְלִים אֶת הַמִּקְוֶה.
phrases.en: If dirt went down into it and was pressed down, [the mikveh continues to be] valid.

phrases.he: יָרַד לְתוֹכוֹ עָפָר וְנִכְבַּשׁ, כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.en: If the spout was narrow at each end and wide in the middle, it does not disqualify [the mikveh] invalid, because it had not been made to gather anything in it.

phrases.he: סִלּוֹן שֶׁהוּא צַר מִכָּאן וּמִכָּאן וְרָחָב מִן הָאֶמְצַע, אֵינוֹ פוֹסֵל, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא נַעֲשָׂה לְקַבָּלָה
מַיִם שְׁאוּבִין וּמֵי גְשָׁמִים שֶׁנִּתְעָרְבוּ בֶחָצֵר, וּבָעֻקָּה, וְעַל מַעֲלוֹת הַמְּעָרָה, אִם רֹב מִן הַכָּשֵׁר, כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.en: Drawn water and rain water which were mixed together in a courtyard or in a cavity or on the steps of a cave: If the greater part was valid, the whole is valid; And if the greater part is invalid, the whole is invalid.

phrases.he: וְאִם רֹב מִן הַפָּסוּל, פָּסוּל. מֶחֱצָה לְמֶחֱצָה, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: If they were equal in quantity, the whole is invalid.

phrases.he: אֵימָתַי, בִּזְמַן שֶׁמִּתְעָרְבִין עַד שֶׁלֹּא יַגִּיעוּ לַמִּקְוֶה.
phrases.en: When [does this apply]? When they were mingled together before they arrived at the mikveh.

phrases.he: הָיוּ מְקַלְּחִין בְּתוֹךְ הַמַּיִם, אִם יָדוּעַ שֶׁנָּפַל לְתוֹכוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה מַיִם כְּשֵׁרִים, עַד שֶׁלֹּא יָרַד לְתוֹכוֹ שְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין מַיִם שְׁאוּבִין, כָּשֵׁר. וְאִם לָאו, פָּסוּל
phrases.en: If [the drawn water] flowed into the [rain] water: it was known that there fell in forty seahs of valid water before there came in three logs of drawn water, [the mikveh is] valid; otherwise it is invalid.

phrases.he: הַשֹּׁקֶת שֶׁבַּסֶּלַע, אֵין מְמַלְּאִין מִמֶּנָּה, וְאֵין מְקַדְּשִׁין בָּהּ, וְאֵין מַזִּין מִמֶּנָּה, וְאֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה צָמִיד פָּתִיל, וְאֵינָהּ פּוֹסֶלֶת אֶת הַמִּקְוֶה.
phrases.en: In the case of a trough in a rock: One may not fill up [the hatat waters] from it, nor may the [hatat waters] be consecrated in it, nor may one sprinkle from it. And it does not require a tightly stopped-up covering, And it does not invalidate the mikveh.

phrases.he: הָיְתָה כְלִי וְחִבְּרָהּ בְּסִיד, מְמַלְּאִין בָּהּ, וּמְקַדְּשִׁין בָּהּ, וּמַזִּין מִמֶּנָּה, וּצְרִיכָה צָמִיד פָּתִיל, וּפוֹסֶלֶת אֶת הַמִּקְוֶה.
phrases.en: If it was a vessel and had been joined to the ground with lime: One may fill up the hatat waters from it and the hatat waters may be consecrated in it, and one may sprinkle from it, And it requires a tightly stopped-up covering; And it invalidates the mikveh invalid.

phrases.he: נִקְּבָה מִלְּמַטָּה אוֹ מִן הַצַּד וְאֵינָהּ יְכוֹלָה לְקַבֵּל מַיִם כָּל שֶׁהֵם, כְּשֵׁרָה. וְכַמָּה יִהְיֶה בַנֶּקֶב. כִּשְׁפוֹפֶרֶת הַנּוֹד.
phrases.en: If a hole was made in it below or at the side so that it could not contain water in however small a quantity, it is valid.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא,
phrases.en: And how large must the hole be? Like the tube of a water-skin.

phrases.he: מַעֲשֶׂה בְשֹׁקֶת יֵהוּא שֶׁהָיְתָה בִירוּשָׁלַיִם, וְהָיְתָה נְקוּבָה כִשְׁפוֹפֶרֶת הַנּוֹד, וְהָיוּ כָל הַטָּהֳרוֹת שֶׁבִּירוּשָׁלַיִם נַעֲשׂוֹת עַל גַּבָּהּ, וְשָׁלְחוּ בֵית שַׁמַּאי וּפְחָתוּהָ, שֶׁבֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, עַד שֶׁיִּפְחֲתוּ רֻבָּהּ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehudah ben Batera said: it happened in the case of the trough of Yehu in Jerusalem that there was a hole in it like the tube of a water-skin, all the pure things in Jerusalem were made using it. But Bet Shammai sent and broke it down, for Bet Shammai say: [it remains a vessel] unless the greater part of it is broken down.

phrases.he: מַעְיָן שֶׁהֶעֱבִירוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי הַשֹּׁקֶת, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: [Water from] a spring which is made to pass over into a trough becomes invalid.

phrases.he: הֶעֱבִירוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי שָׂפָה כָל שֶׁהוּא, כָּשֵׁר חוּצָה לָהּ, שֶׁהַמַּעְיָן מְטַהֵר בְּכָל שֶׁהוּא.
phrases.en: If it was made to pass over the edge in any quantity, [what is] outside [the trough] is valid, for [the water of] a spring purifies however little its quantity.

phrases.he: הֶעֱבִירוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי בְרֵכָה וְהִפְסִיקוֹ, הֲרֵי הוּא כְמִקְוֶה.
phrases.en: If it is made to pass over into a pool and then is stopped, the pool counts as a mikveh.

phrases.he: חָזַר וְהִמְשִׁיכוֹ, פָּסוּל לַזָּבִים וְלַמְצֹרָעִים וּלְקַדֵּשׁ מֵהֶן מֵי חַטָּאת, עַד שֶׁיֵּדַע שֶׁיָּצְאוּ הָרִאשׁוֹנִים
phrases.en: If it is made to flow again, it is invalid for zavim and for those with skin disease and for the preparation of the hatat waters until it is known that the former [water] is gone.

phrases.he: הֶעֱבִירוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי כֵלִים אוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי סַפְסָל,
phrases.en: If it was made to pass over the outside of vessels or over a bench: Rabbi Judah says: behold it remains as it was before.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, הֲרֵי הוּא כְמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: behold it is like a mikveh, except that one may not immerse anything above the bench.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, הֲרֵי הוּא כְמִקְוֶה, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יַטְבִּיל עַל גַּבֵּי הַסַּפְסָל:
מַעְיָן שֶׁהוּא מָשׁוּךְ כְּנָדָל, רִבָּה עָלָיו וְהִמְשִׁיכוֹ, הֲרֵי הוּא כְמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה.
phrases.en: If [water from] a spring that flows into many channels was increased in quantity so that it was made to flow in abundance, it remains as it was before.

phrases.he: הָיָה עוֹמֵד וְרִבָּה עָלָיו וְהִמְשִׁיכוֹ, שָׁוֶה לְמִקְוֶה לְטַהֵר בְּאַשְׁבֹּרֶן, וּלְמַעְיָן לְהַטְבִּיל בּוֹ בְּכָל שֶׁהוּא
phrases.en: If it was standing and its quantity was increased so that it was made to flow, it becomes equal to a mikveh in that it can purify in standing water, and to a spring in that one may immerse [objects] therein however small its quantity.

phrases.he: כָּל הַיַּמִּים כְּמִקְוֶה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (בראשית א), וּלְמִקְוֵה הַמַּיִם קָרָא יַמִּים, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.en: All seas are equivalent to a mikveh, for it is said, "And the gathering (ulemikveh) of the waters He called the seas" (Genesis 1:10), the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, הַיָּם הַגָּדוֹל כְּמִקְוֶה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: only the Great Sea is equivalent to a mikveh, for it says "seas" only because there are in it many kinds of seas.

phrases.he: לֹא נֶאֱמַר יַמִּים, אֶלָּא שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ מִינֵי יַמִּים הַרְבֵּה.
רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, כָּל הַיַּמִּים מְטַהֲרִים בְּזוֹחֲלִין, וּפְסוּלִין לַזָּבִין וְלַמְצֹרָעִים, וּלְקַדֵּשׁ מֵהֶם מֵי חַטָּאת:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: all seas afford cleanness when running, and yet they are unfit for zavim and metzoraim and for the preparation of the hatat waters.

phrases.he: הַזּוֹחֲלִין, כְּמַעְיָן. וְהַנּוֹטְפִים, כְּמִקְוֶה.
phrases.en: Flowing water is considered like a spring and dripping water is considered like a mikveh.

phrases.he: הֵעִיד רַבִּי צָדוֹק עַל הַזּוֹחֲלִין שֶׁרַבּוּ עַל הַנּוֹטְפִים, שֶׁהֵם כְּשֵׁרִים.
phrases.en: Rabbi Zadok testified that if flowing water exceeded dripping water [with which it was mixed] it was valid [as flowing water].

phrases.he: וְנוֹטְפִים שֶׁעֲשָׂאָן זוֹחֲלִין, סוֹמֵךְ אֲפִלּוּ מַקֵּל, אֲפִלּוּ קָנֶה, אֲפִלּוּ זָב וְזָבָה, יוֹרֵד וְטוֹבֵל, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.en: If dripping water became flowing water, its flow may be blocked by a stick or by a reed or even by a zav or a zavah, and then one may go down and immerse oneself in it, the words of Rabbi Judah.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, כָּל דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא מְקַבֵּל טֻמְאָה, אֵין מַזְחִילִין בּוֹ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: one may not stop the flow of water with anything which is liable to uncleanness.

phrases.he: גַּל שֶׁנִּתְלַשׁ וּבוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה, וְנָפַל עַל הָאָדָם וְעַל הַכֵּלִים, טְהוֹרִים.
phrases.en: If a wave was separated [from the sea] and was forty seahs, and it fell on a man or on vessels, they become clean.

phrases.he: כָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה, טוֹבְלִין וּמַטְבִּילִין.
phrases.en: Any place containing forty seahs is valid for immersing oneself and for immersing other things.

phrases.he: מַטְבִּילִין בַּחֲרִיצִין וּבִנְעָצִים וּבְפַרְסַת הַחֲמוֹר הַמְעֹרֶבֶת בַּבִּקְעָה.
phrases.en: One may immerse in trenches or in ditches or even in a donkey-track whose water is connected in a valley.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, מַטְבִּילִין בְּחַרְדָּלִית.
phrases.en: Bet Shammai say: one may immerse in a rain torrent. But Bet Hillel say: one may not immerse.

phrases.he: בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, אֵין מַטְבִּילִין.
phrases.en: They agree that one may block its flow with vessels and immerse oneself in it, but the vessels with which the flow is blocked are not thereby [validly] immersed.

phrases.he: וּמוֹדִים שֶׁהוּא גוֹדֵר כֵּלִים וְטוֹבֵל בָּהֶם.
וְכֵלִים שֶׁגָּדַר בָּהֶם, לֹא הֻטְבְּלוּ
כָּל הַמְעֹרָב לַמִּקְוֶה, כַּמִּקְוֶה.
phrases.en: Anything which is joined with [the water of] a mikveh is like a mikveh.

phrases.he: חוֹרֵי הַמְּעָרָה וְסִדְקֵי הַמְּעָרָה, מַטְבִּיל בָּהֶם כְּמָה שֶׁהֵם.
phrases.en: One may immerse in holes of a cavern and in crevices of a cavern just as they are.

phrases.he: עֻקַּת הַמְּעָרָה, אֵין מַטְבִּילִין בָּהּ אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הָיְתָה נְקוּבָה כִשְׁפוֹפֶרֶת הַנּוֹד.
phrases.en: The pit of a cavern, one may not immerse in it unless it had a hole as big as the tube of a water-skin.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, אֵימָתַי, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהִיא מַעֲמֶדֶת עַצְמָהּ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah said: when [is this the case]? When it stands by itself; but if it does not stand by itself, one may immerse in it just as it is.

phrases.he: אֲבָל אִם אֵינָהּ מַעֲמֶדֶת עַצְמָהּ, מַטְבִּילִין בָּהּ כְּמָה שֶׁהִיא
דְּלִי שֶׁהוּא מָלֵא כֵלִים וְהִטְבִּילָן, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ טְהוֹרִים.
phrases.en: If a bucket was full of utensils and they were immersed, they become clean; But if [the bucket] was not immersed, the water in the bucket is not considered as joined [with the water of the mikveh] unless it be joined [by means of a hole in the bucket which is as big] as the tube of a water-skin.

phrases.he: וְאִם לֹא טָבַל, אֵין הַמַּיִם מְעֹרָבִין, עַד שֶׁיִּהְיוּ מְעֹרָבִין כִּשְׁפוֹפֶרֶת הַנּוֹד

שְׁלשָׁה מִקְוָאוֹת, בָּזֶה עֶשְׂרִים סְאָה, וּבָזֶה עֶשְׂרִים סְאָה, וּבָזֶה עֶשְׂרִים סְאָה מַיִם שְׁאוּבִין, וְהַשָּׁאוּב מִן הַצַּד, וְיָרְדוּ שְׁלשָׁה וְטָבְלוּ בָהֶן וְנִתְעָרְבוּ, הַמִּקְוָאוֹת טְהוֹרִין וְהַטּוֹבְלִים טְהוֹרִים.
phrases.en: Three mikvehs, two of which held twenty seahs [of valid water] and the third held twenty seahs of drawn water, and that holding drawn water was at the side: If three persons went down and immersed themselves in them and [the water of the three mikvehs] joined, the mikvehs are clean and they that immersed themselves become clean.

phrases.he: הָיָה הַשָּׁאוּב בָּאֶמְצַע, וְיָרְדוּ שְׁלשָׁה וְטָבְלוּ בָהֶם וְנִתְעָרְבוּ, הַמִּקְוָאוֹת כְּמוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ, וְהַטּוֹבְלִים כְּמוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ
phrases.en: If the one holding the drawn water was in the middle and three persons went down and immersed themselves in them and [the water of the three mikvehs] joined, the mikvehs continue as they were before and they that immersed themselves are as they were before.

phrases.he: הַסְּפוֹג וְהַדְּלִי שֶׁהָיוּ בָהֶן שְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין מַיִם וְנָפְלוּ לַמִּקְוֶה, לֹא פְסָלוּהוּ, שֶׁלֹּא אָמְרוּ אֶלָּא שְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין שֶׁנָּפְלוּ:
phrases.en: If a sponge or a bucket containing three logs of water fell into a mikveh, they do not make it invalid, because they have only said: "if three logs fell in."

phrases.he: הַשִּׁדָּה וְהַתֵּבָה שֶׁבַּיָּם, אֵין מַטְבִּילִין בָּהֶם, אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הָיוּ נְקוּבִין כִּשְׁפוֹפֶרֶת הַנּוֹד.
phrases.en: A chest or a box which is in the sea: one may not immerse in them unless they have a hole as large as the tube of a water-skin.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, בִּכְלִי גָדוֹל, אַרְבָּעָה טְפָחִים. וּבְקָטָן, רֻבּוֹ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: in the case of a large vessel [the hole should be] four handbreadths, and in a small one [the hole should be as large as] the greater part of it.

phrases.he: אִם הָיָה שַׂק אוֹ קֻפָּה, מַטְבִּילִין בָּהֶם כְּמָה שֶׁהֵם, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַמַּיִם מְעֹרָבִין.
phrases.en: If there was a sack or a basket [in the sea], one may immerse in them as they are, since the water is mixed together.

phrases.he: הָיוּ נְתוּנִים תַּחַת הַצִּנּוֹר, אֵינָם פּוֹסְלִים אֶת הַמִּקְוֶה, אֶלָּא מַטְבִּילִין אוֹתָן וּמַעֲלִין אוֹתָן כְּדַרְכָּן
phrases.en: If they are placed under a water-spout, they do not make the mikveh invalid. And they may be immersed and brought up in the ordinary way.

phrases.he: גִּסְטְרָא שֶׁבַּמִּקְוֶה וְהִטְבִּיל בָּהּ אֶת הַכֵּלִים, טָהֲרוּ מִטֻּמְאָתָן, אֲבָל טְמֵאִים עַל גַּב כְּלִי חֶרֶס.
phrases.en: If there was a broken [earthenware] vessel in the mikveh and utensils were immersed in it, they become clean from their [former] uncleanness but are again rendered unclean because of the earthenware vessel.

phrases.he: אִם הָיוּ הַמַּיִם צָפִים עַל גַּבָּיו כָּל שֶׁהֵן, טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: But if water flowed above it in any quantity, they are clean.

phrases.he: מַעְיָן הַיּוֹצֵא מִן הַתַּנּוּר וְיָרַד וְטָבַל בְּתוֹכוֹ, הוּא טָהוֹר וְיָדָיו טְמֵאוֹת.
phrases.en: If [water of] a spring flowed forth from an oven and a man went down and immersed himself in it, he is clean but his hands become unclean.

phrases.he: וְאִם הָיוּ עַל גַּבָּיו רוּם יָדָיו, אַף יָדָיו טְהוֹרוֹת
phrases.en: But if [the water was as] high above the oven as the height of his hands, his hands also are clean.

phrases.he: עֵרוּב מִקְוָאוֹת, כִּשְׁפוֹפֶרֶת הַנּוֹד, כְּעָבְיָהּ וְכַחֲלָלָהּ, כִּשְׁתֵּי אֶצְבָּעוֹת חוֹזְרוֹת לִמְקוֹמָן.
phrases.en: Mikvaot can be joined together [if their connection is as big] as the tube of a water-skin in thickness and in space, in which two fingers can be fully turned round.

phrases.he: סָפֵק כִּשְׁפוֹפֶרֶת הַנּוֹד, סָפֵק שֶׁאֵינָהּ כִּשְׁפוֹפֶרֶת הַנּוֹד, פְּסוּלָה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא מִן הַתּוֹרָה.
phrases.en: If there is a doubt [whether it is as big] as the tube of a water skin or not, it is invalid, because [this is a mitzvah] from the Torah.

phrases.he: וְכֵן כַּזַּיִת מִן הַמֵּת וְכַזַּיִת מִן הַנְּבֵלָה וְכָעֲדָשָׁה מִן הַשֶּׁרֶץ.
phrases.en: The same applies also to the olive's bulk of a corpse and the olive's bulk of carrion and the lentil's bulk of a sheretz.

phrases.he: כֹּל שֶׁיַּעֲמֹד כִּשְׁפוֹפֶרֶת הַנּוֹד, מְמַעֲטָהּ.
phrases.en: Anything which remains in [the space measuring] the tube of a water-skin lessens [its measure].

phrases.he: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, כֹּל שֶׁהוּא מִבְּרִיַּת הַמַּיִם, טָהוֹר
phrases.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamaliel says: if it is any water creature whatsoever, [the mikvaot] remain clean.

phrases.he: מְטַהֲרִים אֶת הַמִּקְוָאוֹת, הָעֶלְיוֹן מִן הַתַּחְתּוֹן, וְהָרָחוֹק מִן הַקָּרוֹב. כֵּיצַד.
phrases.en: Mikvaot may be made clean [by joining drawn water from] a higher [mikveh to valid water] from a lower [mikveh or drawn water from] a distant [mikveh to valid water] in a [mikveh] near at hand.

phrases.he: מֵבִיא סִלּוֹן שֶׁל חֶרֶס אוֹ שֶׁל אֲבָר, וּמַנִּיחַ יָדוֹ תַּחְתָּיו, עַד שֶׁהוּא מִתְמַלֵּא מַיִם, וּמוֹשְׁכוֹ וּמַשִּׁיקוֹ, אֲפִלּוּ כַשַּׂעֲרָה, דַּיּוֹ.
phrases.en: How so? One brings a pipe of earthenware or of lead and puts his hand beneath it till it is filled with water; then he draws it along till [the two waters] touch even if it be by a hair's breadth it is sufficient.

phrases.he: הָיָה בָעֶלְיוֹן אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה וּבַתַּחְתּוֹן אֵין כְּלוּם, מְמַלֵּא בַכָּתֵף וְנוֹתֵן לָעֶלְיוֹן, עַד שֶׁיֵּרְדוּ לַתַּחְתּוֹן אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה
phrases.en: If in the higher [mikveh] there were forty seahs and nothing in the lower, one may draw water and carry it on the shoulder and place it in the higher [mikveh] till forty seahs have flowed down into the lower [mikveh].

phrases.he: כֹּתֶל שֶׁבֵּין שְׁתֵּי מִקְוָאוֹת שֶׁנִּסְדַּק לַשְּׁתִי, מִצְטָרֵף.
phrases.en: If a wall between two mikvaot had a perpendicular crack, [their waters] may be reckoned together; [If it was cracked] horizontally, they cannot be reckoned together, unless there is at one place [a hole as big] as the tube of a water-skin.

phrases.he: וְלָעֵרֶב, אֵין מִצְטָרֵף, עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בְמָקוֹם אֶחָד כִּשְׁפוֹפֶרֶת הַנּוֹד.
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, חִלּוּף הַדְּבָרִים.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: the rule is reversed.

phrases.he: נִפְרְצוּ זֶה בְתוֹךְ זֶה, עַל רוּם, כִּקְלִפַּת הַשּׁוּם.
phrases.en: If there is a breach from one [mikveh] to the other, [they can be reckoned together] if the height is as [the thickness of] the skin of garlic and the breadth like the tube of a water-skin.

phrases.he: וְעַל רֹחַב, כִּשְׁפוֹפֶרֶת הַנּוֹד
הָאָבִיק שֶׁבַּמֶּרְחָץ, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהוּא בָאֶמְצַע, פּוֹסֵל.
phrases.en: The outlet of a bath-basin: if it is in the center, it renders [the bath] invalid [as a mikveh]; but if it is at the side, it does not render it invalid, because then it is like one mikveh adjoining another mikveh, the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: מִן הַצַּד, אֵינוֹ פוֹסֵל, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא כְמִקְוֶה סָמוּךְ לְמִקְוֶה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אִם מְקַבֶּלֶת הָאַמְבָּטִי רְבִיעִית עַד שֶׁלֹּא יַגִּיעוּ לָאָבִיק, כָּשֵׁר. וְאִם לָאו, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: But the sages say: if the bath- basin can contain a quarter-log of [water] before it reaches the outlet, it is valid; but if not, it is not valid.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר, אִם מְקַבֵּל הָאָבִיק כָּל שֶׁהוּא, פָּסוּל
phrases.en: Rabbi Elazar bar Zadok says: if the outlet can contain any amount of [water], it is invalid.

phrases.he: הַמַּטְהֶרֶת שֶׁבַּמֶּרְחָץ, הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה מְלֵאָה שְׁאוּבִין וְהָעֶלְיוֹנָה מְלֵאָה כְשֵׁרִין, אִם יֵשׁ כְּנֶגֶד הַנֶּקֶב שְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין, פָּסוּל.
phrases.en: The ‘purifier' in the bathhouse: the bottom was full of drawn [water] and the top full of valid [water], if [the space] in front of the hole can contain three logs it is invalid [as a mikveh].

phrases.he: כַּמָּה יְהֵא בַנֶּקֶב וְיִהְיֶה בוֹ שְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין.
phrases.en: How large must the hole be to contain three logs? 1/320th of the pool, the words of Rabbi Yose.

phrases.he: אַחַד מִשְּׁלשׁ מֵאוֹת וְעֶשְׂרִים לַבְּרֵכָה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי.

וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר, אֲפִלּוּ הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה מְלֵאָה כְשֵׁרִים וְהָעֶלְיוֹנָה מְלֵאָה שְׁאוּבִין וְיֵשׁ בְּצַד הַנֶּקֶב שְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין, כָּשֵׁר, שֶׁלֹּא אָמְרוּ אֶלָּא שְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין שֶׁנָּפְלוּ:
phrases.en: But Rabbi Elazar says: even if the bottom [pipe] was full of valid [water] and the top [pipe] full of drawn [water] and by the hole's side were three logs, [the bath is] valid, for they have only said: "if three logs fell in."

phrases.he: יֵשׁ מַעֲלִין אֶת הַמִּקְוֶה וְלֹא פוֹסְלִין, פּוֹסְלִין וְלֹא מַעֲלִין, לֹא מַעֲלִין וְלֹא פוֹסְלִין.
phrases.en: Some materials raise the mikveh up [to the required quantity] and do not make it invalid.

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ מַעֲלִין וְלֹא פוֹסְלִין, הַשֶּׁלֶג, וְהַבָּרָד, וְהַכְּפוֹר, וְהַגְּלִיד, וְהַמֶּלַח, וְהַטִּיט הַנָּרוֹק.
phrases.en: Some make it invalid and do not raise it up [to the required quantity]; And some neither raise it up [to the required quantity] nor make it invalid. These raise it up to the required quantity and do not make the mikveh invalid.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, הָיָה רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל דָּן כְּנֶגְדִּי לוֹמַר, הַשֶּׁלֶג אֵינוֹ מַעֲלֶה אֶת הַמִּקְוֶה.
phrases.en: Snow, hail, frosted dew, ice, salt, and thin mud. Rabbi Akiva said: Rabbi Ishmael once argued against me saying; snow does not raise up the mikveh [to its required quantity].

phrases.he: וְהֵעִידוּ אַנְשֵׁי מֵידְבָא מִשְּׁמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר לָהֶם, צְאוּ וְהָבִיאוּ שֶׁלֶג וַעֲשׂוּ מִקְוֶה בַּתְּחִלָּה.
phrases.en: But the men of Madeba testified in his name that he had once told them: go and bring snow and with it prepare a mikveh from the outset.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אוֹמֵר, אֶבֶן הַבָּרָד, כַּמָּיִם.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yohanan ben Nuri says: hailstones are like drawn water.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד מַעֲלִין וְלֹא פוֹסְלִין.
phrases.en: How do they raise it up [to the required quantity] and not render it invalid? If the mikveh contained forty seahs less one, and a se'ah of them fell in and made up [the required quantity], they thus make up [the required quantity] but do not render it invalid.

phrases.he: מִקְוֶה שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה חָסֵר אַחַת, נָפַל מֵהֶם סְאָה לְתוֹכוֹ וְהֶעֱלָהוּ, נִמְצְאוּ מַעֲלִין וְלֹא פוֹסְלִין
אֵלּוּ פוֹסְלִין וְלֹא מַעֲלִין, הַמַּיִם, בֵּין טְמֵאִים בֵּין טְהוֹרִים, וּמֵי כְבָשִׁים וּמֵי שְׁלָקוֹת, וְהַתֶּמֶד עַד שֶׁלֹּא הֶחֱמִיץ.
phrases.en: These invalidate the mikveh and do not raise it up to [the required quantity]: Drawn water, whether clean or unclean, water that has been used for pickling or for boiling, and grape-skin wine before it becomes vinegar.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד פּוֹסְלִין וְלֹא מַעֲלִין.
phrases.en: How do they make the mikveh invalid and do not raise it up [the required quantity]? If a mikveh contained forty seahs less a kortov, and a kortov of these fell into it, it does not raise it up [the required quantity]; And if there were three logs of any of these, they would invalidate the mikveh.

phrases.he: מִקְוֶה שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה חָסֵר קֹרְטוֹב, וְנָפַל מֵהֶן קֹרְטוֹב לְתוֹכוֹ, לֹא הֶעֱלָהוּ, פּוֹסְלוֹ בִשְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין.
phrases.en: But other liquids, and the juice of fruits, brine, and liquid in which fish has been pickled, and grape-skin wine that has fermented sometimes raise it up to [the required quantity] and sometimes do not raise it up.

phrases.he: אֲבָל שְׁאָר הַמַּשְׁקִין, וּמֵי פֵרוֹת, וְהַצִּיר, וְהַמֻּרְיָס, וְהַתֶּמֶד מִשֶּׁהֶחֱמִיץ, פְּעָמִים מַעֲלִין וּפְעָמִים שֶׁאֵינָן מַעֲלִין. כֵּיצַד.
phrases.en: How so? If a mikveh contained forty seahs less one, and a seah of any of these fell in it, it does not raise it up to [the required quantity].

phrases.he: מִקְוֶה שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה חָסֵר אַחַת, נָפַל לְתוֹכוֹ סְאָה מֵהֶם, לֹא הֶעֱלָהוּ.
phrases.en: But if the mikveh contained forty seahs and a se'ah of any of these was put in and one seah was removed, the mikveh is still valid.

phrases.he: הָיוּ בוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה, נָתַן סְאָה וְנָטַל סְאָה, הֲרֵי זֶה כָשֵׁר
הֵדִיחַ בּוֹ סַלֵּי זֵיתִים וְסַלֵּי עֲנָבִים, וְשִׁנּוּ אֶת מַרְאָיו, כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.en: If he rinsed in the mikveh baskets of olives or baskets of grapes and they changed its color, it remains valid.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, מֵי הַצֶּבַע פּוֹסְלִין אוֹתוֹ בִשְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין, וְאֵינָן פּוֹסְלִין אוֹתוֹ בְשִׁנּוּי מַרְאֶה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: dye-water renders it invalid by a quantity of three logs, but not merely by changing its color.

phrases.he: נָפַל לְתוֹכוֹ יַיִן, וּמֹחַל, וְשִׁנּוּ אֶת מַרְאָיו, פָּסוּל. כֵּיצַד יַעֲשֶׂה.
phrases.en: If wine or the sap of olives fell into it and changed its color, it becomes invalid.

phrases.he: יַמְתִּין לוֹ עַד שֶׁיֵּרְדוּ גְשָׁמִים וְיַחְזְרוּ מַרְאֵיהֶן לְמַרְאֵה הַמָּיִם.
phrases.en: What should one do [to make it valid again]? One should wait until the rain falls and the color reverts to the color of water.

phrases.he: הָיוּ בוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה, מְמַלֵּא בַכָּתֵף וְנוֹתֵן לְתוֹכוֹ עַד שֶׁיַּחְזְרוּ מַרְאֵיהֶן לְמַרְאֵה הַמָּיִם
phrases.en: If it contained forty seahs, water may be drawn and carried on the shoulder and put into it until the color reverts to that of water.

phrases.he: נָפַל לְתוֹכוֹ יַיִן אוֹ מֹחַל וְשִׁנּוּ מִקְצָת מַרְאָיו, אִם אֵין בּוֹ מַרְאֵה מַיִם אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה, הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא יִטְבֹּל בּוֹ:
phrases.en: If wine or the sap of olives fell into the mikveh and changed the color of a portion of the water, if there is not a portion [of the mikveh] that has forty seahs with the color of water, one may not immerse in there.

phrases.he: שְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין מַיִם, וְנָפַל לְתוֹכָן קֹרְטוֹב יַיִן, וַהֲרֵי מַרְאֵיהֶן כְּמַרְאֵה הַיַּיִן, וְנָפְלוּ לְמִקְוֶה, לֹא פְסָלוּהוּ.
phrases.en: If a kortov of wine fell into three logs of water and its color became like that of wine, and the water then fell into a mikveh, it does not render it invalid.

phrases.he: שְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין מַיִם חָסֵר קֹרְטוֹב, וְנָפַל לְתוֹכָן קֹרְטוֹב חָלָב, וַהֲרֵי מַרְאֵיהֶן כְּמַרְאֵה הַמַּיִם, וְנָפְלוּ לְמִקְוֶה, לֹא פְסָלוּהוּ.
phrases.en: If there were three logs of water less a kortov into which a kortov of milk fell, and their color remained like the color of water, and then they fell into a mikveh, they do not render it invalid.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אוֹמֵר, הַכֹּל הוֹלֵךְ אַחַר הַמַּרְאֶה
phrases.en: Rabbi Yohanan ben Nuri says: everything goes by the color.

phrases.he: מִקְוֶה שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה מְכֻוָּנוֹת, יָרְדוּ שְׁנַיִם וְטָבְלוּ זֶה אַחַר זֶה, הָרִאשׁוֹן טָהוֹר, וְהַשֵּׁנִי טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If a mikveh contained forty seahs exactly and two persons went down and immersed themselves one after the other, the first becomes clean but the second remains unclean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אִם הָיוּ רַגְלָיו שֶׁל רִאשׁוֹן נוֹגְעוֹת בַּמַּיִם, אַף הַשֵּׁנִי טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: if the feet of the first were still touching the water, the second also becomes clean.

phrases.he: הִטְבִּיל בּוֹ אֶת הַסָּגוֹס וְהֶעֱלָהוּ, מִקְצָתוֹ נוֹגֵעַ בַּמַּיִם, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If one immersed a thick cloak and when he drew it out a part was still in contact with the water [and then another person immersed himself in the mikveh], he becomes clean.

phrases.he: הַכַּר וְהַכֶּסֶת שֶׁל עוֹר, כֵּיוָן שֶׁהִגְבִּיהַּ שִׂפְתוֹתֵיהֶם מִן הַמַּיִם, הַמַּיִם שֶׁבְּתוֹכָן שְׁאוּבִין.
phrases.en: A pillow case or a cushion of leather, as soon as it is taken out of the water by its open ends the water which still remains in it is drawn water.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד יַעֲשֶׂה, מַטְבִּילָן וּמַעֲלֶה אוֹתָם דֶּרֶךְ שׁוּלֵיהֶם
phrases.en: How should one do it? One should immerse them and draw them up by their lower edges.

phrases.he: הִטְבִּיל בּוֹ אֶת הַמִּטָּה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁרַגְלֶיהָ שׁוֹקְעוֹת בַּטִּיט הֶעָבֶה, טְהוֹרָה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַמַּיִם מְקַדְּמִין.
phrases.en: If he immersed a bed in it, even though its legs sink into the thick mud, it still becomes clean because the water touched them before [the mud].

phrases.he: מִקְוֶה שֶׁמֵּימָיו מְרֻדָּדִין, כּוֹבֵשׁ אֲפִלּוּ חֲבִילֵי עֵצִים, אֲפִלּוּ חֲבִילֵי קָנִים, כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּתְפְּחוּ הַמַּיִם, וְיוֹרֵד וְטוֹבֵל.
phrases.en: The water of a mikveh which is shallow, one may press down even bundles of sticks, even bundles of reeds, so that the level of the water may rise, and then go down and immerse oneself.

phrases.he: מַחַט שֶׁהִיא נְתוּנָה עַל מַעֲלוֹת הַמְּעָרָה, הָיָה מוֹלִיךְ וּמֵבִיא בַמַּיִם, כֵּיוָן שֶׁעָבַר עָלֶיהָ הַגַּל, טְהוֹרָה
phrases.en: If an [unclean] needle is placed on the step [leading down to a mikveh] in a cavern, and the water is put in motion, once a wave has passed over it, [the needle] becomes clean.

phrases.he: אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל טְהוֹרָה, וּמִקְוְאוֹתֶיהָ טְהוֹרִים.
phrases.en: The land of Israel is clean and its mikvaot are clean.

phrases.he: מִקְוְאוֹת הָעַמִּים שֶׁבְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ, כְּשֵׁרִים לְבַעֲלֵי קְרָיִין, אֲפִלּוּ נִתְמַלְּאוּ בְקִילוֹן.
phrases.en: The mikvaot of the nations outside the land are valid for those who had a seminal emission even though they have been filled by a pump-beam; Those in the land of Israel: when outside the entrance [to the city] are valid even for menstruants, and those within the entrance [to the city] are valid for those who had a seminal emission but invalid for all [others] who are unclean.

phrases.he: שֶׁבְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁחוּץ לַמַּפְתֵּחַ, כְּשֵׁרִים אַף לְנִדּוֹת.
מִלִּפְנִים מִן הַמַּפְתֵּחַ, כְּשֵׁרִים לְבַעֲלֵי קְרָיִין, וּפְסוּלִים לְכָל הַטְּמֵאִים.
רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, הַקְּרוֹבִים לָעִיר וְלַדֶּרֶךְ, טְמֵאִים, מִפְּנֵי הַכְּבִיסָה. וְהָרְחוֹקִים, טְהוֹרִים:
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: those which are near to a city or to a road are unclean because of laundering; but those at a distance are clean.

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ בַעֲלֵי קְרָיִין שֶׁהֵם צְרִיכִין טְבִילָה.
phrases.en: These are the men who had a seminal emission who require immersion: If he noticed that his urine issued in drops or was murky: At the beginning he is clean; In the middle and at the end, he is unclean; From the beginning to the end, he is clean.

phrases.he: רָאָה מַיִם חֲלוּקִים אוֹ עֲכוּרִים, בַּתְּחִלָּה, טָהוֹר. בָּאֶמְצַע וּבַסּוֹף, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If it was white and viscous, he is unclean.

phrases.he: מִתְּחִלָּה וְעַד סוֹף, טָהוֹר. לְבָנִים וְנִמְשָׁכִים, טָמֵא.
רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, לְבָנִים כָּעֲכוּרִים:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: what is white counts like what is murky.

phrases.he: הַמֵּטִיל טִפִּין עָבוֹת מִתּוֹךְ הָאַמָּה, טָמֵא, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר חִסְמָא.
phrases.en: If he emitted thick drops from his member, he is unclean, the words of Rabbi Elazar Hisma.

phrases.he: הַמְהַרְהֵר בַּלַּיְלָה וְעָמַד וּמָצָא בְשָׂרוֹ חַם, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If one had sexual dreams in the night and arose and found his flesh heated, he is unclean.

phrases.he: הַפּוֹלֶטֶת זֶרַע בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁי, טְהוֹרָה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה.
phrases.en: If a woman discharged semen on the third day, she is clean, the words of Rabbi Elazar ben Azariah.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר, פְּעָמִים שֶׁהֵם אַרְבַּע עוֹנוֹת, פְּעָמִים שֶׁהֵם חָמֵשׁ, פְּעָמִים שֶׁהֵם שֵׁשׁ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Ishmael says: sometimes there are four time periods, and sometimes five, and sometimes six.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, לְעוֹלָם חָמֵשׁ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says: there are always five.

phrases.he: נָכְרִית שֶׁפָּלְטָה שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, טְמֵאָה.
phrases.en: If a non-Jewish woman discharged semen from an Israelite, it is unclean.

phrases.he: בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁפָּלְטָה שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע מִנָּכְרִי, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: If an Israelite woman discharged semen from a non-Jewish man, it is clean.

phrases.he: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁשִּׁמְּשָׁה בֵיתָהּ, וְיָרְדָה וְטָבְלָה, וְלֹא כִבְּדָה אֶת הַבַּיִת, כְּאִלּוּ לֹא טָבְלָה.
phrases.en: If a woman had intercourse and then went down and immersed herself but did not sweep out the house, it is as though she had not immersed herself.

phrases.he: בַּעַל קֶרִי שֶׁטָּבַל וְלֹא הֵטִיל אֶת הַמַּיִם, כְּשֶׁיָטִיל אֶת הַמַּיִם, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If a man who had a seminal emission immersed himself but did not first pass urine, he again becomes unclean when he passes urine.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, בְּחוֹלֶה וּבְזָקֵן, טָמֵא. בְּיֶלֶד וּבְבָרִיא, טָהוֹר:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: if he was sick or old he is unclean, but if he was young and healthy he remains clean.

phrases.he: נִדָּה שֶׁנָּתְנָה מָעוֹת בְּפִיהָ וְיָרְדָה וְטָבְלָה, טְהוֹרָה מִטֻּמְאָתָהּ, אֲבָל טְמֵאָה הִיא עַל גַּב רֻקָּהּ.
phrases.en: If a menstruant placed coins in her mouth and went down and immersed herself, she becomes clean from her [former] uncleanness, but she becomes unclean on account of her spittle.

phrases.he: נָתְנָה שְׂעָרָהּ בְּפִיהָ, קָפְצָה יָדָהּ, קָרְצָה שִׂפְתוֹתֶיהָ, כְּאִלּוּ לֹא טָבְלָה.
phrases.en: If she put her hair in her mouth or closed her hand or pressed her lips tightly, it is as though she had not immersed herself.

phrases.he: הָאוֹחֵז בְּאָדָם וּבְכֵלִים וּמַטְבִּילָן, טְמֵאִין.
phrases.en: If a person held on to another man or to vessels and immersed them, they remain unclean; but if he had washed his hand before in the water, they become clean.

phrases.he: וְאִם הֵדִיחַ אֶת יָדוֹ בַּמַּיִם, טְהוֹרִים.
רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, יְרַפֶּה, כְּדֵי שֶׁיָּבֹאוּ בָהֶם מָיִם.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: he should hold them loosely that water may enter into them.

phrases.he: בֵּית הַסְּתָרִים, בֵּית הַקְּמָטִים, אֵינָן צְרִיכִין שֶׁיָּבֹאוּ בָהֶן מָיִם
phrases.en: The hidden or wrinkled parts of the body do not need that water should enter into them.

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ חוֹצְצִין בָּאָדָם, חוּטֵי צֶמֶר וְחוּטֵי פִשְׁתָּן וְהָרְצוּעוֹת שֶׁבְּרָאשֵׁי הַבָּנוֹת.
phrases.en: The following block [immersion] in the case of a person: threads of wool, threads of flax and the ribbons on the heads of girls.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, שֶׁל צֶמֶר וְשֶׁל שֵׂעָר אֵינָם חוֹצְצִין, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַמַּיִם בָּאִין בָּהֶם:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: those of wool or of hair do not interpose, because water enters through them.

phrases.he: קִלְקֵי הַלֵּב וְהַזָּקָן, וּבֵית הַסְּתָרִים בָּאִשָּׁה, לִפְלוּף שֶׁחוּץ לָעַיִן, וְגֶלֶד שֶׁחוּץ לַמַּכָּה, וְהָרְטִיָּה שֶׁעָלֶיהָ, וּשְׂרָף הַיָּבֵשׁ, וְגִלְדֵי צוֹאָה שֶׁעַל בְּשָׂרוֹ, וּבָצֵק שֶׁתַּחַת הַצִּפֹּרֶן, וְהַמִּלְמוּלִין, וְטִיט הַיָּוֵן, וְטִיט הַיּוֹצְרִים, וְגֵץ יְוֵנִי.
phrases.en: The matted hair on the heart and on the beard and on a woman's hidden parts; pus outside the eye, hardened pus outside a wound and the plaster over it, dried-up juice, clots of excrement on the body, dough under the finger nails, sweat-crumbs, miry clay, potter's clay, and road-clay.

phrases.he: אֵיזֶהוּ טִיט הַיָּוֵן, זֶה טִיט הַבּוֹרוֹת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (תהלים מ), וַיַּעֲלֵנִי מִבּוֹר שָׁאוֹן מִטִּיט הַיָּוֵן. טִיט הַיּוֹצְרִין, כְּמַשְׁמָעוֹ.
phrases.en: What is meant by 'miry clay’? This means the clay in pits, for it is written: "He lifted me out of the miry pit, the slimy clay" (Psalms 40:3). "Potter's clay" according to its literal sense.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מְטַהֵר בְּשֶׁל יוֹצְרִין וּמְטַמֵּא בְּשֶׁל מָרֵקָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose declares potter's clay clean, but clay for putty unclean. And "road-clay.

phrases.he: וְגֵץ יְוֵנִי, אֵלּוּ יִתְדוֹת הַדְּרָכִים, שֶׁאֵין טוֹבְלִין בָּהֶן וְלֹא מַטְבִּילִין אוֹתָן.
phrases.en: These become like road-side pegs in these [kinds of clay] one may not immerse oneself nor immerse [other things] with them; But in all other clay one may immerse when it is wet.

phrases.he: וּשְׁאָר כָּל הַטִּיט, מַטְבִּילִין בּוֹ כְּשֶׁהוּא לַח.
phrases.en: One may not immerse oneself with dust [still] on one's feet.

phrases.he: וְלֹא יִטְבֹּל בָּאָבָק שֶׁעַל רַגְלָיו.
phrases.en: One may not immerse a kettle with soot [on it] unless he scraped it.

phrases.he: לֹא יִטְבֹּל אֶת הַקֻּמְקְמוּס בַּפֶּחָמִין, אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן שִׁפְשֵׁף
אֵלּוּ שֶׁאֵין חוֹצְצִין, קִלְקֵי הָרֹאשׁ, וּבֵית הַשֶּׁחִי, וּבֵית הַסְּתָרִים בָּאִישׁ.
phrases.en: The following do not block: the matted hair of the head and of the armpits and of a man's hidden parts.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אֶחָד הָאִישׁ וְאֶחָד הָאִשָּׁה, כָּל הַמַּקְפִּיד עָלָיו, חוֹצֵץ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: it is the same with a man or a woman: if it is something which one finds annoying, it blocks; but if it is something which one does not find annoying, it does not interpose.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁאֵין מַקְפִּיד עָלָיו, אֵין חוֹצֵץ

לִפְלוּף שֶׁבָּעַיִן, וְגֶלֶד שֶׁעַל הַמַּכָּה, וּשְׂרָף הַלַּח, וְלִכְלוּכֵי צוֹאָה שֶׁעַל בְּשָׂרוֹ, וְצוֹאָה שֶׁתַּחַת הַצִּפֹּרֶן, וְצִפֹּרֶן הַמְדֻלְדֶּלֶת, כְּשׁוּת שֶׁל קָטָן, לֹא טָמֵא וְלֹא מְטַמֵּא.
phrases.en: Pus within the eye, hardened pus within a wound, juice that is moist, moist excrement on the body, excrement inside the finger nail, and a dangling finger nail and the downy hair of a child. [These] are not liable to uncleanness and do not cause uncleanness.

phrases.he: קְרוּם שֶׁעַל הַמַּכָּה, טָמֵא וּמְטַמֵּא
phrases.en: The membrane which forms over a wound is liable to uncleanness and causes uncleanness.

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ חוֹצְצִים בַּכֵּלִים. הַזֶּפֶת וְהַמּוֹר בִּכְלֵי זְכוּכִית, בֵּין מִבִּפְנִים בֵּין מִבַּחוּץ.
phrases.en: In the case of vessels the following block: pitch and myrrh; In the case of glass vessels, whether inside or outside; On a table or on a board or on a couch; On those that are [usually] kept clean they block; On those that are allowed to remain dirty they do not block.

phrases.he: עַל הַשֻּׁלְחָן וְעַל הַטַּבְלָה וְעַל הַדַּרְגָּשׁ, עַל הַנְּקִיִּים, חוֹצְצִין.
phrases.en: They block in the case of beds belonging to householders, but they do not block on beds belonging to a poor person.

phrases.he: עַל הַבְּלוּסִין, אֵינָן חוֹצְצִין.
phrases.en: They block on the saddle of a house-holder, but they do not block on the saddle of a dealer in water-skins.

phrases.he: עַל מִטּוֹת בַּעַל הַבַּיִת, חוֹצֵץ.
phrases.en: They block in the case of a pack-saddle.

phrases.he: וְעַל שֶׁל עָנִי, אֵינוֹ חוֹצֵץ.
phrases.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamaliel says: [only if the stain is as big] as an Italian issar.

phrases.he: עַל אִכּוּף שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת, חוֹצֵץ.
וְעַל שֶׁל זַקָּקִין, אֵינוֹ חוֹצֵץ. וְעַל הַמַּרְדַּעַת, חוֹצֵץ.
רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר, עַד כְּאִסָּר הָאִיטַלְקִי
עַל הַבְּגָדִים, מִצַּד אֶחָד, אֵינוֹ חוֹצֵץ. מִשְּׁנֵי צְדָדִין, חוֹצֵץ.
phrases.en: On clothing: if on one side [only] they do not block. But [if found] on two sides they do block.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, אַף מִצַּד אֶחָד.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says in the name of Rabbi Ishmael: on one side also.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, שֶׁל בַּנָּאִים, מִצַּד אֶחָד.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: in the case of builders they block if on one side, but in the case of the ditch-digger only if on both sides.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁל בּוּר, מִשְּׁנֵי צְדָדִין
מִטְפַּחַת שֶׁל זַפָּתִין וְשֶׁל יוֹצְרִין וְשֶׁל מְפַסְּלֵי אִילָנוֹת, אֵין חוֹצְצִין.
phrases.en: They do not block in the case of aprons belonging to workers in pitch, potters, or trimmers of trees.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף שֶׁל קַיָּצִין, כַּיּוֹצֵא בָהֶן.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: the same applies also to summer fruit-driers.

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, כָּל הַמַּקְפִּיד עָלָיו, חוֹצֵץ.
phrases.en: This is the general rule: if it is something which one cares enough [to remove], it blocks; but if it is something which one does not care enough [to remove], it does not block.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ מַקְפִּיד עָלָיו, אֵינוֹ חוֹצֵץ
כָּל יְדוֹת הַכֵּלִים שֶׁהִכְנִיסָן שֶׁלֹּא כְדַרְכָּן, אוֹ שֶׁהִכְנִיסָן כְּדַרְכָּן וְלֹא מֵרְקָן, אוֹ שֶׁמֵּרְקָן וְנִשְׁבְּרוּ, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ חוֹצְצִין.
phrases.en: Any handles of vessels which have been fixed not in their usual manner, or, if fixed in their usual manner, have not been fixed firmly, or, if fixed firmly, have been broken, they block.

phrases.he: כְּלִי שֶׁהִטְבִּילוֹ דֶּרֶךְ פִּיו, כְּאִלּוּ לֹא טָבָל.
phrases.en: If a vessel was immersed with its mouth downwards, it is as though it had not been immersed.

phrases.he: הִטְבִּילוֹ כְדַרְכּוֹ בְלֹא זִבּוֹרִית, עַד שֶׁיַּטֶּנּוּ עַל צִדּוֹ.
phrases.en: If immersed in the regular manner but without the attachment, [it becomes clean] only if turned on its side.

phrases.he: כְּלִי שֶׁהוּא צַר מִכָּאן וּמִכָּאן וְרָחָב מִן הָאֶמְצַע, אֵינוֹ טָהוֹר עַד שֶׁיַּטֶּנּוּ עַל צִדּוֹ.
phrases.en: If a vessel is narrow at each end and broad in the center, it becomes clean only if turned on its side.

phrases.he: צְלוֹחִית שֶׁפִּיהָ שׁוֹקֵעַ, אֵינָהּ טְהוֹרָה עַד שֶׁיְּנַקְּבֶנָּה מִצִּדָּהּ.
phrases.en: A flask which has its mouth turned inwards becomes clean only if a hole is made at the side.

phrases.he: קַלְמָרִין הֶדְיוֹטוֹת, אֵינָהּ טְהוֹרָה עַד שֶׁיְּנַקְּבֶנָּה מִצִּדָּהּ.
phrases.en: An inkpot of laymen becomes clean only if a hole is made at the side.

phrases.he: וְקַלְמָרִין שֶׁל יוֹסֵף הַכֹּהֵן הָיְתָה נְקוּבָה בְצִדָּהּ
phrases.en: The inkpot of Joseph the priest had a hole at its side.

phrases.he: הַכַּר וְהַכֶּסֶת שֶׁל עוֹר, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ צְרִיכִין שֶׁיָּבֹאוּ בָהֶם הַמָּיִם.
phrases.en: A bolster and a cushion of leather it is necessary that the water enter inside them.

phrases.he: כֶּסֶת עֲגֻלָּה, וְהַכַּדּוּר, וְהָאֵמוּם, וְהַקָּמֵעַ, וְהַתְּפִלָּה, אֵינָן צְרִיכִין שֶׁיָּבֹאוּ בָהֶם הַמָּיִם.
phrases.en: A round cushion or a ball or a bootmaker's last or an amulet or a phylactery, it is not necessary that the water enter inside them.

phrases.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, כֹּל שֶׁאֵין דַּרְכּוֹ לְהַכְנִיס וּלְהוֹצִיא, טוֹבְלִים סְתוּמִים
phrases.en: This is the general rule: any article the filling of which is not usually taken out and put in may be immersed unopened.

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ שֶׁאֵינָם צְרִיכִים שֶׁיָּבֹאוּ בָהֶם הַמַּיִם, קִשְׁרֵי הֶעָנִי, וְהַנִּימִין, וַחֲבַט שֶׁל סַנְדָּל, וּתְפִלָּה שֶׁל רֹאשׁ בִּזְמַן שֶׁהִיא חוֹצָה, וְשֶׁל זְרוֹעַ בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵינָהּ עוֹלָה וְיוֹרֶדֶת, וְאָזְנֵי הַחֵמֶת, וְאָזְנֵי הַתַּרְמוּל:
phrases.en: The following do not require that the water shall enter inside them:Knots [in the clothes] of a poor man, or in tassels, or in the thong of a sandal, or in a head-tefillin if it is fastened tightly, or in an arm-tefillin if it does not move up or down, or in the handles of a water-skin, or in the handles of a wallet.

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ שֶׁהֵם צְרִיכִים שֶׁיָּבֹאוּ בָהֶן הַמַּיִם, הַקֶּשֶׁר שֶׁבַּפְּרַקְסִים שֶׁבַּכָּתֵף, וְשָׂפָה שֶׁל סָדִין צָרִיךְ לְמַתֵּחַ, וּתְפִלָּה שֶׁל רֹאשׁ בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵינָהּ חוֹצָה, וְשֶׁל זְרוֹעַ בִּזְמַן שֶׁהִיא עוֹלָה וְיוֹרֶדֶת, וּשְׁנָצִין שֶׁל סַנְדָּל, וּבְגָדִים שֶׁהִטְבִּילָן מְכֻבָּסִין, עַד שֶׁיְּבַעְבְּעוּ.
phrases.en: The following require that water shall enter inside them:The knot in an undergarment which is tied to the shoulder. The hem of a sheet must be stretched out. And the knot of head tefillin if it is not fastened tightly, Or of the arm-tefillin if it moves up and down. And the laces of a sandal. Clothes which are immersed when they have just been washed must be kept immersed until they bubble up; But if they are immersed when already dry, they must be kept immersed until they throw up bubbles and then cease to bubble up.

phrases.he: הִטְבִּילָן נְגוּבִין, עַד שֶׁיְּבַעְבְּעוּ וְיָנוּחוּ מִבִּעְבּוּעָן
כָּל יְדוֹת הַכֵּלִים שֶׁהֵם אֲרֻכִּין וְעָתִיד לִקְצֹץ, מַטְבִּילָן עַד מְקוֹם הַמִּדָּה.
phrases.en: Any handles of vessels which are too long and which will be cut short, need only be immersed up to the point of their proper measure.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, עַד שֶׁיַּטְבִּיל אֶת כֻּלּוֹ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: [they are unclean] until the whole of them is immersed.

phrases.he: שַׁלְשֶׁלֶת דְּלִי גָדוֹל, אַרְבָּעָה טְפָחִים, וְשֶׁל קָטָן, עֲשָׂרָה, מַטְבִּילָן עַד מְקוֹם הַמִּדָּה.
phrases.en: The chain of a large bucket, to the length of four handbreadths, and a small bucket, to the length of ten handbreadths, and they need only be immersed up to the point of their proper measure.

phrases.he: רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר, עַד שֶׁיַּטְבִּיל אֶת כָּל הַטַּבַּעַת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Tarfon says: it is not clean unless the whole of the chain-ring is immersed.

phrases.he: הַחֶבֶל שֶׁהוּא קָשׁוּר בַּקֻּפָּה אֵינוֹ חִבּוּר, אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן תָּפָר
phrases.en: The rope bound to a basket is not counted as a connection unless it has been sewn on.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, אֵין מַטְבִּילִין חַמִּין בְּצוֹנֵן וְלֹא צוֹנֵן בְּחַמִּין, לֹא יָפִים בְּרָעִים וְלֹא רָעִים בְּיָפִים.
phrases.en: Bet Shammai say: hot water may not be immersed in cold, or cold in hot, foul in fresh or fresh in foul. But Bet Hillel say: it may be immersed.

phrases.he: בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, מַטְבִּילִין.
phrases.en: A vessel full of liquids which one immersed, it is as if it has not been immersed.

phrases.he: כְּלִי שֶׁהוּא מָלֵא מַשְׁקִין וְהִטְבִּילוֹ, כְּאִלּוּ לֹא טָבָל.
phrases.en: If it was full of urine, this is reckoned as water.

phrases.he: מָלֵא מֵי רַגְלַיִם, רוֹאִים אוֹתָם כְּאִלּוּ הֵם מָיִם.
phrases.en: If it contained hatat waters, [it is unclean] unless the water [of the mikveh which enters the vessel] exceeds the hatat waters.

phrases.he: מָלֵא מֵי חַטָּאת, עַד שֶׁיִּרְבּוּ הַמַּיִם עַל מֵי חַטָּאת.
רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אֲפִלּוּ כְלִי מַחֲזִיק כּוֹר וְאֵין בּוֹ אֶלָּא רְבִיעִית, כְּאִלּוּ לֹא טָבָל:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: even if a vessel with the capacity of a kor contains but a quarter-log, it is as if it had not been immersed.

phrases.he: כָּל הָאֳכָלִין מִצְטָרְפִין לִפְסֹל אֶת הַגְּוִיָּה בְּכַחֲצִי פְרָס.
phrases.en: All foods combine together to make up the half of a half-loaf which makes the body unfit.

phrases.he: כָּל הַמַּשְׁקִין מִצְטָרְפִין לִפְסֹל אֶת הַגְּוִיָּה בִּרְבִיעִית.
phrases.en: All liquids combine together to make up the quarter-log which makes the body unfit.

phrases.he: זֶה חֹמֶר בְּשׁוֹתֶה מַשְׁקִין טְמֵאִין מִבַּמִּקְוֶה, שֶׁעָשׂוּ בוֹ שְׁאָר הַמַּשְׁקִין כַּמָּיִם
phrases.en: This is more of a stringency in the case of one who drinks unclean liquids than in the case of the mikveh, for in this case they have made all other liquids like water.

phrases.he: אָכַל אֳכָלִים טְמֵאִים, וְשָׁתָה מַשְׁקִים טְמֵאִים, טָבַל וֶהֱקִיאָן, טְמֵאִים, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵינָן טְהוֹרִים בַּגּוּף.
phrases.en: If one ate unclean foods or drank unclean liquids and then he immersed and then vomited them up, they are still unclean because they did not become clean in the body.

phrases.he: שָׁתָה מַיִם טְמֵאִים, טָבַל וֶהֱקִיאָם, טְהוֹרִים, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵם טְהוֹרִים בַּגּוּף.
phrases.en: If one drank unclean water and immersed and then vomited it up, it is clean because it became clean in the body.

phrases.he: בָּלַע טַבַּעַת טְהוֹרָה, נִכְנַס לְאֹהֶל הַמֵּת, הִזָּה וְשָׁנָה וְטָבַל וֶהֱקִיאָהּ, הֲרֵי הִיא כְמוֹת שֶׁהָיְתָה.
phrases.en: If one swallowed a clean ring and then went into the tent of a corpse, if he sprinkled himself once and twice and immersed himself and then vomited it up, behold, it remains as it was before.

phrases.he: בָּלַע טַבַּעַת טְמֵאָה, טוֹבֵל וְאוֹכֵל בַּתְּרוּמָה. הֱקִיאָהּ, טְמֵאָה וְטִמְּאַתּוּ.
phrases.en: If one swallowed an unclean ring, he may immerse himself and eat terumah. If he vomited it up, it is unclean and it renders him unclean.

phrases.he: חֵץ שֶׁהוּא תָחוּב בָּאָדָם, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהוּא נִרְאֶה, חוֹצֵץ.
phrases.en: If an arrow was stuck into a man, it blocks so long as it is visible.

phrases.he: וְאִם אֵינוֹ נִרְאֶה, טוֹבֵל וְאוֹכֵל בִּתְרוּמָתוֹ
phrases.en: But if it is not visible, he may immerse himself and eat terumah.

phrases.he: שַׁמַּאי אוֹמֵר, כָּל הַנָּשִׁים דַּיָּן שְׁעָתָן.
phrases.en: Shammai says: For all women who do not have a fixed menstrual cycle, their time is sufficient. Women who discern that menstrual blood emerged do not need to be concerned that perhaps the flow of blood began before they noticed it.

phrases.he: הִלֵּל אוֹמֵר, מִפְּקִידָה לִפְקִידָה, וַאֲפִלּוּ לְיָמִים הַרְבֵּה.
phrases.en: Rather, they assume their ritual impurity status begins at that moment, in terms of rendering impure teruma and ritually pure items with which they come in contact. Hillel says: From examination [mipekida] to examination, i.e.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, לֹא כְדִבְרֵי זֶה וְלֹא כְדִבְרֵי זֶה, אֶלָּא מֵעֵת לְעֵת מְמַעֵט עַל יַד מִפְּקִידָה לִפְקִידָה, וּמִפְּקִידָה לִפְקִידָה מְמַעֶטֶת עַל יַד מֵעֵת לְעֵת.
phrases.en: she assumes ritual impurity status retroactive to the last time she examined herself and determined that she was ritually pure, and this is the halakha even if her examination took place several days earlier. Any ritually pure item with which she came in contact in the interim becomes ritually impure. And the Rabbis say: The halakha is neither in accordance with the statement of this tanna nor in accordance with the statement of that tanna; rather, the principle is: A twenty-four-hour period reduces the time from examination to examination. In other words, if her final self-examination took place more than twenty-four hours earlier, she need only concern herself with ritual impurity for the twenty-four-hour period prior to discerning the blood. And from examination to examination reduces the time from a twenty-four-hour period.

phrases.he: כָּל אִשָּׁה שֶׁיֶּשׁ לָהּ וֶסֶת, דַּיָּהּ שְׁעָתָהּ.
phrases.en: In other words, if she examined herself in the course of the previous day and discovered no blood, she was certainly ritually pure prior to the examination.

phrases.he: וְהַמְשַׁמֶּשֶׁת בְּעִדִּים, הֲרֵי זוֹ כִפְקִידָה, וּמְמַעֶטֶת עַל יַד מֵעֵת לְעֵת וְעַל יַד מִפְּקִידָה לִפְקִידָה
phrases.en: For any woman who has a fixed menstrual cycle [veset], and she examined herself at that time and discovered blood, her time is sufficient, and it is only from that time that she transmits ritual impurity. And with regard to a woman who engages in intercourse while using examination cloths [be’edim] before and after intercourse, with which she ascertains whether her menstrual flow began, the halakhic status of such an action is like that of an examination, and therefore it reduces the time from a twenty-four-hour period, and reduces the time from examination to examination.

phrases.he: כֵּיצַד דַּיָּהּ שְׁעָתָהּ. הָיְתָה יוֹשֶׁבֶת בַּמִּטָּה וַעֲסוּקָה בְטָהֳרוֹת, וּפֵרְשָׁה וְרָאֲתָה, הִיא טְמֵאָה וְכֻלָּן טְהוֹרוֹת.
phrases.en: Her time is sufficient, how so? If the woman was sitting in the bed and engaged in handling ritually pure items, and she left the bed and saw blood, she is ritually impure and those items are ritually pure.

phrases.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ, מְטַמְּאָה מֵעֵת לְעֵת, אֵינָהּ מוֹנָה אֶלָּא מִשָּׁעָה שֶׁרָאָתָה
phrases.en: Although the Rabbis said that a woman without a fixed menstrual cycle transmits ritual impurity retroactively for a twenty-four-hour period, a woman with a fixed cycle counts her menstrual days only from the moment that she saw blood.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אַרְבַּע נָשִׁים דַּיָּן שְׁעָתָן, בְּתוּלָה, מְעֻבֶּרֶת, מֵנִיקָה וּזְקֵנָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: Unlike the women with regard to whom it was taught that they transmit impurity retroactively, there are four women who discern menstrual blood and their time is sufficient, i.e.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, אֲנִי לֹא שָׁמַעְתִּי אֶלָּא בְתוּלָה, אֲבָל הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר:
phrases.en: they transmit impurity only from the moment that they saw the blood: A virgin, a pregnant woman, a nursing woman, and an elderly woman. Rabbi Yehoshua says: I heard this halakha from my teachers only with regard to a virgin, but the halakha is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer.

phrases.he: אֵיזוֹ הִיא בְתוּלָה, כֹּל שֶׁלֹּא רָאֲתָה דָם מִיָּמֶיהָ, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנְּשׂוּאָה. מְעֻבֶּרֶת, מִשֶּׁיִּוָּדַע עֻבָּרָהּ.
phrases.en: Who is the woman characterized as a virgin in this context? It is any woman who has not seen the flow of menstrual blood in all her days, even if she was married and has experienced bleeding as a result of intercourse consummating her marriage.

phrases.he: מֵנִיקָה, עַד שֶׁתִּגְמֹל אֶת בְּנָהּ.
phrases.en: The time of a pregnant woman is from the point in her pregnancy when the existence of her fetus is known to all who see her.

phrases.he: נָתְנָה בְנָהּ לְמֵנִיקָה, גְּמָלַתּוּ אוֹ מֵת,
phrases.en: The time of a nursing woman is until she weans her child from nursing. If she stopped nursing, e.g.

phrases.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, מְטַמְּאָה מֵעֵת לְעֵת.
phrases.en: she gave her child to a wet nurse, weaned him from nursing, or her child died, and she saw menstrual blood, Rabbi Meir says: She transmits impurity for a twenty-four-hour period or from her most recent examination.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, דַּיָּהּ שְׁעָתָהּ:
phrases.en: And the Rabbis say: Even in those cases, her time is sufficient.

phrases.he: אֵיזוֹהִי זְקֵנָה. כֹּל שֶׁעָבְרוּ עָלֶיהָ שָׁלשׁ עוֹנוֹת סָמוּךְ לְזִקְנָתָהּ.
phrases.en: Who is the woman characterized as an elderly woman in this context? It is any woman for whom three typical menstrual cycles of thirty days passed during which she saw no menstrual blood, at a stage of her life close to her old age.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, כָּל אִשָּׁה שֶׁעָבְרוּ עָלֶיהָ שָׁלשׁ עוֹנוֹת, דַּיָּהּ שְׁעָתָהּ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: In the case of any woman for whom three typical menstrual cycles passed during which she saw no menstrual blood, if she then experiences bleeding, her time is sufficient.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, מְעֻבֶּרֶת וּמֵנִיקָה שֶׁעָבְרוּ עֲלֵיהֶן שָׁלשׁ עוֹנוֹת, דַּיָּן שְׁעָתָן:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei says: With regard to a pregnant woman and a nursing woman for whom three typical menstrual cycles passed during which they saw no menstrual blood, if they then saw blood, their time is sufficient.

phrases.he: וּבַמֶּה אָמְרוּ דַּיָּהּ שְׁעָתָהּ. בִּרְאִיָּה רִאשׁוֹנָה.
phrases.en: And in the above cases, with regard to what did the tanna say her time is sufficient? It is with regard to the first sighting of blood, but with regard to the second sighting, her status is like that of any other woman, and she transmits impurity for a twenty-four-hour period or from her most recent examination.

phrases.he: אֲבָל בַּשְּׁנִיָּה, מְטַמְּאָה מֵעֵת לְעֵת.
phrases.en: And if she saw the first sighting as a result of unnatural circumstances, even with regard to the second sighting, the halakha is that her time is sufficient.

phrases.he: וְאִם רָאֲתָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה מֵאֹנֶס, אַף הַשְּׁנִיָּה דַּיָּהּ שְׁעָתָהּ
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ דַּיָּהּ שְׁעָתָהּ, צְרִיכָה לִהְיוֹת בּוֹדֶקֶת, חוּץ מִן הַנִּדָּה וְהַיּוֹשֶׁבֶת עַל דַּם טֹהַר.
phrases.en: Although the Rabbis said that for a woman with a fixed menstrual cycle her time is sufficient and she does not transmit impurity retroactively, she is required to examine herself each day to ensure that she is ritually pure and will not impurify pure items that she is handling.

phrases.he: וּמְשַׁמֶּשֶׁת בְּעִדִּים, חוּץ מִיּוֹשֶׁבֶת עַל דַּם טֹהַר, וּבְתוּלָה שֶׁדָּמֶיהָ טְהוֹרִים.
phrases.en: All women must examine themselves each day except for a menstruating woman, whose impure status is known, and a woman after childbirth who is observing the period of the blood of purity, whose ritually pure status is known even if she experiences bleeding.

phrases.he: וּפַעֲמַיִם צְרִיכָה לִהְיוֹת בּוֹדֶקֶת, בְּשַׁחֲרִית וּבֵין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת, וּבְשָׁעָה שֶׁהִיא עוֹבֶרֶת לְשַׁמֵּשׁ אֶת בֵּיתָהּ.
phrases.en: And even a woman with a fixed menstrual cycle engages in intercourse while using examination cloths to ascertain whether her menstrual flow began, except for a woman after childbirth who is observing the period of the blood of purity, and a virgin whose blood is ritually pure for four days after engaging in intercourse for the first time. And she is required to examine herself twice each day: In the morning, to ascertain if she menstruated during the night, and at twilight, to ascertain if she menstruated during the day. And she is also required to examine herself at a time that she is about to engage in intercourse with her husband.

phrases.he: יְתֵרָה עֲלֵיהֶן כֹּהֲנוֹת, בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁהֵן אוֹכְלוֹת בַּתְּרוּמָה.
phrases.en: The obligation of women of priestly families is greater than that of other women, as they are also required to examine themselves when they seek to partake of teruma.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף בִּשְׁעַת עֲבָרָתָן מִלֶּאֱכֹל בַּתְּרוּמָה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: Even when they conclude partaking of teruma they are required to examine themselves, in order to ascertain whether they experienced bleeding while partaking of teruma.

phrases.he: כָּל הַיָּד הַמַּרְבָּה לִבְדֹּק בְּנָשִׁים, מְשֻׁבַּחַת. וּבַאֲנָשִׁים, תִּקָּצֵץ.
phrases.en: With regard to any hand that is diligent to examine bodily emissions to ascertain ritual impurity, among women such a hand is praiseworthy. But among men such a hand should be severed, as this action is apt to lead to a seminal emission for naught.

phrases.he: הַחֵרֶשֶׁת וְהַשּׁוֹטָה וְהַסּוּמָא וְשֶׁנִּטְרְפָה דַעְתָּהּ, אִם יֶשׁ לָהֶן פִּקְחוֹת, מְתַקְּנוֹת אוֹתָן וְהֵן אוֹכְלוֹת בַּתְּרוּמָה.
phrases.en: In the case of a woman who is deaf [haḥereshet], or an imbecile, or blind, or who went insane, and is therefore unable to examine herself reliably, if such women have competent friends, those friends prepare them by examining them and immersing them in a ritual bath. And on that basis the incompetent women may partake of teruma after the sun sets.

phrases.he: דֶּרֶךְ בְּנוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל, מְשַׁמְּשׁוֹת בִּשְׁנֵי עִדִּים, אֶחָד לוֹ וְאֶחָד לָהּ.
phrases.en: It is the custom of Jewish women that they engage in intercourse with their husbands while using two examination cloths, one for the husband, to see if there is any of the wife’s blood on him after intercourse, and one for her, to ascertain after intercourse whether her menstrual flow has begun.

phrases.he: הַצְּנוּעוֹת מְתַקְּנוֹת לָהֶן שְׁלִישִׁי, לְתַקֵּן אֶת הַבָּיִת
phrases.en: And the modest women prepare a third examination cloth, to examine themselves and prepare the pubic area for intercourse.

phrases.he: נִמְצָא עַל שֶׁלּוֹ, טְמֵאִין וְחַיָּבִין קָרְבָּן.
phrases.en: If blood was found on his cloth, the woman and her husband are both ritually impure for seven days, in accordance with the halakha of a menstruating woman and of one who engages in intercourse with a menstruating woman, and are each liable to bring a sin offering for unwittingly performing an action punishable with excision from the World-to-Come [karet].

phrases.he: נִמְצָא עַל שֶׁלָּהּ אוֹתְיוֹם, טְמֵאִין וְחַיָּבִין קָרְבָּן.
phrases.en: If blood was found on her cloth immediately [otyom] after intercourse, the woman and her husband are likewise ritually impure for seven days and are each liable to bring a sin offering.

phrases.he: נִמְצָא עַל שֶׁלָּהּ לְאַחַר זְמַן, טְמֵאִים מִסָּפֵק וּפְטוּרִים מִן הַקָּרְבָּן
phrases.en: If blood was found on her cloth after time passed, they are both ritually impure due to uncertainty, as it is possible that the blood appeared only after intercourse, and they are exempt from bringing the sin offering.

phrases.he: אֵיזֶהוּ אַחַר זְמַן. כְּדֵי שֶׁתֵּרֵד מִן הַמִּטָּה וְתָדִיחַ פָּנֶיהָ.
phrases.en: What is considered as being: After time passed? It is a period of time equivalent to the time needed for her to descend from the bed and rinse her face, a euphemism for her pubic area.

phrases.he: וְאַחַר כָּךְ, מְטַמְּאָה מֵעֵת לְעֵת וְאֵינָהּ מְטַמְּאָה אֶת בּוֹעֲלָהּ.
phrases.en: And afterward, she retroactively transmits impurity to all ritually pure items with which she came into contact for the preceding twenty-four-hour period, by rabbinic law, but she does not transmit seven-day impurity to the man with whom she engaged in intercourse. He is impure with this impurity by rabbinic law only until the evening, like one who came in contact with a menstruating woman.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, אַף מְטַמְּאָה אֶת בּוֹעֲלָהּ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says: In the case where blood was found on her cloth after time passed, she even transmits seven-day impurity by rabbinic law to the man with whom she engaged in intercourse.

phrases.he: וּמוֹדִים חֲכָמִים לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא בְּרוֹאָה כֶתֶם, שֶׁמְּטַמְּאָה אֶת בּוֹעֲלָהּ
phrases.en: The mishna concludes: The Rabbis concede to Rabbi Akiva in the case of a woman who sees a blood stain and then engages in intercourse, that she transmits seven-day impurity to the man with whom she engaged in intercourse, although this impurity also applies by rabbinic law.

phrases.he: כָּל הַנָּשִׁים בְּחֶזְקַת טָהֳרָה לְבַעֲלֵיהֶן.
phrases.en: All women have the presumptive status of purity for their husbands, and therefore one is not required to ascertain whether his wife is ritually pure before engaging in intercourse with her.

phrases.he: הַבָּאִין מִן הַדֶּרֶךְ, נְשֵׁיהֶן לָהֶן בְּחֶזְקַת טָהֳרָה.
phrases.en: Even with regard to husbands returning from a journey, if their wives were ritually pure when they left, their wives have the presumptive status of purity for them.
