phrases.en: The assumption is that the impurity was not found because the examination was not conducted properly. And the Rabbis say: One continues searching the relevant area until he reaches bedrock or virgin soil, beneath which there is certainly no ritual impurity.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, בּוֹדֵק עַד שֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לְסֶלַע אוֹ לִבְתוּלָה:
phrases.en: If no ritual impurity is found at that stage, presumably an animal dragged the olive-bulk of the corpse from beneath the pile, and the pile of rocks is pure.

phrases.he: שִׁבְעָה סַמָּנִין מַעֲבִירִין עַל הַכֶּתֶם.
phrases.en: There are seven substances that one applies to the stain on a garment to ascertain whether it is a blood stain or a dye, as these seven substances remove the blood.

phrases.he: רֹק תָּפֵל, וּמֵי גְרִיסִין, וּמֵי רַגְלַיִם, וְנֶתֶר, וּבוֹרִית, קְמוּנְיָא, וְאֶשְׁלָג.
phrases.en: They are: Tasteless saliva, and liquid from split beans, and urine, and natron, and borit, Cimolian earth [kamonya], and potash [eshlag].

phrases.he: הִטְבִּילוֹ וְעָשָׂה עַל גַּבָּיו טָהֳרוֹת, הֶעֱבִיר עָלָיו שִׁבְעָה סַמָּנִין וְלֹא עָבַר, הֲרֵי זֶה צֶבַע, הַטָּהֳרוֹת טְהוֹרוֹת, וְאֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְהַטְבִּיל.
phrases.en: If one immersed the garment with the stain whose nature is unknown and then handled ritually pure items with the garment, and then applied these seven substances to the stain and it did not disappear, that stain is presumably from a dye, and therefore the ritually pure items are pure, and he need not immerse the garment again, as there is no impurity.

phrases.he: עָבַר אוֹ שֶׁדֵּהָה, הֲרֵי זֶה כֶתֶם, וְהַטָּהֳרוֹת טְמֵאוֹת, וְצָרִיךְ לְהַטְבִּיל
phrases.en: If the stain disappeared or if it faded, that is a blood stain, and the ritually pure items that he handled are impure, and he must immerse the garment again.

phrases.he: אֵיזֶהוּ רֹק תָּפֵל, כֹּל שֶׁלֹּא טָעַם כְּלוּם.
phrases.en: What is tasteless saliva? It is saliva that emerges from the mouth of any person who tasted nothing all night, when he first awakens in the morning.

phrases.he: מֵי גְרִיסִין, לְעִסַּת גְּרִיסִין שֶׁל פּוֹל, חֲלוּקַת נָפֶשׁ. מֵי רַגְלַיִם, שֶׁהֶחֱמִיצוּ.
phrases.en: Liquid from split beans is created through the chewing of split beans that divided naturally, not by human hand, which is then applied to the stain. The urine that is an effective detergent is specifically urine that fermented for three days.

phrases.he: וְצָרִיךְ לְכַסְכֵּס שָׁלשׁ פְּעָמִים לְכָל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד.
phrases.en: And one must rub each and every one of the substances three times over the stain, and one must apply them separately, and one must apply them in the order they are listed in the mishna.

phrases.he: הֶעֶבִירָן שֶׁלֹּא כְסִדְרָן, אוֹ שֶׁהֶעֱבִיר שִׁבְעָה סַמָּנִין כְּאַחַת, לֹא עָשָׂה וְלֹא כְלוּם
phrases.en: If one applied them in a manner that is not in their prescribed order, or if one applied all seven substances simultaneously, he has done nothing. One cannot determine by means of that examination whether it is blood or a dye.

phrases.he: כָּל אִשָּׁה שֶׁיֶּשׁ לָהּ וֶסֶת, דַּיָּהּ שְׁעָתָהּ.
phrases.en: For any woman who has a fixed menstrual cycle that is not time dependent, but is dependent on a physical sensation, her time is sufficient, i.e.

phrases.he: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן הַוְּסָתוֹת, מְפַהֶקֶת, וּמְעַטֶּשֶׁת, וְחוֹשֶׁשֶׁת בְּפִי כְרֵסָהּ, וּבְשִׁפּוּלֵי מֵעֶיהָ, וְשׁוֹפַעַת, וּכְמִין צְמַרְמוֹרוֹת אוֹחֲזִין אוֹתָהּ, וְכֵן כַּיּוֹצֵא בָהֶן.
phrases.en: she does not transmit ritual impurity retroactively, for twenty-four hours or until the last time she examined herself (see 2a). And these are the fixed menstrual cycles based on sensation: When a woman menstruates after she yawns [mefaheket], or after she sneezes, or after she senses pain near her stomach or in her lower abdomen, or after she secretes a discharge, or after a type of feverish shuddering [tzemarmorot] overtakes her. And likewise the same applies with regard to any sensation of the like.

phrases.he: וְכֹל שֶׁקָּבְעָה לָהּ שָׁלשׁ פְּעָמִים, הֲרֵי זוֹ וָסֶת
phrases.en: And in the case of any woman who establishes a pattern for herself by experiencing such a sensation three times before the onset of menstruation, that is a fixed menstrual cycle.

phrases.he: הָיְתָה לְמוּדָה לִהְיוֹת רוֹאָה בִתְחִלַּת הַוְּסָתוֹת, כָּל הַטָּהֳרוֹת שֶׁעָשְׂתָה בְתוֹךְ הַוְּסָתוֹת, טְמֵאוֹת.
phrases.en: If a woman was accustomed to see the flow of blood at the beginning of the sensation that accompanies her fixed cycle, even if on one occasion she happened to experience bleeding only at the end of the sensation, all the ritually pure items that she handled within the duration of that sensation that accompanies her fixed cycle are ritually impure.

phrases.he: בְּסוֹף הַוְּסָתוֹת, כָּל הַטָּהֳרוֹת שֶׁעָשְׂתָה בְתוֹךְ הַוְּסָתוֹת, טְהוֹרוֹת.
phrases.en: If the woman was accustomed to experience bleeding at the end of the sensation that accompanies her fixed cycle, all the ritually pure items that she handled within the duration of that sensation that accompanies her fixed cycle are pure.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אַף יָמִים וְשָׁעוֹת, וְסָתוֹת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yosei says: Even specific days and specific hours determine a fixed menstrual cycle: If a woman was accustomed to see the flow of blood on a certain day of the month at sunrise, it is prohibited for her to engage in intercourse with her husband only at sunrise; but during the night before and the following day, it is permitted for her to engage in intercourse.

phrases.he: הָיְתָה לְמוּדָה לִהְיוֹת רוֹאָה עִם הָנֵץ הַחַמָּה, אֵינָהּ אֲסוּרָה אֶלָּא עִם הָנֵץ הַחַמָּה.
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, כָּל הַיּוֹם שֶׁלָּהּ:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: Once sunrise passed and she did not menstruate, the entire day is hers and she may engage in intercourse, in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yosei; but contrary to the opinion of Rabbi Yosei, intercourse the night before is prohibited.

phrases.he: הָיְתָה לְמוּדָה לִהְיוֹת רוֹאָה יוֹם חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר וְשִׁנְּתָה לִהְיוֹת רוֹאָה לְיוֹם עֶשְׂרִים, זֶה וָזֶה אֲסוּרִין.
phrases.en: If the woman was accustomed to see the flow of blood on the fifteenth day and she deviated from the norm to see the flow of blood on the twentieth day, then on both this day, the fifteenth, and that day, the twentieth, it is prohibited for her to engage in intercourse.

phrases.he: שִׁנְּתָה פַעֲמַיִם לְיוֹם עֶשְׂרִים, זֶה וָזֶה אֲסוּרִין.
phrases.en: If she deviated from the norm twice, then on both this day, the fifteenth, and that day, the twentieth, it is likewise prohibited for her to engage in intercourse.

phrases.he: שִׁנְּתָה שָׁלשׁ פְּעָמִים לְיוֹם עֶשְׂרִים, הֻתַּר חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר וְקָבְעָה לָהּ יוֹם עֶשְׂרִים, שֶׁאֵין אִשָּׁה קוֹבַעַת לָהּ וֶסֶת, עַד שֶׁתִּקְבָּעֶנָּה שָׁלשׁ פְּעָמִים.
phrases.en: If she deviated from the norm to see the flow of blood on the twentieth day three times, it becomes permitted for her to engage in intercourse on the fifteenth, and she has established the twentieth day for herself as the day of her fixed menstrual cycle, as a woman establishes a fixed menstrual cycle only after she establishes it three times.

phrases.he: וְאֵינָהּ מִטַּהֶרֶת הַוֶּסֶת, עַד שֶׁתֵּעָקֵר מִמֶּנָּה שָׁלשׁ פְּעָמִים
phrases.en: And a woman is purified from the existing fixed menstrual cycle, in the sense that intercourse is permitted on that day, only when she has been displaced from that day three times.

phrases.he: נָשִׁים בִּבְתוּלֵיהֶם כַּגְּפָנִים. יֵשׁ גֶּפֶן שֶׁיֵּינָהּ אָדֹם, וְיֵשׁ גֶּפֶן שֶׁיֵּינָהּ שָׁחֹר, וְיֵשׁ גֶּפֶן שֶׁיֵּינָהּ מְרֻבֶּה, וְיֵשׁ גֶּפֶן שֶׁיֵּינָהּ מֻעָט.
phrases.en: Women, with regard to the blood that flows when their hymens are ruptured, are like grapevines: There is a vine that produces wine that is red, and there is a vine that produces wine that is black; and there is a vine that produces wine in abundance, and there is a vine that produces only a meager amount of wine. Rabbi Yehuda says: In every vine, there are grapes fit to produce wine, but any vine in which there are no grapes fit to produce wine, this is a dry vine [durkati].

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, כָּל גֶּפֶן יֶשׁ בָּהּ יַיִן.
phrases.en: Likewise, any woman who experiences bleeding is capable of giving birth, whereas one who does not experience bleeding is like a dry vine, unable to give birth.

phrases.he: וְשֶׁאֵין בָּהּ יַיִן, הֲרֵי זֶה דּוֹרְקְטִי
תִּינוֹקֶת שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעַ זְמַנָּהּ לִרְאוֹת וְנִסֵּת,
phrases.en: In the case of a young girl whose time to see a menstrual flow, i.e.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, נוֹתְנִין לָהּ אַרְבָּעָה לֵילוֹת.
phrases.en: the age of puberty, has not yet arrived, and she married and engaged in intercourse and her hymen was torn, Beit Shammai say: The Sages give her four nights after intercourse during which the blood is attributed to the torn hymen and she remains ritually pure. Thereafter, any blood is assumed to be menstrual blood and renders her impure.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, עַד שֶׁתִּחְיֶה הַמַּכָּה.
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel say: The blood is attributed to the torn hymen until the wound heals.

phrases.he: הִגִּיעַ זְמַנָּהּ לִרְאוֹת וְנִסֵּת,
phrases.en: In the case of a young woman whose time to see a menstrual flow has arrived but she has not yet begun to menstruate, and she married and engaged in intercourse and her hymen was torn, Beit Shammai say: The Sages give her the first night during which the blood is attributed to the torn hymen.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, נוֹתְנִין לָהּ לַיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹן.
phrases.en: Thereafter, any blood is assumed to be menstrual blood.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, עַד מוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת, אַרְבָּעָה לֵילוֹת.
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel say: The blood is attributed to the torn hymen until the conclusion of Shabbat, and she may engage in intercourse with her husband for four nights, as it was customary for a virgin to marry on Wednesday.

phrases.he: רָאֲתָה וְעוֹדָהּ בְּבֵית אָבִיהָ,
בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, נוֹתְנִין לָהּ בְּעִילַת מִצְוָה.
phrases.en: In the case of a young woman who saw menstrual blood before marriage while she was still in her father’s house, Beit Shammai say: The Sages give her permission to engage only in relations that consummate a marriage, which are a mitzva, after which she is ritually impure due to the blood.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, כָּל הַלַּיְלָה כֻּלָּהּ:
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel say: The husband and wife may engage even in several acts of intercourse, as any blood seen throughout the entire night is attributed to the torn hymen.

phrases.he: נִדָּה שֶׁבָּדְקָה עַצְמָהּ יוֹם שְׁבִיעִי שַׁחֲרִית וּמָצְאתָה טְהוֹרָה, וּבֵין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת לֹא הִפְרִישָׁה, וּלְאַחַר יָמִים בָּדְקָה וּמָצְאתָה טְמֵאָה, הֲרֵי הִיא בְחֶזְקַת טָהֳרָה.
phrases.en: In the case of a menstruating woman who examined herself on the seventh day of menstruation in the morning and found that she is ritually pure and eligible to immerse in a ritual bath that evening, but during twilight of the seventh day she did not perform an examination that marks the transition between the days when she has a flow of blood and the days when she no longer has a flow of blood but immersed despite not having performed the examination, and after several days she examined herself and found that she is ritually impure, the presumptive status of that woman is one of ritual purity from the time of her immersion until her examination, and all ritually pure items that she handled in the interim remain pure.

phrases.he: בָּדְקָה עַצְמָהּ בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי בְּשַׁחֲרִית וּמָצְאתָה טְמֵאָה, וּבֵין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת לֹא הִפְרִישָׁה, וּלְאַחַר זְמַן בָּדְקָה וּמָצְאתָה טְהוֹרָה, הֲרֵי זוֹ בְחֶזְקַת טֻמְאָה, וּמְטַמְּאָה מֵעֵת לְעֵת וּמִפְּקִידָה לִפְקִידָה.
phrases.en: If she examined herself on the seventh day of menstruation in the morning and found that she is ritually impure, i.e., her menstrual flow continued, and during twilight of the seventh day she did not perform an examination to confirm the transition from ritual impurity to ritual purity but immersed nonetheless, and after several days she examined herself and found that she is ritually pure, the presumptive status of that woman is one of ritual impurity from the time of her immersion until her examination, and all ritually pure items that she handled in the interim are impure. Since she found blood during her last examination in her days of menstruation, the concern is that the flow of blood continued during the days that followed, and therefore her immersion on the eve of the eighth day was ineffective.

phrases.he: וְאִם יֶשׁ לָהּ וֶסֶת, דַּיָּהּ שְׁעָתָהּ.
phrases.en: In a case where there was no blood found during the examination on the seventh morning and she did not examine herself during twilight, and several days later she discovered blood, where the mishna says that a woman’s presumptive status is one of ritual purity, that is the halakha only for the days following immersion.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, כֹּל שֶׁלֹּא הִפְרִישָׁה בְטָהֳרָה מִן הַמִּנְחָה וּלְמַעְלָה, הֲרֵי זוֹ בְחֶזְקַת טֻמְאָה.
phrases.en: But she transmits ritual impurity to the ritually pure items that she handled before the examination in which she found blood for a twenty-four-hour period and from examination to examination, in accordance with the halakha of a woman who experiences bleeding (see 2a). And if she has a fixed menstrual cycle, on the day that she examined herself and found blood, her time is sufficient, i.e., it is assumed that the bleeding began then, and she does not transmit impurity retroactively.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אֲפִלּוּ בַשְּׁנִיָּה לְנִדָּתָהּ בָּדְקָה וּמָצְאתָה טְהוֹרָה, וּבֵין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת לֹא הִפְרִישָׁה, וּלְאַחַר זְמַן בָּדְקָה וּמָצְאָה טְמֵאָה, הֲרֵי זוֹ בְחֶזְקַת טָהֳרָה:
phrases.en: And Rabbi Yehuda says: With regard to any woman who did not perform the examination marking her transition from ritual impurity to ritual purity on the seventh day from minḥa time onward, even if she performed an examination and found no blood that morning, the presumptive status of that woman is one of ritual impurity. And the Rabbis say: Even if on the second day of her menstruation she performed the examination and found that she is ritually pure, and she did not perform the examination marking her transition from ritual impurity to ritual purity on the seventh day during twilight, and after several days she examined herself and found that she is ritually impure, the presumptive status of that woman is one of ritual purity from the time of her immersion until her examination.

phrases.he: הַזָּב וְהַזָּבָה שֶׁבָּדְקוּ עַצְמָן בְּיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן וּמָצְאוּ טָהוֹר, וּבַיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי וּמָצְאוּ טָהוֹר, וּשְׁאָר יָמִים שֶׁבֵּינְתַיִם לֹא בָדְקוּ,
phrases.en: With regard to a zav and a zava, who are required to count and examine themselves on each of seven clean days before purification in a ritual bath, who examined themselves on the first day and found themselves ritually pure, i.e.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, הֲרֵי הֵן בְּחֶזְקַת טָהֳרָה.
phrases.en: with no blood, and they examined themselves on the seventh day and found themselves ritually pure, and on the rest of the intervening days they did not examine themselves, Rabbi Eliezer says: The presumptive status of the zav and the zava is one of ritual purity.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, אֵין לָהֶם אֶלָּא יוֹם רִאשׁוֹן וְיוֹם שְׁבִיעִי בִלְבָד.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says: In that case, the zav and the zava have counted only the first day and the seventh day, two of the seven clean days, and they must count another five days to complete the tally.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, אֵין לָהֶם אֶלָּא יוֹם שְׁבִיעִי בִלְבָד:
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says: The zav and the zava have counted only the seventh day, and they must count another six days to complete the tally.

phrases.he: הַזָּב וְהַזָּבָה וְהַנִּדָּה וְהַיּוֹלֶדֶת וְהַמְצֹרָע שֶׁמֵּתוּ, מְטַמְּאִין בְּמַשָּׂא עַד שֶׁיִּמֹּק הַבָּשָׂר.
phrases.en: The corpses of a zav, and a zava, and a menstruating woman, and a woman after childbirth, and a leper, who died, transmit ritual impurity by carrying their corpses, until the flesh decays.

phrases.he: נָכְרִי שֶׁמֵּת, טָהוֹר מִלְּטַמֵּא בְמַשָּׂא.
phrases.en: With regard to the corpse of a gentile who died, although when alive he transmits impurity like a zav, once he dies he is ritually pure and is prevented from transmitting impurity.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, כָּל הַנָּשִׁים מֵתוֹת נִדּוֹת.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: The status of all women when they die is as though they were menstruating women at the time of death. Therefore, the garments that they were wearing before they died are impure and require immersion.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, אֵין נִדָּה אֶלָּא שֶׁמֵּתָה נִדָּה:
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel say: Only a woman who died with the impurity of a menstruating woman has the status of a menstruating woman after death.

phrases.he: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁמֵּתָה וְיָצָא מִמֶּנָּה רְבִיעִית דָּם, מְטַמְּאָה מִשּׁוּם כֶּתֶם, וּמְטַמְּאָה בְאֹהֶל.
phrases.en: With regard to a woman who died, and after her death a quarter-log of blood emerged from her body, although the blood emerged after death, it transmits ritual impurity by touching and carrying, due to the impurity of the spot of blood of a menstruating woman.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אֵינָהּ מְטַמְּאָה מִשּׁוּם כֶּתֶם, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנֶּעֱקַר מִשֶּׁמֵּתָה.
phrases.en: This impurity as blood of menstruation applies to any amount of blood she emits, despite the halakha that generally, the blood of a corpse transmits impurity only if it is at least a quarter-log in volume. And as it is a quarter-log of blood, it transmits impurity in a tent, as it is the blood of a corpse.

phrases.he: וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּיוֹשֶׁבֶת עַל מַשְׁבֵּר וּמֵתָה וְיָצָא מִמֶּנָּה רְבִיעִית דָּם, שֶׁהִיא מְטַמְּאָה מִשּׁוּם כֶּתֶם.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: That quarter-log of blood does not transmit impurity due to the impurity of the spot of blood of a menstruating woman, because that blood was displaced after she died. And Rabbi Yehuda concedes in the case of a woman who is sitting in childbirth on the travailing chair [mashber] and she died, and a quarter-log of blood emerged from her body, that this blood transmits ritual impurity due to the impurity of the spot of blood of a menstruating woman.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, לְפִיכָךְ אֵינָהּ מְטַמְּאָה בְאֹהֶל:
phrases.en: In that case, the blood was displaced while she was still alive. Rabbi Yosei said: For that reason, that quarter-log of blood does not transmit impurity in a tent, as it did not come from a corpse.

phrases.he: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיוּ אוֹמְרִים, הַיּוֹשֶׁבֶת עַל דַּם טֹהַר, הָיְתָה מְעָרָה מַיִם לַפֶּסַח.
phrases.en: Initially the Sages would say, with regard to a woman who gave birth and observed the seven or fourteen days of impurity for a male or female child, respectively, and then immersed in a ritual bath and who is observing the period of the blood of purity, that she would pour water from a vessel in her hands to rinse the Paschal offering. Although it is permitted for such a woman to engage in intercourse with her husband, her halakhic status is like that of one who immersed that day and the sun has not yet set. She therefore assumes second-degree ritual impurity and confers third-degree ritual impurity upon teruma with which she comes into contact. Consequently, she may touch the vessel, as second-degree ritual impurity does not render a vessel impure.

phrases.he: חָזְרוּ לוֹמַר, הֲרֵי הִיא כְמַגַּע טְמֵא מֵת לַקָּדָשִׁים, כְּדִבְרֵי בֵית הִלֵּל.
phrases.en: She may not touch the water, as it is designated for rinsing the Paschal offering and therefore it is treated with the sanctity of sacrificial food, which is rendered impure by second-degree ritual impurity. The Sages then said: Her status is like that of one who came into contact with one impure with impurity imparted by a corpse, i.e., one with first-degree ritual impurity, who renders consecrated items impure. But with regard to all non-sacred items, even non-sacred items treated with the sanctity of sacrificial food, such as the water used to rinse the Paschal offering, she has second-degree ritual impurity.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, אַף כִּטְמֵא מֵת:
phrases.en: Consequently, it is permitted for her to touch not only the vessel, but the water inside it as well, in accordance with the statement of Beit Hillel. Beit Shammai say: The status of the woman is even like that of one who is impure due to contact with a corpse, who is a primary source of ritual impurity and renders even a non-sacred vessel impure.

phrases.he: וּמוֹדִים שֶׁהִיא אוֹכֶלֶת בַּמַּעֲשֵׂר, וְקוֹצָה לָהּ חַלָּה, וּמַקֶּפֶת וְקוֹרְאָה לָהּ שֵׁם.
phrases.en: And Beit Shammai concede to Beit Hillel that a woman observing the days of purity partakes of second-tithe produce, as it is permitted for one who immersed that day to eat second-tithe produce. And she separates part of her dough as ḥalla, and she draws the vessel with the part of the dough that she separated near the rest of the dough, and she designates it with the name of ḥalla.

phrases.he: וְאִם נָפַל מֵרֻקָּהּ וּמִדַּם טָהֳרָהּ עַל כִּכָּר שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, שֶׁהוּא טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: And Beit Shammai further concede to Beit Hillel that if a drop from her saliva or from the blood of purity fell onto a loaf of teruma, the loaf is ritually pure, as any liquid discharged from the body of one who immersed that day is ritually pure. There is another dispute between the tanna’im with regard to a woman who completed her days of purity.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, צְרִיכָה טְבִילָה בָּאַחֲרוֹנָה.
phrases.en: Beit Shammai say: Her immersion at the end of the days of impurity does not render it permitted for her to enter the Temple or to partake of teruma; rather, she requires immersion even at the conclusion of the days of purity.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, אֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה טְבִילָה בָּאֲחֲרוֹנָה:
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel say: She does not require immersion at the conclusion of the days of purity to render it permitted for her to partake of teruma, as the immersion at the end of the days of impurity is sufficient.

phrases.he: הָרוֹאָה יוֹם אַחַד עָשָׂר וְטָבְלָה לָעֶרֶב וְשִׁמְּשָׁה,
phrases.en: There is a dispute with regard to a woman who sees blood on the eleventh day, which is the final day of the period fit for the flow of a zava. It is permitted for her to engage in intercourse with her husband after observing one clean day corresponding to the one day that she saw blood, but in this case, she failed to observe one clean day.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, מְטַמְּאִין מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב, וְחַיָּבִין בַּקָּרְבָּן.
phrases.en: Rather, she immersed in a ritual bath that evening, the eve of the twelfth day, and then engaged in intercourse with her husband. Beit Shammai say: Since she did not observe that corresponding clean day, she retains the status of a zava. Therefore both she, the zava, and her husband, who engaged in intercourse with a zava, transmit impurity to items designated for lying or sitting, to the extent that these transmit impurity to food and drink that came in contact with them, and in her case, to people as well.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, פְּטוּרִין מִן הַקָּרְבָּן.
phrases.en: And each of them is liable to bring a sin offering for participating in intercourse involving a zava. And Beit Hillel say: Although they transmit impurity to items designated for lying or sitting, they are exempt from bringing the sin offering.

phrases.he: טָבְלָה בַיוֹם שֶׁלְּאַחֲרָיו וְשִׁמְּשָׁה אֶת בֵּיתָהּ וְאַחַר כָּךְ רָאֲתָה,
phrases.en: Since the twelfth day is unfit for the flow of a zava, and even if she were to experience bleeding on the eleventh, twelfth, and thirteenth days she would not become a greater zava, one who experiences bleeding on the eleventh does not need to observe a corresponding clean day. If the woman immersed on the day following the eleventh day and she engaged in intercourse with the man of her house, i.e.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, מְטַמְּאִין מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב וּפְטוּרִים מִן הַקָּרְבָּן.
phrases.en: her husband, on that twelfth day and then saw blood, Beit Shammai say: They transmit impurity to items designated for lying or sitting by rabbinic law, as the Sages issued a decree of impurity in the case when the second day is the twelfth day, due to a case when the second day is within the eleven days fit for the flow of a zava. And they are exempt from bringing the sin offering, as she observed part of the twelfth day, and the bleeding she experienced after engaging in intercourse, which occurred during her period of menstruation, is not fit to be appended to the discharge of the zava on the eleventh day.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, הֲרֵי זֶה גַרְגְּרָן.
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel say: That husband is a glutton, as he could not wait for the conclusion of the twelfth day before engaging in intercourse. Nevertheless, the Sages did not issue a decree of impurity.

phrases.he: וּמוֹדִים בְּרוֹאָה בְתוֹךְ אַחַד עָשָׂר יוֹם וְטָבְלָה לָעֶרֶב וְשִׁמְּשָׁה, שֶׁמְּטַמְּאִין מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב וְחַיָּבִין בַּקָּרְבָּן.
phrases.en: And Beit Hillel concede to Beit Shammai in a case where the woman sees blood in the midst of the eleven-day period, and she immersed in the evening and engaged in intercourse with her husband without observing a corresponding clean day, that they transmit impurity to items designated for lying or sitting. And each of them is liable to bring a sin offering for participating in intercourse involving a zava. If she saw blood in the midst of the eleven days and observed part of a corresponding clean day and immersed on the day following the day that she saw blood and engaged in intercourse with her husband, that is wayward conduct, as the possibility exists that she will experience bleeding after intercourse that will be appended to the bleeding of the previous day, rendering her a zava and disqualifying the immersion.

phrases.he: טָבְלָה בַיּוֹם שֶׁלְּאַחֲרָיו וְשִׁמְּשָׁה, הֲרֵי זוֹ תַרְבּוּת רָעָה, וּמַגָּעָן וּבְעִילָתָן תְּלוּיִים
phrases.en: And the status of ritually impure items with which they came into contact and the status of their intercourse is contingent upon whether she experiences bleeding on the day of her immersion, in which case the ritually pure items become impure and they are liable to bring a sin offering, or whether she does not experience bleeding that day, in which case the ritually pure items remain pure and the woman and man are exempt from bringing a sin offering.

phrases.he: כָּל מַשְׁקֶה שֶׁתְּחִלָּתוֹ לְרָצוֹן אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין סוֹפוֹ לְרָצוֹן, אוֹ שֶׁסּוֹפוֹ לְרָצוֹן אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין תְּחִלָּתוֹ לְרָצוֹן, הֲרֵי זֶה בְכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: Any liquid which was desired at the beginning though it was not desired at the end, or which was desired at the end though it was not desired at the beginning, comes under the law of "if water be put.

phrases.he: מַשְׁקִין טְמֵאִים מְטַמְּאִין לְרָצוֹן וְשֶׁלֹּא לְרָצוֹן
phrases.en: Unclean liquids render unclean whether [their action] is desired or is not desired.

phrases.he: הַמַּרְעִיד אֶת הָאִילָן לְהַשִּׁיר מִמֶּנּוּ אֳכָלִין אוֹ אֶת הַטֻּמְאָה, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן. לְהַשִּׁיר מִמֶּנּוּ מַשְׁקִין,
phrases.en: If one shook a tree in order to cause food or something unclean to fall down from it, [the rain water dropping down from it] does not come under the law of ‘if water be put.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, הַיּוֹצְאִין וְאֶת שֶׁבּוֹ, בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: If [he shook the tree] in order to cause liquids to fall down from it: Bet Shammai says: both [the liquids] that fall down and [the liquids] that remain [on the tree] come under the law of ‘if water be put.

phrases.he: בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, הַיּוֹצְאִין, בְּכִי יֻתַּן, וְאֶת שֶׁבּוֹ, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מִתְכַּוֵּן שֶׁיֵּצְאוּ מִכֻּלּוֹ:
phrases.en: But Bet Hillel say: [the liquids] that fall down come under the law of ‘if water be put’, but [the liquids] that remain [on the tree] do not come under the law of ‘if water be put,' because his intention was that [the liquids] should drop down from all the tree.

phrases.he: הַמַּרְעִיד אֶת הָאִילָן וְנָפַל עַל חֲבֵרוֹ, אוֹ סוֹכָה וְנָפְלָה עַל חֲבֶרְתָּהּ, וְתַחְתֵּיהֶן זְרָעִים אוֹ יְרָקוֹת הַמְחֻבָּרִין לַקַּרְקַע,
phrases.en: If one shook a tree and it fell on another tree, or a branch and it fell on another branch, and under them were seeds or vegetables [still] joined to the ground: Bet Shammai say: this comes under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: But Bet Hillel say: this does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: R.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ מִשּׁוּם אַבָּא יוֹסֵי חֲלֵי קוּפְרִי אִישׁ טִבְעוֹן, תְּמַהּ עַצְמְךָ אִם יֵשׁ מַשְׁקֶה טָמֵא בַתּוֹרָה, עַד שֶׁיִּתְכַּוֵּן וְיִתֵּן, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (ויקרא יא), וְכִי יֻתַּן מַיִם עַל זֶרַע:
phrases.en: Joshua said in the name of Abba Yose Holikofri a man of Tivon: Be surprised if there is any liquid that according to the Torah causes susceptibility to uncleanness except one put it on with intention, for it is said: "If water be put upon the seed."

phrases.he: הַנּוֹעֵר אֲגֻדָּה שֶׁל יָרָק וְיָרְדוּ מִצַּד הָעֶלְיוֹן לַתַּחְתּוֹן,
phrases.en: If one shook a bundle of vegetables and [water] dropped down from the upper [side] to the lower [side]: Bet Shammai say: this comes under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: But Bet Hillel say: this does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, אֵינָם בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: Bet Hillel said to Bet Shammai: if one shakes a stalk, do we fear lest water drops from one leaf on the other leaf? Bet Shammai said to them: a stalk is only one, but a bundle has many stalks.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ בֵית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי, וַהֲלֹא הַנּוֹעֵר אֶת הַקֶּלַח, חוֹשְׁשִׁין אָנוּ שֶׁמָּא יָצְאוּ מִן הֶעָלֶה לֶעָלֶה.
אָמְרוּ לָהֶן בֵּית שַׁמַּאי, שֶׁהַקֶּלַח אֶחָד, וַאֲגֻדָּה קְלָחִים הַרְבֵּה.
phrases.en: Bet Hillel said to them: behold, if one lifted a sack full of produce and put it beside the river, do we fear lest water drops from the upper [side] to the lower [side]? But if he lifted two sacks and placed them one upon the other, the lower [sack] comes under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית הִלֵּל, הֲרֵי הַמַּעֲלֶה שַׂק מָלֵא פֵרוֹת וּנְתָנוֹ עַל גַּב הַנָּהָר, חוֹשְׁשִׁין אָנוּ שֶׁמָּא יָרְדוּ מִצַּד הָעֶלְיוֹן לַתַּחְתּוֹן.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: the lower [sack] remains insusceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: אֲבָל אִם הֶעֱלָה שְׁנַיִם וּנְתָנָן זֶה עַל גַּב זֶה, הַתַּחְתּוֹן בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, הַתַּחְתּוֹן טָהוֹר:
הַמְמַחֵק אֶת הַכְּרֵישָׁה, וְהַסּוֹחֵט שְׂעָרוֹ בִּכְסוּתוֹ,
phrases.en: If one rubbed a leek or pressed his hair or his garment, Rabbi Yose says: the liquid which came out comes under the law of ‘if water be put’, but the liquid that remained does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’, because his intention was that the liquid should come out of all of it.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, הַיּוֹצְאִין בְּכִי יֻתַּן, וְאֶת שֶׁבּוֹ אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מִתְכַּוֵּן שֶׁיֵּצְאוּ מִכֻּלּוֹ:
הַנּוֹפֵחַ בַּעֲדָשִׁים לְבָדְקָן אִם יָפוֹת הֵן,
phrases.en: If one blew on lentils in order to test whether they were good: Rabbi Shimon says: this does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: But the sages say: this does come under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: If one ate sesame with his finger, with regard to the liquid that was on his hand: Rabbi Shimon says: this does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: וְהָאוֹכֵל שֻׁמְשְׁמִין בְּאֶצְבָּעוֹ, מַשְׁקִין שֶׁעַל יָדוֹ,
רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: But the sages say: this does come under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: If one hid his fruit in water from thieves, it does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: הַטּוֹמֵן פֵּרוֹתָיו בַּמַּיִם מִפְּנֵי הַגַּנָּבִים, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
מַעֲשֶׂה בְאַנְשֵׁי יְרוּשָׁלַיִם שֶׁטָּמְנוּ דְבֵלָתָן בַּמַּיִם מִפְּנֵי הַסִּיקָרִין, וְטִהֲרוּ לָהֶן חֲכָמִים.
phrases.en: Once it happened that the men of Jerusalem hid their fig cakes in water from the robbers, and the sages declared that they were not susceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: הַנּוֹתֵן פֵּרוֹתָיו בְּשִׁבֹּלֶת הַנָּהָר לַהֲבִיאָן עִמּוֹ, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן
phrases.en: If one put his fruit in the stream of a river to make it come down with him, it does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: זֵעַת בָּתִּים, בּוֹרוֹת, שִׁיחִין וּמְעָרוֹת, טְהוֹרָה. זֵעַת הָאָדָם, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: The sweat of houses, of cisterns, of ditches and caverns does not cause susceptibility to uncleanness. A man's perspiration does not cause susceptibility to uncleanness.

phrases.he: שָׁתָה מַיִם טְמֵאִין וְהִזִּיעַ, זֵעָתוֹ טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: If a man drank unclean water and perspired, his perspiration does not cause susceptibility to uncleanness.

phrases.he: בָּא בְמַיִם שְׁאוּבִים וְהִזִּיעַ, זֵעָתוֹ טְמֵאָה.
phrases.en: If he entered into drawn water and perspired, his perspiration causes susceptibility to uncleanness.

phrases.he: נִסְתַּפֵּג וְאַחַר כָּךְ הִזִּיעַ, זֵעָתוֹ טְהוֹרָה
phrases.en: If he dried himself and then perspired, his perspiration does not cause susceptibility to uncleanness.

phrases.he: מֶרְחָץ טְמֵאָה, זֵעָתָהּ טְמֵאָה. וּטְהוֹרָה, בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: The sweat of an unclean bath is unclean, But that of a clean bath comes under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: הַבְּרֵכָה שֶׁבַּבַּיִת, הַבַּיִת מַזִּיעַ מֵחֲמָתָהּ, אִם טְמֵאָה, זֵעַת כָּל הַבַּיִת שֶׁמֵּחֲמַת הַבְּרֵכָה, טְמֵאָה
phrases.en: If there was a pool in a house, the house sweats because of it if the pool was unclean, the sweat of all the house which was caused by the pool is unclean.

phrases.he: שְׁתֵּי בְרֵכוֹת, אַחַת טְהוֹרָה וְאַחַת טְמֵאָה, הַמַּזִּיעַ קָרוֹב לַטְּמֵאָה, טָמֵא. קָרוֹב לַטְּהוֹרָה, טָהוֹר. מֶחֱצָה לְמֶחֱצָה, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: Two pools, the one clean and the other unclean: The sweat near the unclean pool is unclean, And the sweat near the clean pool is clean, And what is at equal distance [from both pools] is unclean.

phrases.he: בַּרְזֶל טָמֵא שֶׁבְּלָלוֹ עִם בַּרְזֶל טָהוֹר, אִם רֹב מִן הַטָּמֵא, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: Unclean iron was smelted with clean iron: If the greater part [came] from the unclean iron, it is unclean; If the greater part [came] from the clean iron, it is clean; But if there was half of each, it is unclean.

phrases.he: וְאִם רֹב מִן הַטָּהוֹר, טָהוֹר. מֶחֱצָה לְמֶחֱצָה, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: Pots owned by Israelites and non-Jews used for passing water: If the greater part is from the unclean [urine], it is unclean; If the greater part is from the clean [urine], it is clean; But if there was half of each, it is unclean.

phrases.he: גִּסְטְרָיוֹת שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל וְנָכְרִים מַטִּילִין לְתוֹכָהּ, אִם רֹב מִן הַטָּמֵא, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: Waste-water, in which rain had fallen: If the greater part consisted of the unclean water, it is unclean; If the greater part consisted of clean water, it is clean; But if there was half of each, it is unclean.

phrases.he: וְאִם רֹב מִן הַטָּהוֹר, טָהוֹר. מֶחֱצָה לְמֶחֱצָה, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: When [is this the case]? When the waste-water came first; but if the rain water came before [the waste-water], it is unclean whatever the quantity [of the rain water].

phrases.he: מֵי שְׁפִיכוּת שֶׁיָּרְדוּ עֲלֵיהֶן מֵי גְשָׁמִים, אִם רֹב מִן הַטָּמֵא, טָמֵא.
וְאִם רֹב מִן הַטָּהוֹר, טָהוֹר. מֶחֱצָה לְמֶחֱצָה, טָמֵא.
אֵימָתַי, בִּזְמַן שֶׁקָּדְמוּ מֵי שְׁפִיכוּת.
אֲבָל אִם קָדְמוּ מֵי גְשָׁמִים, אֲפִלּוּ כָל שֶׁהֵן, לְמֵי שְׁפִיכוּת, טָמֵא
הַטּוֹרֵף אֶת גַּגּוֹ וְהַמְכַבֵּס אֶת כְּסוּתוֹ וְיָרְדוּ עֲלֵיהֶן גְּשָׁמִים, אִם רֹב מִן הַטָּמֵא, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If one flattened out his roof or washed his garment and rain came down upon it: If the greater part consisted of the unclean water, it is unclean; If the greater part consisted of the clean water, it is clean; But if there was half of each, it is unclean.

phrases.he: וְאִם רֹב מִן הַטָּהוֹר, טָהוֹר. מֶחֱצָה לְמֶחֱצָה, טָמֵא.
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אִם הוֹסִיפוּ לְנַטֵּף:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: if the dripping increased, [it is clean].

phrases.he: עִיר שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל וְנָכְרִים דָּרִים בָּהּ וְהָיָה בָהּ מֶרְחָץ מַרְחֶצֶת בְּשַׁבָּת, אִם רֹב נָכְרִים, רוֹחֵץ מִיָּד.
phrases.en: A city in which Israelites and non-Jews dwell together and there was a bathhouse working on Shabbat: If the majority [of the inhabitants] were non-Jews, one may bathe in it immediately [after the conclusion of the Shabbat]; If the majority were Israelites, one must wait until the water can be heated; If they were half and half, one must [also] wait until the water can be heated.

phrases.he: וְאִם רֹב יִשְׂרָאֵל, יַמְתִּין כְּדֵי שֶׁיֵּחַמּוּ הַחַמִּין.
מֶחֱצָה לְמֶחֱצָה, יַמְתִּין כְּדֵי שֶׁיֵּחַמּוּ הַחַמִּין.
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, בְּאַמְבָּטִי קְטַנָּה, אִם יֶשׁ בָּהּ רָשׁוּת, רוֹחֵץ בָּהּ מִיָּד:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: if the bathhouse was small and there was there a [non-Jewish] authority, one may bathe in it immediately [after the conclusion of Shabbat].

phrases.he: מָצָא בָהּ יָרָק נִמְכָּר, אִם רֹב נָכְרִים, לוֹקֵחַ מִיָּד.
phrases.en: If one found in that city vegetables sold [on Shabbat]: If the majority [of the inhabitants] were non-Jews, one may buy them immediately [after the conclusion of Shabbat]; If the majority were Israelites, one must wait until [vegetables] can arrive from the nearest place; If they were half and half, one must [also] wait until [vegetables] can arrive from the nearest place; If there was there a [non-Jewish] authority, one may buy them immediately [after the conclusion of Shabbat].

phrases.he: וְאִם רֹב יִשְׂרָאֵל, יַמְתִּין כְּדֵי שֶׁיָּבֹאוּ מִמָּקוֹם קָרוֹב.
מֶחֱצָה לְמֶחֱצָה, יַמְתִּין כְּדֵי שֶׁיָּבֹאוּ מִמָּקוֹם קָרוֹב.
וְאִם יֶשׁ בּוֹ רָשׁוּת, לוֹקֵחַ מִיָּד
מָצָא בָהּ תִּינוֹק מֻשְׁלָךְ, אִם רֹב נָכְרִים, נָכְרִי.
phrases.en: If one found [an abandoned] child there: If the majority [of the inhabitants] were non-Jews, it is considered a non-Jew; If the majority were Israelites, it is considered an Israelite; If they were half and half, it is also considered an Israelite.

phrases.he: וְאִם רֹב יִשְׂרָאֵל, יִשְׂרָאֵל. מֶחֱצָה לְמֶחֱצָה, יִשְׂרָאֵל.
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, הוֹלְכִין אַחַר רֹב הַמַּשְׁלִיכִין:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: we must consider the majority of those who abandon their children.

phrases.he: מָצָא בָהּ מְצִיאָה, אִם רֹב נָכְרִים, אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְהַכְרִיז.
phrases.en: If one found there lost property, If the majority [of the inhabitants] were non-Jews, he need not proclaim it; If the majority were Israelites, he must proclaim it; If they were half and half, he must [also] proclaim it.

phrases.he: וְאִם רֹב יִשְׂרָאֵל, צָרִיךְ לְהַכְרִיז.
phrases.en: If one found bread there we must consider who form the majority of the bakers.

phrases.he: מֶחֱצָה לְמֶחֱצָה, צָרִיךְ לְהַכְרִיז.
phrases.en: If it was bread of clean flour, we must consider who form the majority of those who eat bread of pure flour.

phrases.he: מָצָא בָהּ פַּת, הוֹלְכִין אַחַר רֹב הַנַּחְתּוֹמִין.
וְאִם הָיְתָה פַת עִסָּה, הוֹלְכִים אַחַר רֹב אוֹכְלֵי פַת עִסָּה.
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אִם הָיְתָה פַת קִבָּר, הוֹלְכִין אַחַר רֹב אוֹכְלֵי פַת קִבָּר:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: if it was coarse bread, we must consider who form the majority of those who eat coarse bread.

phrases.he: מָצָא בָהּ בָּשָׂר, הוֹלְכִין אַחַר רֹב הַטַּבָּחִים.
phrases.en: If one found meat there, we follow the majority of the butchers.

phrases.he: אִם הָיָה מְבֻשָּׁל, הוֹלְכִים אַחַר רֹב אוֹכְלֵי בָשָׂר מְבֻשָּׁל
phrases.en: If it was cooked meat, we follow the majority of those who eat cooked meat.

phrases.he: הַמּוֹצֵא פֵרוֹת בַּדֶּרֶךְ, אִם רֹב מַכְנִיסִין לְבָתֵּיהֶן, פָּטוּר. וְלִמְכֹּר בַּשּׁוּק, חַיָּב. מֶחֱצָה לְמֶחֱצָה, דְּמַאי.
phrases.en: If one found produce on the road: If the majority [of the inhabitants] gathered produce into their homes, he is exempt [from tithes]; If [the majority gathered it] for selling in the market, he is liable [for tithes]; If they were half and half, the produce is demai.

phrases.he: אוֹצָר שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל וְנָכְרִים מַטִּילִין לְתוֹכוֹ, אִם רֹב נָכְרִים, וַדַּאי.
phrases.en: A granary into which both Israelites and non-Jews put their produce, If the majority were non-Jews, [the produce must be considered] certainly untithed; If the majority were Israelites, [it must be considered] demai; If they were half and half, [it must be considered] certainly untithed, the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.he: וְאִם רֹב יִשְׂרָאֵל, דְּמַאי.
מֶחֱצָה לְמֶחֱצָה, וַדַּאי, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אֲפִלּוּ כֻלָּם נָכְרִים וְיִשְׂרָאֵל אֶחָד מַטִּיל לְתוֹכוֹ, דְּמַאי:
phrases.en: But the sages say: even if they were all non-Jews, and only one Israelite put his produce into the granary, [it must be considered] demai.

phrases.he: פֵּרוֹת שְׁנִיָּה שֶׁרַבּוּ עַל שֶׁל שְׁלִישִׁית, וְשֶׁל שְׁלִישִׁית עַל שֶׁל רְבִיעִית, וְשֶׁל רְבִיעִית עַל שֶׁל חֲמִישִׁית, וְשֶׁל חֲמִישִׁית עַל שֶׁל שִׁשִּׁית, וְשֶׁל שִׁשִּׁית עַל שֶׁל שְׁבִיעִית, וְשֶׁל שְׁבִיעִית עַל שֶׁל מוֹצָאֵי שְׁבִיעִית, הוֹלְכִין אַחַר הָרֹב. מֶחֱצָה לְמֶחֱצָה, לְהַחֲמִיר:
phrases.en: If the produce of the second year exceeded in quantity the produce of the third year, or the produce of the third year exceeded the produce of the fourth year, or the produce of the fourth year exceeded the produce of the fifth year, or the produce of the fifth year exceeded the produce of the sixth year, or the produce of the sixth year exceeded the produce of the seventh year, or the produce of the seventh year exceeded the produce of the year after the conclusion of the seventh year, we follow the majority. If half and half, the rule is stringent.

phrases.he: שַׂק שֶׁהוּא מָלֵא פֵרוֹת וּנְתָנוֹ עַל גַּב הַנָּהָר, אוֹ עַל פִּי הַבּוֹר, אוֹ עַל מַעֲלוֹת הַמְּעָרָה, וְשָׁאֲבוּ, כֹּל שֶׁשָּׁאֲבוּ, בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: If a sack full of produce was put by the side of a river or by the side of the mouth of a cistern or on the steps of a cavern, and [the produce] absorbed water, all [the produce] which absorbed the water comes under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, כֹּל שֶׁהוּא כְנֶגֶד הַמַּיִם, בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: all [the produce] which faced the water comes under the law of ‘if water be put’, but all [the produce] which did not face the water does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: וְכֹל שֶׁאֵינוֹ כְנֶגֶד הַמַּיִם, אֵינוֹ בְּכִי יֻתַּן
חָבִית שֶׁהִיא מְלֵאָה פֵרוֹת וּנְתוּנָה לְתוֹךְ הַמַּשְׁקִין, אוֹ מְלֵאָה מַשְׁקִין וּנְתוּנָה לְתוֹךְ הַפֵּרוֹת, וְשָׁאֲבוּ, כֹּל שֶׁשָּׁאֲבוּ, בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: A jar full of produce which was put into liquids, or a jar full of liquids was put into produce and [the produce] absorbed, all [the produce] which absorbed comes under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: בְּאֵלּוּ מַשְׁקִים אָמְרוּ, בְּמַיִם וּבְיַיִן וּבְחֹמֶץ.
phrases.en: Concerning what liquids were they speaking? Water, wine and vinegar; but all the other liquids do not cause susceptibility to uncleanness.

phrases.he: וּשְׁאָר כָּל הַמַּשְׁקִין, טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: Rabbi Nehemiah says pulse is insusceptible, because pulse does not absorb [liquids].

phrases.he: רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה מְטַהֵר בְּקִטְנִית, שֶׁאֵין הַקִּטְנִית שׁוֹאָבֶת
הָרוֹדֶה פַת חַמָּה וּנְתָנָהּ עַל פִּי חָבִית שֶׁל יַיִן, רַבִּי מֵאִיר מְטַמֵּא. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מְטַהֵר.
phrases.en: One who drew hot bread off the side of an oven and put it upon the mouth of a jar of wine: Rabbi Meir declares it susceptible to uncleanness; But Rabbi Judah declares it insusceptible.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מְטַהֵר בְּשֶׁל חִטִּים וּמְטַמֵּא בְשֶׁל שְׂעֹרִים, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַשְּׂעֹרִים שׁוֹאֲבוֹת
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose declares it insusceptible in the case of wheat bread and susceptible in the case of barley bread, because barley absorbs [liquids].

phrases.he: הַמְרַבֵּץ אֶת בֵּיתוֹ וְנָתַן בּוֹ חִטִּים וְטָנְנוּ, אִם מֵחֲמַת הַמַּיִם, בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: If one sprinkled [the floor of] his house [with water] and put wheat therein and it became moist: If [the moisture came] from the water, it comes under the law of ‘if water be put’; But if [the moisture came] from the stones [on the floor], it does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: וְאִם מֵחֲמַת הַסֶּלַע, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: If one washed his garment in a tub and put wheat therein and it became moist: If [the moisture came] from the water, it comes under the law of ‘if water be put’; But if [the moisture came] of itself, it does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: הַמְכַבֵּס אֶת כְּסוּתוֹ בַּעֲרֵבָה, נָתַן בָּהּ חִטִּים וְטָנְנוּ, אִם מֵחֲמַת הַמַּיִם, בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
אִם מֵחֲמַת עַצְמָן, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
הַמְטַנֵּן בְּחֹל, הֲרֵי זֶה בְכִי יֻתַּן.
מַעֲשֶׂה בְאַנְשֵׁי הַמָּחוֹז שֶׁהָיוּ מְטִנִּין בְּחֹל, אָמְרוּ לָהֶם חֲכָמִים, אִם כָּךְ הֱיִיתֶם עוֹשִׂים, לֹא עֲשִׂיתֶם טָהֳרָה מִימֵיכֶם:
phrases.en: If one put [produce] in sand for it to become moist, this comes under the law of ‘if water be put’. It happened with the men of Mahoz that they used to moisten [their produce] with sand, and the sages said to them: if you have always acted in this manner, you have never prepared your food in purity.

phrases.he: הַמְטַנֵּן בְּטִיט הַנָּגוּב,
phrases.en: If one moistened [produce] with drying clay: Rabbi Shimon says: if there was still in it dripping liquid, it comes under the law of ‘if water be put’; But if there was not, it does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, אִם יֶשׁ בּוֹ מַשְׁקֶה טוֹפֵחַ, בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: If one sprinkled his threshing-floor with water, he need not be concerned lest wheat be put there and it become moist.

phrases.he: וְאִם לָאו, אֵינוֹ בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: If one gathered grass with the dew still on it in order to moisten wheat with it, it does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’, But if his intention was for this purpose, it does come under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: הַמְרַבֵּץ אֶת גָּרְנוֹ, אֵינוֹ חוֹשֵׁשׁ שֶׁמָּא נָתַן בָּהּ חִטִּים וְטָנְנוּ.
phrases.en: If one carried wheat to be milled and rain came down upon it and he was glad of it, it comes under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: הַמְלַקֵּט עֲשָׂבִים כְּשֶׁהַטַּל עֲלֵיהֶם, לְהָטֵן בָּהֶם חִטִּים, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
אִם נִתְכַּוֵּן לְכָךְ, הֲרֵי זֶה בְכִי יֻתַּן.
הַמּוֹלִיךְ חִטִּין לִטְחֹן וְיָרְדוּ עֲלֵיהֶן גְּשָׁמִים, אִם שָׂמַח, בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׂמֹחַ, אֶלָּא אִם עָמָד:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah said: one cannot help being glad of it. Rather, [it comes under the law] only if he stopped [on his way].

phrases.he: הָיוּ זֵיתָיו נְתוּנִים בַּגַּג וְיָרְדוּ עֲלֵיהֶן גְּשָׁמִים, אִם שָׂמַח, בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: If his olives were put on the roof and rain came down upon them and he was glad of it, it comes under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׂמֹחַ, אֶלָּא, אִם פָּקַק אֶת הַצִּנּוֹר אוֹ אִם חִלְחֵל לְתוֹכָן:
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah said: one cannot help being glad of it. Rather, [it comes under the law] only if he plugged up the gutter or if he shook the water [onto the olives].

phrases.he: הַחַמָּרִין שֶׁהָיוּ עוֹבְרִים בַּנָּהָר וְנָפְלוּ שַׂקֵּיהֶם לַמַּיִם, אִם שָׂמְחוּ, בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: If donkey-drivers were crossing a river and their sacks [filled with produce] fell into the water and they were happy about it, it comes under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׂמֹחַ, אֶלָּא, אִם הָפְכוּ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: one cannot help being happy about it. Rather, [it comes under the law] only if they turned over [the sacks].

phrases.he: הָיוּ רַגְלָיו מְלֵאוֹת טִיט, וְכֵן רַגְלֵי בְהֶמְתּוֹ, עָבַר בַּנָּהָר, אִם שָׂמַח, בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: If one's feet were full of clay, similarly, the feet of his beast, and he crossed a river and he was happy about it, this comes under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׂמֹחַ, אֶלָּא, אִם עָמַד וְהֵדִיחַ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: one cannot help being happy about it. Rather, [it comes under the law] only if he stopped and rinsed off his [feet] or those of his [domesticated] beast.

phrases.he: בְּאָדָם וּבִבְהֵמָה טְמֵאָה, לְעוֹלָם טָמֵא
phrases.en: But with an unclean [beast] it always causes susceptibility to uncleanness.

phrases.he: הַמּוֹרִיד אֶת הַגַּלְגַּלִּים וְאֶת כְּלֵי הַבָּקָר בִּשְׁעַת הַקָּדִים לַמַּיִם בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁיָּחוּצוּ, הֲרֵי זֶה בְכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: If one lowered wheels or the gear of oxen into water at the time of the hot east wind in order that they might become tightened, this comes under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: הַמּוֹרִיד בְּהֵמָה לִשְׁתּוֹת, הַמַּיִם הָעוֹלִים בְּפִיהָ, בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: If one took down a beast to drink, the water which came up on its mouth comes under the law of ‘if water be put’, but that which came up on its feet does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: וּבְרַגְלֶיהָ, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: If he intended that its feet should be washed, even the water that came up on its feet comes under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: אִם חָשַׁב שֶׁיּוּדְחוּ רַגְלֶיהָ, אַף הָעוֹלִין בְּרַגְלֶיהָ, בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: At the time of footsoreness or of threshing it always causes susceptibility to uncleanness.

phrases.he: בִּשְׁעַת הַיַּחַף וְהַדַּיִשׁ, לְעוֹלָם טָמֵא.
phrases.en: If a deaf-mute, an imbecile or a minor took it down, even though his intention was that its feet should be washed, it does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’, because with these the act alone counts, but not the intention.

phrases.he: הוֹרִיד חֵרֵשׁ שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחוֹשֵׁב שֶׁיּוּדְחוּ רַגְלֶיהָ, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן, שֶׁיֶּשׁ לָהֶן
מַעֲשֶׂה וְאֵין לָהֶן מַחֲשָׁבָה:
הַשּׁוֹחֶה לִשְׁתּוֹת, הַמַּיִם הָעוֹלִים בְּפִיו וּבִשְׂפָמוֹ, בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: If one bent down to drink, the water which came up on his mouth or on his moustache comes under the law of ‘if water be put’; But [what came up] on his nose or on his head or on his beard does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: בְּחָטְמוֹ וּבְרֹאשׁוֹ וּבִזְקָנוֹ, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: If one drew water with a jar, the water which came up on its outside, or on the rope which was wound round its neck, or on the rope which was needed for its use, comes under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: הַמְמַלֵּא בְּחָבִית, הַמַּיִם הָעוֹלִים אַחֲרֶיהָ, וּבַחֶבֶל שֶׁהוּא מְכֻנָּן עַל צַוָּארָהּ, וּבַחֶבֶל שֶׁהוּא לְצָרְכָּהּ, הֲרֵי זֶה בְכִי יֻתַּן. כַּמָּה הוּא צָרְכָּהּ.
phrases.en: How much rope is needed for its use? Rabbi Shimon ben Eleazar says: a handbreadth.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר, טֶפַח.
phrases.en: If he put the jar under the rain-pipe, it does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: נְתָנָהּ תַּחַת הַצִּנּוֹר, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן
מִי שֶׁיָּרְדוּ עָלָיו גְּשָׁמִים, אֲפִלּוּ אַב הַטֻּמְאָה, אֵינוֹ בְכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: If rain came down upon a person, even if he was unclean with a father of impurity, it does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’; But if he shook it off, it does come under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: וְאִם נִעֵר, בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: If one stood under a rain-pipe to cool himself or to wash himself, [the water falling on him] is unclean if he is unclean; If he is clean, it [only] comes under the law of if water be put.

phrases.he: עָמַד תַּחַת הַצִּנּוֹר לְהָקֵר אוֹ לִדּוֹחַ, בְּטָמֵא, טְמֵאִין. וּבְטָהוֹר, בְּכִי יֻתַּן
הַכּוֹפֶה קְעָרָה עַל הַכֹּתֶל בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁתּוּדַח, הֲרֵי זֶה בְכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: If one inclined a dish against a wall that it might be rinsed [by rainwater], it comes under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: אִם בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁלֹּא יִלְקֶה הַכֹּתֶל, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן
phrases.en: But if in order that the wall might not be damaged, it does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: חָבִית שֶׁיָּרַד הַדֶּלֶף לְתוֹכָהּ,
phrases.en: A jar into which a leak [from a roof] fell: Bet Shammai say: it should be broken.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, יְשַׁבֵּר.
phrases.en: But Bet Hillel say: it may be emptied out.

phrases.he: בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, יְעָרֶה.
phrases.en: But they agree that one may put out his hand and take produce from it and they are insusceptible to uncleanness.

phrases.he: וּמוֹדִים שֶׁהוּא מוֹשִׁיט אֶת יָדוֹ וְנוֹטֵל פֵּרוֹת מִתּוֹכָהּ, וְהֵם טְהוֹרִים
עֲרֵבָה שֶׁיָּרַד הַדֶּלֶף לְתוֹכָהּ, הַנִּתָּזִין וְהַצָּפִין אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן. נְטָלָהּ לְשָׁפְכָהּ,
phrases.en: A tub into which a leak [from a roof] fell, the water which splashed out or ran over does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: If one moved the tub in order to pour out the water: Bet Shammai say: it comes under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: But Bet Hillel say: it does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: הִנִּיחָהּ שֶׁיֵּרֵד הַדֶּלֶף לְתוֹכָהּ, הַנִּתָּזִין וְהַצָּפִין,
בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: If one placed the tub in order that the leak [from the roof] should fall into it: Bet Shammai say: the water that splashes out or runs over comes under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: But Bet Hillel say: it does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: נְטָלָהּ לְשָׁפְכָהּ, אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ מוֹדִים שֶׁהֵן בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: If one moved the tub in order to pour out the water, both agree that it comes under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: הַמַּטְבִּיל אֶת הַכֵּלִים וְהַמְכַבֵּס אֶת כְּסוּתוֹ בִּמְעָרָה, הַמַּיִם הָעוֹלִים בְּיָדָיו, בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: If one immersed vessels or washed his garment in a cavern, the water that came up on his hands comes under the law of ‘if water be put’; but what came up on his feet does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: בְּרַגְלָיו, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר, אִם אִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ שֶׁיֵּרֵד אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נִטַּנְּפוּ רַגְלָיו, אַף הָעוֹלִין בְּרַגְלָיו בְּכִי יֻתַּן:
phrases.en: Rabbi Elazar says: if it was not possible for him to go down into the cavern without soiling his feet, what came up on his feet also comes under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: קֻפָּה שֶׁהִיא מְלֵאָה תֻרְמוֹסִין וּנְתָנוּהָ לְתוֹךְ מִקְוֶה, מוֹשִׁיט יָדוֹ וְנוֹטֵל תֻּרְמוֹסִין מִתּוֹכָהּ, וְהֵם טְהוֹרִים.
phrases.en: A basket full of lupines placed in a mikveh, one may put out his hand and take lupines from it and they remain clean.

phrases.he: הֶעֱלָם מִן הַמַּיִם, הַנּוֹגְעִים בַּקֻּפָּה, טְמֵאִים, וּשְׁאָר כָּל הַתֻּרְמוֹסִים, טְהוֹרִים.
phrases.en: But if he lifted them out of the water, those that touch the basket are unclean, but the rest of the lupines are clean.

phrases.he: צְנוֹן שֶׁבַּמְּעָרָה, נִדָּה מְדִיחָתוֹ וְהוּא טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: If there was a radish in a cavern, a niddah may rinse it and leave it clean.

phrases.he: הֶעֱלַתּוּ כָל שֶׁהוּא מִן הַמַּיִם, טָמֵא
phrases.en: But if she lifted it, however little, out of the water, it becomes unclean.

phrases.he: פֵּרוֹת שֶׁנָּפְלוּ לְתוֹךְ אַמַּת הַמַּיִם, פָּשַׁט מִי שֶׁהָיוּ יָדָיו טְמֵאוֹת וּנְטָלָן, יָדָיו טְהוֹרוֹת וְהַפֵּרוֹת טְהוֹרִים.
phrases.en: If produce fell into a channel of water, and one whose hands were unclean put out his hands and took it, his hands become clean and the produce [also] remains clean.

phrases.he: וְאִם חָשַׁב שֶׁיּוּדְחוּ יָדָיו, יָדָיו טְהוֹרוֹת וְהַפֵּרוֹת בְּכִי יֻתַּן
phrases.en: But if his intention was that his hands should be rinsed, his hands become clean and the produce comes under the law of ‘if water be put.’

phrases.he: קְדֵרָה שֶׁהִיא מְלֵאָה מַיִם וּנְתוּנָה לְתוֹךְ הַמִּקְוֶה וּפָשַׁט אַב הַטֻּמְאָה אֶת יָדוֹ לְתוֹכָהּ, טְמֵאָה. מַגַּע טֻמְאוֹת, טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.en: If a pot full of water was placed in a mikveh, and a person who was unclean by a father of impurity put his hand into the pot, it becomes unclean. But if [he was unclean] by a "touch of defilement," the pot remains clean.

phrases.he: וּשְׁאָר כָּל הַמַּשְׁקִין, טְמֵאִין, שֶׁאֵין הַמַּיִם מְטַהֲרִים אֶת שְׁאָר הַמַּשְׁקִין
phrases.en: But any of the other liquids [contained in the pot] becomes unclean, for water cannot purify the other liquids.

phrases.he: הַמְמַלֵּא בְקִילוֹן, עַד שְׁלשָׁה יָמִים, טְמֵאִין.
phrases.en: If one drew water through a kilon (a pump-beam), it causes susceptibility to uncleanness for three days.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, אִם נִגְּבוּ, מִיָּד טְהוֹרִים.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva says: if it was dried, it at once does not cause susceptibility to uncleanness; but if it was not dried, it causes susceptibility even for thirty days.

phrases.he: וְאִם לֹא נִגְּבוּ, אֲפִלּוּ עַד שְׁלשִׁים יוֹם, טְמֵאִים
עֵצִים שֶׁנָּפְלוּ עֲלֵיהֶם מַשְׁקִין וְיָרְדוּ עֲלֵיהֶם גְּשָׁמִים, אִם רַבּוּ, טְהוֹרִים.
phrases.en: If [unclean] liquids fell upon wood and rain came down upon it and [the rain water] exceeded [the liquids] in quantity, they are clean.

phrases.he: הוֹצִיאָם שֶׁיֵּרְדוּ עֲלֵיהֶם גְּשָׁמִים, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁרַבּוּ, טְמֵאִים.
phrases.en: If he took [the wood out] so that rain would come down upon it, they are unclean even though [the rain water] exceeded in quantity.

phrases.he: בָּלְעוּ מַשְׁקִים טְמֵאִים, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוֹצִיאָם שֶׁיֵּרְדוּ עֲלֵיהֶם גְּשָׁמִים, טְהוֹרִין.
phrases.en: If [the wood] had absorbed unclean liquids, even if he took the wood outside in order that rain should come down upon it, it is clean.

phrases.he: וְלֹא יַסִּיקֵם אֶלָּא בְיָדַיִם טְהוֹרוֹת בִּלְבָד.
phrases.en: But one may not light the wood in an oven except with clean hands.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, אִם הָיוּ לַחִין וְהִסִּיקָן, וְרַבּוּ הַמַּשְׁקִין הַיּוֹצְאִין מֵהֶן עַל הַמַּשְׁקִין שֶׁבָּלְעוּ, טְהוֹרִים:
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: if the wood was moist and then he lit it, and the liquids that came out of it exceeded in quantity the liquids which it had absorbed, they become clean.

phrases.he: מִי שֶׁטָּבַל בַּנָּהָר, וְהָיָה לְפָנָיו נָהָר אַחֵר וְעָבַר בּוֹ, טִהֲרוּ שְׁנִיִּים אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנִים.
phrases.en: One who immersed himself in a river and then there was in front of him another river and he crossed it, the second [water] purifies the first [water].

phrases.he: דָּחָהוּ חֲבֵרוֹ לְשָׁכְרוֹ, וְכֵן לִבְהֶמְתּוֹ, טִהֲרוּ שְׁנִיִּים אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנִים.
phrases.en: If his fellow pushed him in during exercise or his beast [pushed him in], the second [water] purifies the first [water].

phrases.he: וְאִם כִּמְשַׂחֵק עִמּוֹ, הֲרֵי זֶה בְכִי יֻתַּן
phrases.en: But if [he did it] out of playfulness, it comes under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: הַשָּׁט עַל פְּנֵי הַמַּיִם, הַנִּתָּזִין, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: One who swam in water, the water that splashed out does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’; But if it was his intention to splash his friend, this comes under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: וְאִם נִתְכַּוֵּן לְהַתִּיז עַל חֲבֵרוֹ, הֲרֵי זֶה בְכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: If one made a ‘bird’ in the water, neither [the water] that splashed out nor what remained in it comes under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: הָעוֹשֶׂה צִפּוֹר בַּמַּיִם, הַנִּתָּזִין וְאֶת שֶׁבָּהּ, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן
פֵּרוֹת שֶׁיָּרַד הַדֶּלֶף לְתוֹכָן וּבְלָלָן שֶׁיְּנֻגְּבוּ,
phrases.en: Produce onto which a leak [from a roof] fell and he mixed it up in order that it might become dry [quickly]: Rabbi Shimon says: it comes under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: But the sages say: it does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן:
הַמּוֹדֵד אֶת הַבּוֹר בֵּין לְעָמְקוֹ בֵּין לְרָחְבּוֹ, הֲרֵי זֶה בְכִי יֻתַּן, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן.
phrases.en: One who measures a cistern whether for its depth of for its breadth, it comes under the law of ‘if water be put' the words of Rabbi Tarfon.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, לְעָמְקוֹ, בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: But Rabbi Akiva says: if [it was measured] for its depth, it comes under the law of ‘if water be put’; but if for its breadth, it does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: וּלְרָחְבּוֹ, אֵינוֹ בְכִי יֻתַּן
פָּשַׁט יָדוֹ אוֹ רַגְלוֹ אוֹ קָנֶה לְבוֹר לֵידַע אִם יֶשׁ בּוֹ מַיִם, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: If one put his hand or his foot or a reed into a cistern in order to check whether it had any water, it does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’; But if to ascertain how much water it had, it comes under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: לֵידַע כַּמָּה מַיִם יֶשׁ בּוֹ, הֲרֵי זֶה בְכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: If one threw a stone into a cistern to check whether it had any water, [the water] that was splashed up does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’, and also [the water] that is on the stone is clean.

phrases.he: זָרַק אֶבֶן לְבוֹר לֵידַע אִם יֶשׁ בּוֹ מַיִם, הַנִּתָּזִין, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן. וְאֶת שֶׁבָּאֶבֶן, טְהוֹרִים
הַחוֹבֵט עַל הַשֶּׁלַח, חוּץ לַמַּיִם, בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: One beats upon a hide: If outside the water, it comes under the law of ‘if water be put’; Inside the water, it does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: לְתוֹךְ הַמַּיִם, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אַף לְתוֹךְ הַמַּיִם בְּכִי יֻתַּן, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מִתְכַּוֵּן שֶׁיֵּצְאוּ עִם הַצּוֹאָה:
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: even inside the water it comes under the law of ‘if water be put’, because his intention was that the water should come off together with the filth.

phrases.he: הַמַּיִם הָעוֹלִין בַּסְּפִינָה וּבָעֵקֶל וּבַמְּשׁוֹטוֹת, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: The water that comes up into a ship or into the bilge or on the oars does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: בַּמְּצוֹדוֹת וּבָרְשָׁתוֹת וּבַמִּכְמָרוֹת, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: The water that comes up in snares, nets, or in fishing nets does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’; But if he shook them out it does come under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: וְאִם נִעֵר, בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: One who leads a ship out into the Great Sea in order to forge its bolts, or one who takes a nail out into the rain in order to forge it, or one who puts a brand out in the rain in order to extinguish it, this comes under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: הַמּוֹלִיךְ אֶת הַסְּפִינָה לַיָּם הַגָּדוֹל לְצָרְפָהּ, הַמּוֹצִיא מַסְמֵר לַגְּשָׁמִים לְצָרְפוֹ, הַמַּנִּיחַ אֶת הָאוּד בַּגְּשָׁמִים לְכַבּוֹתוֹ, הֲרֵי זֶה בְכִי יֻתַּן
קַסְיָא שֶׁל שֻׁלְחָנוֹת וְהַשִּׁיפָא שֶׁל לְבֵנִים, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: [Water on] the covering of tables or on the matting of bricks does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’; But if they were shaken, it does come under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: וְאִם נִעֵר, בְּכִי יֻתַּן
כָּל הַנִּצּוֹק, טָהוֹר, חוּץ מִדְּבַשׁ הַזִּיפִין, וְהַצַּפָּחַת.
phrases.en: A flow pouring [from one vessel to another] is clean, except [the flow] of honey of ziphim bees and honey batter.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, אַף הַמִּקְפָּה שֶׁל גְּרִיסִין וְשֶׁל פּוֹל, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא סוֹלֶדֶת לְאַחֲרֶיהָ:
phrases.en: Bet Shammai say: also [the flow of] thick pottage of split beans, because it thickens up backwards.

phrases.he: הַמְעָרֶה מֵחַם לְחַם, וּמִצּוֹנֵן לְצוֹנֵן, וּמֵחַם לְצוֹנֵן, טָהוֹר. מִצּוֹנֵן לְחַם, טָמֵא.
phrases.en: One who pours hot water into hot water, or cold water into cold water, or hot water [poured] into cold water remains clean; But from cold water into hot water, the [cold water] becomes unclean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, אַף הַמְעָרֶה מֵחַם לְחַם וְכֹחוֹ שֶׁל תַּחְתּוֹן יָפֶה מִשֶּׁל עֶלְיוֹן, טָמֵא:
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: even in the case of hot water poured into hot water it becomes unclean if the strength of the heat of the lower [water] is greater than that of the upper [water].

phrases.he: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁהָיוּ יָדֶיהָ טְהוֹרוֹת, וּמְגִיסָה בִקְדֵרָה טְמֵאָה, אִם הִזִּיעוּ יָדֶיהָ, טְמֵאוֹת.
phrases.en: If a woman whose hands were clean stirred an unclean pot and her hands perspired, they become unclean.

phrases.he: הָיוּ יָדֶיהָ טְמֵאוֹת, וּמְגִיסָה בִקְדֵרָה טְהוֹרָה, אִם הִזִּיעוּ יָדֶיהָ, הַקְּדֵרָה טְמֵאָה.
phrases.en: If her hands were unclean and she stirred a clean pot and her hands perspired the pot becomes unclean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אִם נָטְפוּ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: only if her hands dripped.

phrases.he: הַשּׁוֹקֵל עֲנָבִים בְּכַף מֹאזְנַיִם, הַיַּיִן שֶׁבַּכַּף, טָהוֹר, עַד שֶׁיְּעָרֶה לְתוֹךְ הַכְּלִי.
phrases.en: One who weighs grapes with a balance, the wine in the scale is clean until it is poured into a vessel.

phrases.he: הֲרֵי זֶה דוֹמֶה לְסַלֵּי זֵיתִים וַעֲנָבִים כְּשֶׁהֵן מְנַטְּפִין
phrases.en: Behold, this is like baskets of olives and grapes when they are dripping [with sap].

phrases.he: הַמַּעֲלֶה פֵרוֹתָיו לַגַּג מִפְּנֵי הַכְּנִימָה, וְיָרַד עֲלֵיהֶם טַל, אֵינָם בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: One who carries his produce up to the roof because of maggots, and dew came down upon it, it does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’; But if he intended for this to happen, it does come under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: אִם נִתְכַּוֵּן לְכָךְ, הֲרֵי זֶה בְכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: If a deaf-mute, or a person not of sound senses, or a minor carried it up, although he expected that dew should come down upon it, it does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’, because with these the act alone counts, but not the intention.

phrases.he: הֶעֱלָן חֵרֵשׁ, שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחִשַּׁב שֶׁיֵּרֵד עֲלֵיהֶן הַטַּל, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן, שֶׁיֶּשׁ לָהֶן
מַעֲשֶׂה וְאֵין לָהֶן מַחֲשָׁבָה:
הַמַּעֲלֶה אֶת הָאֲגֻדּוֹת וְאֶת הַקְּצִיעוֹת וְאֶת הַשּׁוּם לַגַּג בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁיַּמְתִּינוּ, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן.
phrases.en: One who carries up to the roof bundles [of vegetables] or cakes of figs or garlic so as to keep them fresh, it does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’.

phrases.he: כָּל הָאֲגֻדּוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית הַשְּׁוָקִים, טְמֵאִין.
phrases.en: All bundles [of vegetables] in the market places are unclean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מְטַהֵר בַּלַּחִים.
אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר, וְכִי מִפְּנֵי מָה טִמְּאוּ, אֶלָּא מִפְּנֵי מַשְׁקֵה הַפֶּה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah declares them clean if they are fresh. Rabbi Meir said: Why did they declare them unclean? Only because of liquid from the mouth.

phrases.he: כָּל הַקְּמָחִין וְהַסְּלָתוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית הַשְּׁוָקִים, טְמֵאִים.
phrases.en: All coarse and fine flours of the market places are unclean.

phrases.he: הַחִילְקָה, הַטְּרָגִיס וְהַטִּסְגִי, טְמֵאִים בְּכָל מָקוֹם
phrases.en: Crushed wheat, groats, and pearl-barley are unclean everywhere.

phrases.he: כָּל הַבֵּיצִים בְּחֶזְקַת טָהֳרָה, חוּץ מִשֶּׁל מוֹכְרֵי מַשְׁקֶה.
phrases.en: All eggs are presumed to be clean except those of sellers of liquids.

phrases.he: וְאִם הָיוּ מוֹכְרִין עִמָּהֶן פֵּרוֹת יְבֵשִׁים, טְהוֹרוֹת.
phrases.en: But if they sold with them dry produce, they are clean.

phrases.he: כָּל הַדָּגִים בְּחֶזְקַת טֻמְאָה.
phrases.en: All fish are presumed unclean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, חֲתִיכַת אִלְתִּית וְדָג הַמִּצְרִי הַבָּא בְקֻפָּה וְקוּלְיָס הָאִסְפָּנִין, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ בְחֶזְקַת טָהֳרָה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Judah says: pieces of aylatit and Egyptian fish which arrives in a basket, and Spanish tunny, these may be presumed clean. All kinds of brine may be presumed unclean.

phrases.he: כָּל הַצִּיר בְּחֶזְקַת טֻמְאָה.
phrases.en: Concerning all these an am ha-aretz may be trusted when he declares them to be clean, except in the case of small fish, since they are usually stored with any am ha-aretz.

phrases.he: וְעַל כֻּלָּם, עַם הָאָרֶץ נֶאֱמָן לוֹמַר טְהוֹרִים הֵן, חוּץ מִשֶּׁל דָּגָה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן מַפְקִידִין אוֹתָהּ אֵצֶל עַם הָאָרֶץ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer ben Jacob says: clean brine into which water fell in any quantity must be deemed unclean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר, צִיר טָהוֹר שֶׁנָּפַל לְתוֹכוֹ מַיִם כָּל שֶׁהֵן, טָמֵא
שִׁבְעָה מַשְׁקִין הֵן. הַטַּל וְהַמַּיִם, הַיַּיִן וְהַשֶּׁמֶן, וְהַדָּם, וְהֶחָלָב, וּדְבַשׁ דְּבוֹרִים.
phrases.en: There are seven liquids: dew, water, wine, oil, blood, milk and bees’ honey.

phrases.he: דְּבַשׁ צְרָעִים, טָהוֹר, וּמֻתָּר בַּאֲכִילָה
phrases.en: Hornets’ honey does not cause susceptibility to uncleanness and may be eaten.

phrases.he: תּוֹלָדוֹת לַמַּיִם, הַיּוֹצְאִין מִן הָעַיִן, מִן הָאֹזֶן, מִן הַחֹטֶם, מִן הַפֶּה, מֵי רַגְלַיִם, בֵּין גְּדוֹלִים בֵּין קְטַנִּים, לְדַעְתּוֹ וְשֶׁלֹּא לְדַעְתּוֹ.
phrases.en: Derivatives of water are: the liquids that come from the eye, from the ear, from the nose and from the mouth, and urine, whether of adults or of children, whether [its flow is] conscious or unconscious.

phrases.he: תּוֹלָדוֹת לַדָּם, דַּם שְׁחִיטָה.
phrases.en: Derivatives of blood are: blood from the slaughtering of cattle and wild animals and birds that are clean, and blood from bloodletting for drinking.

phrases.he: בַּבְּהֵמָה וּבַחַיָּה וּבָעוֹפוֹת הַטְּהוֹרִים, וְדַם הַקָּזָה לִשְׁתִיָּה. מֵי חָלָב, כֶּחָלָב.
phrases.en: Whey is like milk, And the sap of olives is deemed like oil, since it is never free from oil, the words of Rabbi Shimon.

phrases.he: וְהַמֹּחַל, כַּשֶּׁמֶן, שֶׁאֵין הַמֹּחַל יוֹצֵא מִידֵי שֶׁמֶן, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.
רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין עִמּוֹ שָׁמֶן.
phrases.en: Rabbi Meir says: even though it contains no oil.

phrases.he: דַּם הַשֶּׁרֶץ, כִּבְשָׂרוֹ, מְטַמֵּא וְאֵינוֹ מַכְשִׁיר, וְאֵין לָנוּ כַּיּוֹצֵא בוֹ
phrases.en: The blood of a sheretz is like its flesh, it causes uncleanness but does not cause susceptibility to uncleanness, and there is nothing else like it.

phrases.he: אֵלּוּ מְטַמְּאִין וּמַכְשִׁירִין. זוֹבוֹ שֶׁל זָב, וְרֻקּוֹ, וְשִׁכְבַת זַרְעוֹ, וּמֵימֵי רַגְלָיו, וּרְבִיעִית מִן הַמֵּת, וְדַם הַנִּדָּה.
phrases.en: The following cause uncleanness and also susceptibility [to uncleanness]; The flow of a zav, his spittle, his semen and his urine; A quarter-log of blood from a corpse, and the blood of a menstruant.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע אֵינָהּ מַכְשֶׁרֶת.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: semen does not cause susceptibility. R.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אוֹמֵר, דַּם הַנִּדָּה אֵינוֹ מַכְשִׁיר.
phrases.en: Elazar ben Azariah says: the blood of a menstruant does not cause susceptibility.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, דַּם הַמֵּת אֵינוֹ מַכְשִׁיר.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon says: the blood of a corpse does not cause susceptibility, and if it fell on a gourd, he can scrape it off, and it remains clean.

phrases.he: וְאִם נָפַל עַל הַדְּלַעַת, גּוֹרְדָהּ וְהִיא טְהוֹרָה
אֵלּוּ לֹא מְטַמְּאִין וְלֹא מַכְשִׁירִין.
phrases.en: The following cause neither uncleanness nor susceptibility to uncleanness: Sweat, rotten secretion, excrement, blood issuing with any of these, liquid [issuing from a child born in the] eight month.

phrases.he: הַזֵּעָה, וְהַלֵּחָה סְרוּחָה, וְהָרְאִי, וְהַדָּם הַיּוֹצֵא עִמָּהֶם, וּמַשְׁקֵה בֶן שְׁמֹנָה.
רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, חוּץ מִדָּמוֹ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Yose says: except its blood.

phrases.he: וְהַשּׁוֹתֶה מֵי טְבֶרְיָה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיּוֹצְאִין נְקִיִּים.
phrases.en: [The discharge from the bowels of] one who drinks the water of Tiberias even though it comes out clean.

phrases.he: דַּם שְׁחִיטָה בַּבְּהֵמָה, בַּחַיָּה וּבָעוֹפוֹת הַטְּמֵאִים, וְדַם הַקָּזָה לִרְפוּאָה.
phrases.en: Blood from the slaughtering of cattle and wild animals and birds that are unclean, and blood from bloodletting for healing.

phrases.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מְטַמֵּא בָאֵלּוּ.
phrases.en: Rabbi Eliezer declares these unclean.

phrases.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר, חֲלֵב הַזָּכָר, טָהוֹר
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: the milk of a male is clean.

phrases.he: חֲלֵב הָאִשָּׁה מְטַמֵּא לְרָצוֹן וְשֶׁלֹּא לְרָצוֹן, וַחֲלֵב הַבְּהֵמָה אֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא אֶלָּא לְרָצוֹן.
phrases.en: A woman's milk renders unclean whether [its flow is] desired or is not desired, but the milk of cattle renders unclean only if [its flow is] desired.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, קַל וָחֹמֶר הַדְּבָרִים.
phrases.en: Rabbi Akiva said: there is a kal vehomer argument here: if a woman's milk, which is specifically for infants, can render unclean whether [its flow is] desired or is not desired, all the more should the milk of cattle, which is for infants and adults, should render unclean both when [its flow is] desired and when it is not desired.

phrases.he: מָה אִם חֲלֵב הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְיֻחָד אֶלָּא לִקְטַנִּים, מְטַמֵּא לְרָצוֹן וְשֶׁלֹּא לְרָצוֹן, חֲלֵב הַבְּהֵמָה שֶׁהוּא מְיֻחָד לִקְטַנִּים וְלִגְדוֹלִים, אֵינוֹ דִין שֶׁיְּטַמֵּא לְרָצוֹן וְשֶׁלֹּא לְרָצוֹן.
אָמְרוּ לוֹ, לֹא, אִם טִמֵּא חֲלֵב הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁלֹּא לְרָצוֹן, שֶׁדַּם מַגֵּפָתָהּ טָמֵא, יְטַמֵּא חֲלֵב הַבְּהֵמָה שֶׁלֹּא לְרָצוֹן, שֶׁדַּם מַגֵּפָתָהּ טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: They said to him: No; a woman's milk renders unclean when [its flow is] not desired, because the blood issuing from her wound is unclean; but how could the milk of cattle render unclean when [its flow is] not desired, seeing that the blood issuing from its wound is clean? He said to them: I am stricter in the case of milk than in the case of blood, for if one milks for healing, [the milk] is unclean, whereas if one lets blood for healing, [the blood] is clean.

phrases.he: אָמַר לָהֶם, מַחְמִיר אֲנִי בְּחָלָב מִבְּדָם, שֶׁהַחוֹלֵב לִרְפוּאָה, טָמֵא, וְהַמַּקִּיז לִרְפוּאָה, טָהוֹר.
phrases.en: They said to him: let baskets of olives and grapes prove it; for liquids flowing from them are unclean only when [the flow is] desired, but when [the flow is] not desired they are clean.

phrases.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ, סַלֵּי זֵיתִים וַעֲנָבִים יוֹכִיחוּ, שֶׁהַמַּשְׁקִים הַיּוֹצְאִין מֵהֶן לְרָצוֹן, טְמֵאִים, וְשֶׁלֹּא לְרָצוֹן, טְהוֹרִים.
phrases.en: He said to them: No; if you say [thus] of baskets of olives and grapes which are at first a solid food and at the end become a liquid, could you say [the same] of milk which remains a liquid from beginning to end? Thus far was the argument.

phrases.he: אָמַר לָהֶן, לֹא, אִם אֲמַרְתֶּם בְּסַלֵּי זֵיתִים וַעֲנָבִים, שֶׁתְּחִלָּתָן אֹכֶל וְסוֹפָן מַשְׁקֶה, תֹּאמְרוּ בְחָלָב שֶׁתְּחִלָּתוֹ וְסוֹפוֹ מַשְׁקֶה.
phrases.en: Rabbi Shimon said: from here on in we used to argue before him: let rain water prove it, for it remains a liquid from beginning to end, and renders unclean only when [its flow is] desired.

phrases.he: עַד כָּאן הָיְתָה תְשׁוּבָה.
אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מִכָּאן וָאֵילָךְ הָיִינוּ מְשִׁיבִין לְפָנָיו, מֵי גְשָׁמִים יוֹכִיחוּ, שֶׁתְּחִלָּתָן וְסוֹפָן מַשְׁקֶה וְאֵינָן מְטַמְּאִין אֶלָּא לְרָצוֹן.
phrases.en: But he said to us: No; if you say [thus] of rain water, it is because most of it is intended not for human usage but for the soil and for trees, whereas most milk is intended for human usage.

phrases.he: אָמַר לָנוּ, לֹא, אִם אֲמַרְתֶּם בְּמֵי גְשָׁמִים, שֶׁאֵין רֻבָּן לָאָדָם, אֶלָּא לָאֲרָצוֹת וְלָאִילָנוֹת, וְרֹב הֶחָלָב, לָאָדָם
הָרוֹאֶה רְאִיָּה אַחַת שֶׁל זוֹב,
phrases.en: If a man has seen one issue of zov: Bet Shammai says: he is to be compared to [a woman] who observes a day for each day.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, כְּשׁוֹמֶרֶת יוֹם כְּנֶגֶד יוֹם.
phrases.en: But Bet Hillel says: he is to be compared to one who has had a seminal emission.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, כְּבַעַל קֶרִי.
phrases.en: Should he see [one day] and on the second it stopped, and on the third day he saw two [issues], or one [issue] that was as copious as two: Bet Shammai says: he is a full zav.

phrases.he: רָאָה אַחַת, וּבַשֵּׁנִי הִפְסִיק, וּבַשְּׁלִישִׁי רָאָה שְׁתַּיִם אוֹ אַחַת מְרֻבָּה כִשְׁתַּיִם,
בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, זָב גָּמוּר.
phrases.en: But Bet Hillel says: he defiles those objects on which he sits or lies, and must also go into running water, but he is exempt from the sacrifice.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, מְטַמֵּא מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב, וְצָרִיךְ בִּיאַת מַיִם חַיִּים, וּפָטוּר מִן הַקָּרְבָּן.
phrases.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Yehudah said: Bet Shammai agrees that in such a case he is not real zav.

phrases.he: אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יְהוּדָה, מוֹדִים בֵּית שַׁמַּאי בָּזֶה שֶׁאֵינוֹ זָב גָּמוּר.
phrases.en: What do they disagree about? The case of one who saw two [issues], or one [issue] that was as copious as two [on one day], and stopped on the second day, and on the third day he saw another [issue].

phrases.he: וְעַל מַה נֶּחְלְקוּ, עַל הָרוֹאֶה שְׁתַּיִם אוֹ אַחַת מְרֻבָּה כִשְׁתַּיִם, וּבַשֵּׁנִי הִפְסִיק, וּבַשְּׁלִישִׁי רָאָה אַחַת,
בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, זָב גָּמוּר.
phrases.en: Bet Shammai says: he is a real zav; But Bet Hillel say: he only defiles those objects on which he sits or lies, and must also go into running water, but he is exempt from the sacrifice.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, מְטַמֵּא מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב, וְצָרִיךְ בִּיאַת מַיִם חַיִּים, וּפָטוּר מִן הַקָּרְבָּן:
הָרוֹאֶה קֶרִי בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁי לִסְפִירַת זוֹבוֹ,
phrases.en: If one sees an issue of semen on the third day of counting his zov: Bet Shammai says: it undoes the two preceding days; But Bet Hillel says: it undoes only that day.

phrases.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, סוֹתֵר שְׁנֵי יָמִים שֶׁלְּפָנָיו.
phrases.en: Rabbi Ishmael says: one who sees it on the second day, it undoes the preceding day.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, לֹא סָתַר אֶלָּא יוֹמוֹ.
phrases.en: But Rabbi Akiva says: it matters not whether he saw it on the second day or on the third day: Bet Shammai says: it undoes the two preceding days; And Bet Hillel says: it undoes only that day.

phrases.he: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר, הָרוֹאֶה בַשֵּׁנִי, סוֹתֵר אֶת שֶׁלְּפָנָיו.
phrases.en: But they agree that if he saw it on the fourth day [of counting] it undoes only that day.

phrases.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, אֶחָד הָרוֹאֶה בַשֵּׁנִי וְאֶחָד הָרוֹאֶה בַשְּׁלִישִׁי, שֶׁבֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, סָתַר שְׁנֵי יָמִים שֶׁלְּפָנָיו.
phrases.en: This is if he saw semen; but he saw zov, then even if this had occurred on the seventh day, it undoes all the days that had preceded.

phrases.he: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, לֹא סָתַר אֶלָּא יוֹמוֹ.
וּמוֹדִים בְּרוֹאֶה בָרְבִיעִי שֶׁלֹּא סָתַר אֶלָּא יוֹמוֹ, בְּרָאָה קֶרִי.
אֲבָל אִם רָאָה זוֹב, אֲפִלּוּ יוֹם שְׁבִיעִי, סָתַר אֶת שֶׁלְּפָנָיו
רָאָה אַחַת הַיּוֹם וּשְׁתַּיִם לְמָחָר, שְׁתַּיִם הַיּוֹם וְאַחַת לְמָחָר, שָׁלשׁ לִשְׁלשָׁה יָמִים אוֹ לִשְׁלשָׁה לֵילוֹת, הֲרֵי זֶה זָב גָּמוּר:
phrases.en: If he saw one issue on one day and two on the next day, or two on one day and one on the next day, or three on three [consecutive] days, or three nights, he is a full zav.
